A fee exemption or waiver can count as public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), so confirm prevailing wage exposure with counsel. Applies only in unincorporated Napa County; each city has its own inclusionary and linkage rules (Pass 3). Code text was read from the Zoneomics mirror (Ordinances 1334 of 2010, 1386 of 2013, 1491 of June 4, 2024 and 1495 of Sept 24, 2024); fee amounts come from Sonoma Index-Tribune and CBS Bay Area coverage of the Oct 21, 2025 vote. napacounty.gov pages and DocumentCenter PDFs sit behind Cloudflare and refused automated access on 2026-11-06, so the county's own page could not be opened; the official FAQ is https://www.napacounty.gov/3951/Affordable-Housing-Impact-Fee-Housing-Co.
audit_note: The adopted (amended) fee table and phase-in are still not on any official page that could be opened: napacounty.gov FAQ 3951 returned a Cloudflare challenge to curl and 403 to WebFetch, and Legistar matter 25-1814 has only the pre-hearing draft resolution and a post-meeting slide deck with no final
prevailing_wage_basis: The inclusionary requirement and impact fee are charges on private development and provide no public funds (Labor Code 1720(a)(1), (c)(1)). The developer-relevant feature is the fee exemption for 100 percent affordable projects. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.

program_name: Napa County Density Bonus and Incentives (County Code 18.107.170-18.107.190)
administering_agency: Napa County Planning, Building and Environmental Services
typical_award_size: Density bonus, incentives and concessions, parking reductions and development standard waivers per Government Code 65915; the chapter defers to state law where they conflict.
affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds (County Code 18.107.170 implements Gov. Code 65915 for housing developments as defined in state law). Affordable housing agreement required for any bonus, incentive, parking reduction or waiver: rental target units affordable at least 55 years (or longer if financing requires), for-sale units 45 years with sale to a qualified nonprofit if no income-qualified buyer within 180 days (18.107.180(E)-(G)). Requests are filed with the first discretionary permit with detailed submittals; incentives and waivers may be denied only on specified written findings (18.107.180(B)-(C)). On-site inclusionary units can count toward the bonus; paying in-lieu fees does not (18.107.170(D)(3)).
layering_notes: Unincorporated Napa County is mostly Agricultural Preserve and Agricultural Watershed zoning, so multifamily sites are scarce; the 2023-2031 Housing Element (adopted Dec 19, 2023, HCD compliance letter Feb 22, 2024) relies on a 106-unit RHNA and RHNA transfers to the City of Napa. Inclusionary units count toward the state bonus (Latinos Unidos del Valle de Napa y Solano v. County of Napa, 2013). Ordinance 1495 (Sept 24, 2024) updated the incentives and density bonus sections. Code text read from the Zoneomics mirror; napacounty.gov pages and DocumentCenter PDFs sit behind Cloudflare and refused automated access on 2026-11-06, so the county's own page could not be opened; confirm against the official code at library.municode.com or the County.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Verified against the official text of Ordinance 1495 (Napa County Legistar matter 24-1623, enactment O-1495, adopted Sept 24, 2024), which amends 18.107.170 and 18.107.180 and reserves 18.107.150 and 160. Added the 180-day nonprofit sale rule and the inclusionary-unit counting rule. The statement that the chapter defers to state law (18.107.190) was read only on the Zoneomics mirror; 18.107.170(D)(4) in the official text caps any bonus at what state law authorizes.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Affordable Unit Permit Fee Waiver and Expedited Processing (County Code 18.107.120)
administering_agency: Napa County Planning, Building and Environmental Services
typical_award_size: Under County Code 18.107.120 (as amended by Ordinance 1495, Sept 24, 2024), residential projects that build affordable units under 18.107.080, 18.107.100 or 18.107.110 get: building permit application fees waived for the affordable units, flexibility in unit size and interior features, attached affordable units allowed in single-family projects, and expedited permit processing. If a state density bonus is requested, these incentives count only when each is requested as a state incentive. The Zoneomics mirror also shows housing impact fees refundable if a project does not proceed and a refund is requested within 90 days; that provision was not in the official text read.
affordability_requirement: Units must satisfy Chapter 18.107 affordability (40-year minimum; 55 years for density bonus rentals).
next_deadline: The Oct 21, 2025 fee action also directed staff to design a fee deferral program for owners renting units as affordable housing; watch for the ordinance in 2026.
layering_notes: Modest value for multifamily since the chapter is written around inclusionary units in small unincorporated projects. Waived fees count as public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and can trigger state prevailing wage, so confirm with counsel. Code text read from the Zoneomics mirror; napacounty.gov pages and DocumentCenter PDFs sit behind Cloudflare and refused automated access on 2026-11-06, so the county's own page could not be opened; confirm with the County.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: 18.107.120 verified in the official text of Ordinance 1495 (Napa County Legistar matter 24-1623, enactment O-1495). The 90-day impact fee refund provision is from the Zoneomics mirror only. No fee deferral ordinance from the Oct 21, 2025 direction was found in Napa County Legistar matters through July 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule is recorded for this program. The program waives building permit application fees for compliant affordable units (County Code 18.107.120). Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.

program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), Napa County non-entitlement formula share
administering_agency: Napa County Housing and Community Services (HCD formula grantee)
typical_award_size: HCD CY 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA: Napa County CY 2024 $219,600 and CY 2025 $241,967; five-year estimate 2024-2028 $1,372,500. By comparison the City of Napa (entitlement) is $223,362 and $239,253 for the same years. Earlier rounds: 2020 formula awards to the City of Napa only; the City also administers PLHA for American Canyon, Calistoga, St. Helena and Yountville under delegation agreements, not for the County.
affordability_requirement: PLHA statute: rental assistance at or below 60% AMI unless the plan targets up to 120% AMI (150% in high-cost areas); 55-year covenant for rental development; County five-year plan governs local uses.
next_deadline: HCD releases the annual formula allocation each year; the County must hold a resolution and five-year plan for 2024-2028. No County NOFA to developers was found; the County's plan and uses could not be read because its site blocks automated access.
layering_notes: Small dollars (about $220,000 to $240,000 a year) better suited to ADU loans, predevelopment or operating subsidy than to a construction gap. PLHA states no wage rule of its own; construction use is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), subject to the 1720(c) exemptions (see prevailing_wage_basis). Confirm with Housing and Community Services (707-253-4112) whether the County's five-year plan directs PLHA to multifamily or to its ADU forgivable loan program ($105,000 maximum per ADU as of April 2026).
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports it.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines and Formula Allocation NOFA contain no prevailing wage section; only the separate Non-Entitlement Competitive NOFA (Section VI.C) states that awarded funds are subject to state prevailing wage unless a 1720(c) exception applies, and this record is the formula share. https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf ; https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-allocation-nofa.pdf

program_name: HOME and CDBG, Napa County (state non-entitlement status)
administering_agency: California HCD state HOME and CDBG programs; Napa County Housing and Community Services as applicant
typical_award_size: None directly. Napa County is not a HUD CDBG entitlement urban county or a HOME participating jurisdiction. The City of Napa is the only CDBG entitlement in the county (FY 2024-25 entitlement $583,519) and draws HOME and ESG through State HCD grants. No County of Napa state HOME or CDBG award for 2024 or 2025 surfaced in HCD award lists.
per_unit_cap: HOME per-unit subsidy limits (24 CFR 92.250) apply to any state HOME award.
affordability_requirement: State HOME: 20% of HOME units at 50% AMI, rest at 60% AMI, 55-year HCD covenant. State CDBG: 51% of units for households at or below 80% AMI.
next_deadline: Follow HCD state HOME and CDBG NOFAs (state records). A developer in unincorporated Napa or the four small cities needs the County or city to apply as the state HOME or CDBG grantee.
layering_notes: There is no county-level HOME or CDBG pipeline to layer in Napa; this is a negative finding. The City of Napa CDBG and HOME programs are Pass 3. Napa County received $207,965 of State ESG for CA-517 in the 2024 NOFA, usable for shelter and rapid rehousing, not capital. Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units or 8 or more CDBG-assisted units; state prevailing wage turns on the local or state funds in the deal and the Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions (see prevailing_wage_basis). Status inferred from the City of Napa 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan, the City FY 2024-25 CAPER and HCD award lists; confirm with the County.
audit_note: HUD FY 2025 CPD allocation pages (hud.gov/hud-partners/community-budget-25) returned 403 and the FY25 legacy page loads no data, so County entitlement status and the City of Napa allocation could not be checked against an official table.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: County conduit multifamily housing revenue bonds (none; CMFA used in Napa County)
administering_agency: Napa County (not an active conduit issuer); California Municipal Finance Authority used instead
typical_award_size: No county issuance program found. Recent Napa County deals used CMFA: Napa Park Homes, City of Napa, 140 units acquisition-rehab, $43,575,000 (2026); St. Anton Partners refinancing, City of Napa, $20,135,000; BRIDGE Housing, Calistoga and St. Helena, $20,544,520.
affordability_requirement: Per CDLAC: at least 20% of units at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI, 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Not applicable. Use CMFA, CSCDA or CalHFA as issuer; the Board of Supervisors or city council holds the TEFRA hearing for sites in its jurisdiction.
layering_notes: Negative finding recorded so later passes do not search again. 4% deals in Napa pair CMFA bonds with CTCAC credits, County Affordable Housing Fund or City of Napa funds, and HCD programs (Manzanita used AHSC, NHTF and HOME). Conduit bonds alone do not trigger state prevailing wage; the deal's public subordinate loans usually do.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: CMFA pages confirm Napa Park Homes $43,575,000 (140 units, 128 at 50 to 60% AMI, 55 years), St. Anton $20,135,000 refinancing in the City of Napa and BRIDGE Housing $20,544,520 in Calistoga and St. Helena. Napa County Legistar shows no County housing bond issuance since 2022.
prevailing_wage_basis: DIR PW 2006-001 Horizons at Indio (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf) and the Decision on Administrative Appeal PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village (CSCDA bonds): conduit tax-exempt housing revenue bond proceeds, which flow from bondholders through a private trustee to the borrower and never pass through public coffers, are not a payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) or a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). CMFA conduit bonds used in Napa County (for example Napa Park Homes, https://www.cmfa-ca.com/cmfa-issues-43575000-tax-exempt-financing-napa-park-homes/) therefore do not by themselves trigger state prevailing wage. Other public funds in the same deal (County Affordable Housing Fund or City of Napa loans, HOME, AHSC) are tested separately under their own rules.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Housing Authority of the City of Napa (countywide HCV administrator)
administering_agency: Housing Authority of the City of Napa (HACN, HUD CA073), a City of Napa agency that administers Section 8 for all of Napa County
typical_award_size: About 1,455 active vouchers as of early 2024 (City Consolidated Plan); the 2021 Administrative Plan allows up to 20% of budget authority to be project-based, with a 45-PBV limited preference for Napa Continuum of Care coordinated entry referrals and 15 tenant-based vouchers. Recent allocations: 8 PBVs for Stoddard West (City of Napa, 2017), 38 PBVs for Heritage House (3700 Valle Verde Drive), 8 PBVs for Napa Cove (66 units, American Canyon). Shelter Plus Care PSH renewal about $214,000 in the 2026 CoC listing.
per_unit_cap: HAP contract rent capped at the lower of reasonable rent or 110% of FMR (Napa FMRs are high, which supports PSH underwriting).
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 50% AMI (75% at 30% AMI on admission); PBV units limited to 25% of units in a building unless serving elderly, disabled or supportive services households.
next_deadline: No open PBV RFP as of November 8, 2026. HACN selects PBV owner proposals by advertised RFP under 24 CFR 983.51(b)(1) or without competition under 983.51(b)(2) for projects selected through a competitive public funding process within the prior three years; developers request PBVs after a CTCAC, HCD or HOME award.
layering_notes: Recorded at county level because HACN is the only public housing agency in Napa County and attaches PBVs to projects in American Canyon and other cities; the Napa County Housing Authority runs farmworker centers only and holds no vouchers. Developers normally request PBVs after a CTCAC or HCD award, which lets HACN use the non-competitive path. PBV HAP contracts run up to 20 years with extensions. Federal Davis-Bacon applies to PBV new construction or rehab of 9 or more contract units; state prevailing wage is not triggered by PBVs alone. City of Napa records in Pass 3 will cover HACN's city-only programs.
cycle_notes: Rolling, request-driven. The comprehensive Administrative Plan rewrite (HOTMA and NSPIRE) presented to the HACN board February 3, 2026 and targeted for April 7, 2026 was not adopted then; the April 7, 2026 agenda carried only the FY 2026-27 Annual Plan, and the October 6, 2026 board report says comprehensive updates are still underway. The 2021 Administrative Plan remains in effect, amended October 6, 2026 for Chapter 16 payment standards (EHV standards cut from 120% to the 90-110% FMR range per Notice PIH 2026-20; 2027 payment standards effective January 1, 2027). Most recent PBV awards in Legistar: Napa Cove (January 2022) and Valley Lodge (February 2022). Next HACN board meeting November 17, 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon wages apply to PBV development activity (new construction or rehab under an Agreement to enter into a HAP contract) involving nine or more contract units, per 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153); PBVs on existing housing with no development activity do not trigger it, and state prevailing wage is not triggered by PBVs alone. The HACN 2021 Administrative Plan requires PBV advertisements to state labor standards compliance.

program_name: Napa County Housing Authority Farmworker Centers (CSA No. 4 assessment and HCD matching funds)
administering_agency: Napa County Housing Authority (Board of Supervisors sitting as the Authority)
typical_award_size: Operating support for three county-owned dormitory centers (180 beds, about 400 farmworkers a year): County Service Area No. 4 vineyard assessment at $14 per planted acre raises about $650,000 a year (about 30% of operating cost); HCD Napa County Farmworker Centers Account match up to $250,000 a year (Health and Safety Code 50711.5, funded by SB 2); AB 1890 (Chapter 905, Statutes of 2026, signed Sept 30, 2026) raises the match to $500,000 a year once the Legislature appropriates it; AB 317 (2017) $200,000 General Fund support expires FY 2028-29. The County Affordable Housing Fund also subsidizes operations.
affordability_requirement: Centers serve migrant and seasonal farmworkers; AB 1890 bars use of the state funds to house H-2A workers.
next_deadline: Not available to outside developers; funds flow only to the County-owned centers. CSA 4 assessment is reauthorized by growers every five years.
layering_notes: Reclassified from other to negative finding in the 5_audit pass: the HCD Napa County Farmworker Centers Account (Health and Safety Code 50711.5) is an annual state match of up to $250,000 paid only to the Napa County Housing Authority for operating its own three farmworker centers, funded from the SB 2 Building Homes and Jobs Trust Fund, with an equal local match required; nothing is deployable to outside developers. Napa's only county housing authority is a farmworker-center operator with no Housing Choice Vouchers or development lending; the public housing agency for the county is the Housing Authority of the City of Napa. Farmworker rental projects in Napa instead layer the state Joe Serna Jr. Farmworker Housing Grant, the State Farmworker Housing Tax Credit (Pass 1) and the County Affordable Housing Fund, which once reserved $2,000,000 for farmworker projects and whose fees exempt farmworker units of 1,200 sq ft or less. The 2024 Napa County Farmworker Housing Needs and Impacts Assessment found 16% of year-round and 26% of seasonal workers in overcrowded housing. napacounty.gov is Cloudflare-blocked; the Authority page is https://www.napacounty.gov/467/Housing-Authority (707-253-4112). AB 1890 figures were not re-checked in this audit.
prevailing_wage_basis: Health and Safety Code 50711.5(a) funds the financing, maintenance and operation of the Napa County Housing Authority Farmworker Centers and states no prevailing wage rule. Operations are not public works under Labor Code 1720(a)(1), but Labor Code 1771 applies prevailing wage to contracted maintenance work (not to work by agency forces), so coverage depends on how specific maintenance or repair work is performed. https://california.public.law/codes/health_and_safety_code_section_50711.5 ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1771
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: record funds operation and maintenance of public centers, not development; true changed to unclear.

program_name: Napa City and County Continuum of Care (CA-517) and HHAP homelessness funding
administering_agency: Napa County Housing and Community Services (CoC collaborative applicant and HHAP administrative entity) with the Napa City and County CoC board
typical_award_size: HHAP Round 7 preliminary allocations (HCD, 2026): Napa City & County CoC $511,466.08 and Napa County $477,368.34, delivered as third and fourth disbursements of HHAP 6 under the Amended HHAP 6 NOFA dated August 7, 2026 ($829,350,000 statewide). HHAP Round 5: Napa County $698,089.89 and Napa City & County CoC $727,623.09 (regional total $1,425,712.98, awarded individually). HHAP Round 6: nearly $1,000,000 awarded March 2, 2026 for rapid rehousing and rental subsidies, permanent housing services, coordination and the City of Napa prevention and diversion program. HHAP Round 2: County $160,645 plus CoC redirect $250,000. State dashboard: $4,900,000 HHAP rounds 1-5 to the Napa area 2019-2025 ($3,000,000 direct to the County) and $15,000,000 Encampment Resolution Funding rounds 1-3. HUD FY 2025 CoC awards to CA-517 were small: $21,564 coordinated assessment, $40,874 HMIS, $50,000 planning; the 2026 local priority listing (July 23, 2026) ranks about $300,000 County engagement and housing navigation, $400,000 City of Napa outreach, $214,000 HACN Shelter Plus Care PSH renewal, $108,000 DV bonus and $500,000 CoC bonus. State ESG via CA-517: $207,965 (2024 NOFA).
affordability_requirement: HUD CoC and HHAP target people experiencing homelessness; HHAP permanent housing uses include operating subsidies, rental assistance and capital for PSH. program_name: Napa County Affordable ADU Forgivable Loan Program (single-unit, recorded for completeness)
administering_agency: Napa County Housing and Community Services
typical_award_size: Under the updated underwriting guidelines (V2) adopted by the Board on March 10, 2026: base forgivable loan $60,000 for a 1-bedroom or $85,000 for a 2-bedroom ADU plus up to $20,000 in rebates, for a total maximum of $80,000 or $105,000 (lesser of that amount or actual development cost). 5.0% simple deferred interest, forgiven monthly (1/60) over the 5-year affordability term; opt-out by repaying the unforgiven balance. Launched March 2023 (2023 range was $45,000 to $105,000). Funded from the Affordable Housing Fund.
per_unit_cap: $105,000 per ADU (2-bedroom, including $20,000 rebate); $80,000 for a 1-bedroom.
affordability_requirement: Owner-occupant of a single-family home in Napa County rents the ADU to a household at or below 80% AMI at HCD 80% AMI rents (2026 examples $2,563 for 1-bedroom, $2,884 for 2-bedroom) under a 5-year covenant; loan forgiven on compliance.
next_deadline: Open until funds are exhausted; applications through the County.
layering_notes: Not a multifamily source; recorded so the Affordable Housing Fund's competing uses are visible (ADU loans, farmworker centers, homeless services and fair housing all draw on the same fee revenue). Terms from the Napa Valley Community Foundation launch notice (March 17, 2023) and County news releases quoted in search results; napacounty.gov pages and DocumentCenter PDFs sit behind Cloudflare and refused automated access on 2026-11-06, so the county's own page could not be opened; the 2026 notice is https://www.napacounty.gov/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=858.
audit_note: Prevailing wage re-checked November 10, 2026 against the loan documents attached to the V2 guidelines (matter 26-308): loan agreement, deed of trust, regulatory agreement and note are all with the County of Napa, not the Housing Authority, so the trigger stays false under Labor Code 1720(c)(1). Award terms verified against the same guidelines.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(c)(1): private residential projects built on private property are not subject to prevailing wage unless built under an agreement with a state agency, a redevelopment agency or successor agency, or a local public housing authority (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). The ADU Guidelines V2 adopted by the Board on March 10, 2026 (Legistar matter 26-308, https://napa.legistar1.com/napa/attachments/201f9d80-fbde-4df8-9dd9-b7548f13765b.pdf) attach the loan documents, and the only public party is the County of Napa: the Accessory Dwelling Unit Loan Agreement (Exhibit B, p. 14) is between the County of Napa, a political subdivision, and the Borrower, and is signed for the County by the County Executive Officer with County Counsel approval (p. 24); the Deed of Trust names the County of Napa as beneficiary, and the Regulatory Agreement and Promissory Note run to the County. The Napa County Housing Authority is not a party. The borrower must own and occupy the single-family home on whose lot the ADU is built (Loan Agreement Recital C), so 1720(c)(1) applies and the forgivable loan, though public funds under 1720(b), does not trigger prevailing wage. 1720(c)(5)(C) (assistance for rehabilitation of a single-family home) is not relied on because the program funds new ADU construction. The program documents contain no prevailing wage provision. A project that also used state agency or Housing Authority funds would need a new review.

program_name: Solano County Housing Trust Fund (SCHTF)
administering_agency: Solano County Administrator's Office with the Department of Resource Management
typical_award_size: Capitalized with $2,000,000 ARPA (ordinance Aug 2022), $1,700,000 ARPA added Dec 12, 2023, and a regular $200,000 annual General Fund contribution (formerly the Community Investment Fund). Awards through the November 2023 RFP/NOFA: $3,200,000 loan to The Hampstead Companies for Prospera at Homestead in Dixon (107 units at or below 60% AMI, 3% interest) and $93,000 to Napa-Solano Habitat for Humanity (three homes, Fairfield). Oct 2024: $1,500,000 for site work on the County-owned 580 North 1st Street, Dixon parcel (demolition approved Sept 22, 2026). Aug 4, 2026: Board approved a $400,000 loan (3% simple interest, payments deferred to year seven) to EAH Housing for Tabor Commons, Fairfield (66 units: 41 at 30% AMI including 16 IDD units, 10 at 60% and 15 at 70% AMI), conditioned on the City of Fairfield contribution, plus deferral of about $446,354 in County public facilities fees, and a $200,000 grant to Habitat for Harmony Village, Vacaville (10 ownership homes at or below 80% AMI). per_unit_cap: None published. Prospera loan equals about $30,000 per unit.

next_deadline: No open round as of November 9, 2026. The last RFP was November 2023; guidelines allow an RFP or NOFA at least once per funding cycle and let the Board allocate funds to a specific project at any time.
layering_notes: Solano's only county gap source and a small one. It is used as the last dollars in a 9% deal (Tabor Commons) or as a larger patient loan where the County wants RHNA-credited units in Dixon. Local and state funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so state prevailing wage applies unless a 1720(c) exemption fits the deal, such as 1720(c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (see prevailing_wage_basis). audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true rested on public-funds logic only; no program or local rule found, changed to unclear. The layering note says ARPA loans trigger prevailing wage; no rule supporting that was found.

Loans are public funds under 1720(b)(1) or (b)(4), but qualifying below-market loans may be exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) and small subsidies under 1720(c)(3). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

typical_award_size: No county HOME or CDBG entitlement. State CDBG 2024 awards to the County of Solano: $300,000 Affordable Housing Development Site Feasibility Study and $300,000 Pocket/Cottage Housing Feasibility Study (Resolution 2024-213 of Dec 10, 2024; award Sept 3, 2025; $559,909 contract with Lisa Wise Consulting approved May 5, 2026, through June 30, 2028). No County of Solano award appears in HCD's HOME 2022-2023 awardee list. Fairfield, Vacaville and Vallejo are HUD entitlements (Pass 3).

A developer wanting state HOME in Dixon, Rio Vista or the unincorporated area needs the County or city to apply as grantee. audit_note: Tier 4: Legistar file 26-285 and HCD Standard Agreement 24-CDBG-10025 confirm a single $600,000 state CDBG planning award ($560,748 activity, $39,252 admin), award Sept 3, 2025, $559,909 Lisa Wise contract through June 30, 2028; the agreement lists the work as one sub award (Solano Housing Feasibility Study) rather than two $300,000 awards, which does not change screening. prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

Confirm with County Planning whether the Program C.2 code amendment has been adopted. The Vallejo-hosted guide figures (state set-asides, parking caps, May 2025 Solano AMI $124,600) match state law but are not County-issued.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Verified against the HCD-hosted adopted Solano County 2023-2031 Housing Element (Program C.2 and the prior-element review table, which says no density bonus ordinance was adopted). A Solano Legistar title search for density bonus items since 2024 returned only ALUC reviews of city ordinances. Reframed the record around state law applied directly.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. program_name: Welfare Exemption processing, Solano County Assessor
administering_agency: Solano County Assessor/Recorder, Exemptions Division, 675 Texas Street Suite 2700, Fairfield, 707-784-6210, exemptions@solanocounty.gov
typical_award_size: Full exemption of property tax on qualifying low-income rental units under Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g) once the BOE issues an Organizational Clearance Certificate (BOE-277); the Assessor rules on property use.
affordability_requirement: Units occupied by households at or below 80% AMI (140% AMI over-income allowance on BOE-267-L3); regulatory agreement, LIHTC or public financing required; managing general partner a qualifying nonprofit or qualifying LLC.
next_deadline: File BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual) with BOE-267-L, L1 and L2 supplements by February 15 each year; late claims through December 31 receive a partial exemption.
layering_notes: Standard statewide exemption (Pass 1 BOE record), recorded per county because the assessor administers it. Solano has no local property tax abatement JPA. The Assessor's page points to BOE Publication 149; office hours Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: Assessor page matches February 15 annual filing, BOE-277 OCC requirement, Publication 149 reference, 707-784-6210, exemptions@solanocounty.gov, 675 Texas Street Suite 2700 and 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. hours. prevailing_wage_trigger false is uncited (an exemption is not a payment of public funds).
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) and (b)(4) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works requires construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, including fees, loans or other obligations normally required in executing the construction contract that are reduced or waived. The welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) reduces property tax on the completed property; it pays no construction cost, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage.

CoC HHAP Round 5 $1,725,588.34. The 2026-27 state budget HHAP allocation gives the same pair about $4,070,000. CoC HHAP Round 4 permanent housing RFP offered $470,167.50 (2024). HUD CoC awards: $2,247,299 (FY 2024); FY 2025 round 1 $642,829 for STOP Plus. State dashboard: $13,600,000 HHAP rounds 1-5 to the Solano area, $6,500,000 direct to the County. State ESG 2024 via CA-518: $186,481 to Vacaville Solano Services Corporation.
affordability_requirement: HUD CoC and HHAP target people experiencing homelessness; HHAP allows PSH capital, operating subsidies and rental assistance (no cap on permanent housing uses per HCD's Dec 2025 memo), but Solano has programmed its rounds to rental subsidies, tenancy supports and interim housing.
next_deadline: No open local round as of November 8, 2026. HUD has released the 2026 CoC NOFO and Housing First Solano posted it, but no local 2026 letter of intent or application dates were posted yet. The 2025 local competition closed December 19, 2025 (letters of intent December 8, 2025) and did not accept new PSH or RRH applications. County HHAP Round 6 ($1,968,381, accepted by the Board in summer 2026) must be 75% contractually obligated and 50% expended by June 30, 2027. No CAP Solano JPA HHAP RFP was open on its site as of November 8, 2026.
layering_notes: For PSH underwriting the usable pieces are County Behavioral Health rental subsidies and tenancy services (Abode Services contract, $26,142,891 for Dec 2023 to June 2026) and HHAP operating commitments, not capital. Solano has no housing sales tax measure. The 2026 PIT count was Jan 29, 2026. HHAP capital, if used, would be public funds under Labor Code 1720(b); current Solano rounds fund beds and services, not construction (see prevailing_wage_basis).
cycle_notes: HUD CoC: CAP Solano JPA (collaborative applicant) runs a local competition after each HUD NOFO; FY 2025 local timeline was December 2025, with Tier 1 $646,384, Tier 2 $2,121,770, CoC Bonus $430,923 and DV Bonus $182,617 available to the Vallejo/Solano CoC. HHAP: County Behavioral Health HHAP Round 6 agreement runs through June 30, 2030 and sustains existing housing supports, rental subsidies and tenancy services; the CoC files a separate HHAP plan through CAP Solano JPA. capsolanojpa.gov and housingfirstsolano.org now open to automated access.
prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 578.99(h): the Davis-Bacon Act does not apply to the CoC program. The HHAP Round 6 NOFA states no prevailing wage requirement, and Solano HHAP rounds fund board and care beds, services at Fair Haven Commons (mental health specialists and the Caminar contract), flexible rental subsidies and interim housing operations, none of which is construction under Labor Code 1720(a)(1). A future HHAP or CoC capital award would need a project-level 1720 analysis. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/578.99 ; https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/calich/hhap-6-nofa.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Solano County Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA) housing interventions
administering_agency: Solano County Health and Social Services, Behavioral Health Division (BH Housing and Homelessness 707-553-5525, bhhousing@solanocounty.gov)
typical_award_size: FY 2026-29 Integrated Plan approved by the Board June 9, 2026. Year one (FY 2026-27) Housing Interventions component allocation $9,636,071 (30% of $32,120,235) plus $1,415,984 carryover, $11,052,055 available. Solano's population exceeds 200,000, so it cannot claim the small-county exemption; up to 25% of housing funds may go to capital development, half must serve chronically homeless people. Current delivery is through Abode Services (outreach, navigation, rental subsidy administration, rapid rehousing, PSH services at Blue Oak Landing and Fair Haven Commons) and the BHSA-funded ARCH program; an interim housing placement RFP closed July 9, 2026.
affordability_requirement: Adults and transition-age youth with serious mental illness or substance use disorder who are homeless or at risk; County BH client eligibility required.
next_deadline: No open developer or sponsor round as of November 8, 2026. The FY 2026-29 Integrated Plan took effect July 1, 2026 with annual updates. The Abode Services successor was approved in August 2026: three contracts for August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 ($6,318,267 permanent supportive housing, $3,877,619 rapid rehousing, $1,600,000 street outreach), funded by HHAP, HHIP, BHBH, opioid settlement, BHSA and 1991 Realignment. Ask BH Housing whether BHSA capital (up to the 25% cap) or project-based operating subsidies will be offered to PSH sponsors.
layering_notes: Roughly $9,600,000 a year makes Solano's BHSA housing pot the largest county-controlled housing source after HHAP; most of it funds rental subsidies and services, which is what a PSH operating budget needs. Classified grant because the plan funds rental subsidy for housing and allows up to 25% for capital development. Pair with Homekey+ or HHAP capital and SCHA or city PBVs. BHSA capital is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b) but carries no wage rule of its own; coverage turns on the 1720(c) exemptions and project facts (see prevailing_wage_basis). Budget figures from Appendix A of the adopted plan (content.solanocounty.gov).
cycle_notes: BHSA Integrated Plan FY 2026-27 to 2028-29 approved by the Board June 9, 2026 after public comment April 10 to May 10, 2026 and a May 19, 2026 hearing; in effect July 1, 2026. Housing Interventions are delivered through provider contracts (Abode Services, renewed through June 30, 2027) rather than a developer NOFA. The renewed Abode contracts shift eligible costs to Medi-Cal Community Supports and Transitional Rent so BHSA is reserved for allowable housing interventions. Interim housing placement RFP closed July 9, 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The DHCS BHSA County Policy Manual chapter 7 (Housing Interventions, section C.10 capital development) states no prevailing wage requirement, and no Solano term was found. Rental and operating subsidies are not construction under 1720(a)(1); BHSA capital grants are public funds whose coverage depends on 1720(c) and the other sources in the deal. https://policy-manual.mes.dhcs.ca.gov/behavioral-health-services-act-county-policy-manual/V1.0.0/7-bhsa-components-and-requirements

program_name: Contra Costa County Affordable Housing Program: HOME and CDBG-Housing (annual NOFA)
administering_agency: Contra Costa County Department of Conservation and Development (DCD), Housing and Community Improvement Division, 30 Muir Road, Martinez; Kristin Sherk, Principal Planner, 925-655-2889, dcd.housing@dcd.cccounty.us
typical_award_size: FY 2026/27 Board award (May 19, 2026): $4,294,840 CDBG-Housing and $3,500,000 HOME across five projects, including $2,000,000 HOME to Lakeside Recapitalization (RCD, Concord, 122 units) and $2,500,000 CDBG plus $1,500,000 HOME to Trinity Plaza (Eden and CHDC, Richmond, 65 senior units). FY 2025/26: $4,889,000 CDBG and $3,456,343 HOME plus $2,550,000 recaptured HOME-ARP. FY 2027/28 NOFA (released Sept 15, 2026) estimates up to $14,000,000 across CDBG-Housing, HOME and Measure X. FY 2026/27 Action Plan expected resources: CDBG $4,724,092 annual allocation plus $1,000,000 program income; HOME $2,927,850 plus $400,000 program income. ESG $384,307 (services and shelter only).
per_unit_cap: HOME Maximum Project Subsidy for rental units in Contra Costa County (effective April 10, 2026, FY 2027/28 Guidelines Appendix B), used to set County-assisted unit counts: 0BR $187,658, 1BR $215,122, 2BR $261,595, 3BR $338,419, 4BR $371,477. Performance retention of at least $50,000 (up to 10% of the loan) held by DCD.
affordability_requirement: 55-year County Regulatory Agreement (57 years from loan documents if the occupancy date cannot be established). County policy goal: 100% of County-assisted units at or below 50% AMI and 10% at or below 30% AMI; HOME units at HOME rent limits. 15% of Consortium HOME must go to CHDO-sponsored projects; CDBG new construction only through a qualified CBDO.
next_deadline: 2026-12-07 (FY 2027/28 applications due 5:00 PM via City Data Services). NOFA released Sept 15, 2026; application live Oct 15, 2026; TA meeting Oct 21, 2026; technical questions due Nov 23, 2026; AHFC meets April to May 2027; Board approves May to June 2027. Prior cycle: FY 2026/27 applications were due Dec 11, 2025.
layering_notes: County pages on www.contracosta.ca.gov refuse automated fetches (403); the same pages and DocumentCenter PDFs were opened on 2026-11-06 through the site's CivicPlus origin host (ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com), and Board reports were read through the contra-costa.legistar.com API. Standard terms: 3% simple interest, 55-year term, annual payments from residual receipts shared 75% to soft lenders pro rata and 25% to the borrower, special payment from 75% of cost savings, due on sale or refinance; the County will not cut its rate below the home city's rate. Davis-Bacon applies to HOME projects with 12 or more HOME-assisted units and CDBG projects with eight or more units; the developer must determine state prevailing wage, which turns on the County loan and the Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions. Build America Buy America applies to CDBG and HOME projects over $250,000. The County is the HUD entitlement for the Urban County (all of the county except Antioch, Concord, Pittsburg and Walnut Creek, which have their own CDBG) and lead of the Contra Costa HOME Consortium, so HOME can be used countywide including inside those four cities. Awards are sized by the HOME per-unit subsidy table and used as gap money for 4% and 9% tax credit deals; the FY 2026/27 Trinity Plaza and Lakeside awards are both acquisition-rehab recapitalizations. HOME-ARP ($12,108,330 allocation) is closed to new applications. The County staff report notes awards are made contingent on other commitments by Dec 31 of the following year, with recapture if unmet.
prevailing_wage_basis: FY 2027/28 Affordable Housing Program Guidelines Section 8.4: Davis-Bacon applies when there are more than 11 HOME-assisted units, and CDBG triggers Davis-Bacon in housing projects of 8 or more total units; state prevailing wage is the developer's responsibility to determine (Section 8.6).

program_name: Measure X Housing Fund (affordable housing development share)
administering_agency: Contra Costa County Department of Conservation and Development (75% share); Health, Housing and Homeless Services (H3) administers the 25% services share
typical_award_size: Measure X is a countywide half-cent sales tax (Nov 2020, 20 years, began April 1, 2021). The Board committed $10,000,000 in year one and about $12,000,000 a year after; the County's Measure X allocation table shows the Local Housing Trust Fund line at $12,600,000 (FY 2023-24), $12,902,400 (FY 2024-25), $13,156,577 (FY 2025-26) and $13,306,957 (FY 2026-27), with a 20-year total near $258,000,000. Capital share available through the housing NOFA: $9,707,500 in FY 2025/26 (including $2,000,000 recaptured from Anton San Ramon) and $7,880,690 in FY 2026/27. FY 2026/27 awards: $5,380,690 to 949 Moraga Road (SAHA and Sunflower Hill, Lafayette, 47 IDD units) and $2,500,000 to Rumrill Commons (Novin, San Pablo, 39 units). Earlier: $5,000,000 to El Cerrito Plaza Parcel A South (Related, 69 units), $4,968,158 to Choice in Aging Senior Housing (SAHA, Pleasant Hill, 82 units, matched with $2,963,384 state LHTF), $1,770,958 to Village of Hope Pittsburg (Hope Solutions, 15 PSH cottages). Minimums: $500,000 for capital projects, $250,000 for renovation and microhome projects, $25,000 to $500,000 for predevelopment with no more than $1,000,000 a year for predevelopment (Board, Sept 16, 2025).
per_unit_cap: None beyond the HOME per-unit subsidy table used to count Measure X-assisted units; recent awards range from about $72,000 to $118,000 per total unit.
affordability_requirement: Priority to households at or below 50% AMI (designated target population); up to 80% AMI eligible. Rental loans 55 years; homeownership 20 years or more (80% AMI, 81% to 120% allowed). Grants only for pilot, innovation and capacity-building projects.
next_deadline: 2026-12-07 (FY 2027/28 NOFA with CDBG-Housing and HOME, applications due 5:00 PM). Loan agreement required within two years of contingent award; work must start within one year of loan execution; grants spent within two years.
layering_notes: County pages on www.contracosta.ca.gov refuse automated fetches (403); the same pages and DocumentCenter PDFs were opened on 2026-11-06 through the site's CivicPlus origin host (ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com), and Board reports were read through the contra-costa.legistar.com API. Largest discretionary local source in the 12 target counties. Same 3% simple, 55-year residual receipts terms as HOME, but no federal cross-cutting rules, so it is the preferred fill for projects inside cities without their own gap funds and for IDD, senior and farmworker deals. Predevelopment loans are not forgivable and must be repaid even if the project dies. The County used Measure X as the local match to win a $2,963,384 state Local Housing Trust Fund grant (FY 2024/25) and as match for Homekey awards (El Portal Place, $5,200,000). The 25% H3 share (about $4,068,983 in FY 2026/27) funds services, prevention and legal aid through a separate two-year RFP and is not capital. Awards are contingent on other commitments (Dec 31, 2027 for FY 2026/27 awards) and executed loans by June 30, 2028; the County recaptured $2,000,000 when Anton San Ramon stalled and pulled Harbor Pointe's Measure X request in May 2026. Local and state funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so state prevailing wage applies unless a 1720(c) exemption fits the deal, such as 1720(c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (see prevailing_wage_basis).

program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance In-Lieu Fee Fund (Chapter 822-4)
administering_agency: Contra Costa County Department of Conservation and Development
typical_award_size: FY 2026/27: $1,216,295 available; awards $1,000,000 to Orbisonia Village (Pacific West, Bay Point, 167 units) and $216,295 to Harbor Pointe (USA Properties, Discovery Bay, 168 units). FY 2025/26: $1,054,134 awarded. Fees come from unincorporated projects of five or more units that pay in lieu of building 15% affordable units; the fee is set annually by the Board (for rentals, the 55-year gap between average two-bedroom rent and the affordable rent; for sale units, the gap between the affordable price and the countywide median sale price).
per_unit_cap: Mixed-income projects are capped at an award based on the number of 80% AMI or 50% AMI units that exceed the inclusionary requirement.
affordability_requirement: New construction for households up to 80% AMI, unincorporated county only; preference for two-bedroom and larger units and for projects exceeding the inclusionary minimum. Cannot fund units required by density bonus or inclusionary obligations. Forgivable low-interest loan reconveyed after five years in service as affordable housing.
next_deadline: 2026-12-07 (included in the County housing NOFA when a balance exists; the FY 2027/28 NOFA names CDBG-Housing, HOME and Measure X, so confirm an in-lieu balance with DCD). FY 2026/27 awards required commitments by July 1, 2026 (Orbisonia) and Dec 31, 2027 (Harbor Pointe).

next_deadline: Tied to CDLAC rounds. Allow for a TEFRA hearing and inducement resolution before the CDLAC deadline.
layering_notes: County pages on www.contracosta.ca.gov refuse automated fetches (403); the same pages and DocumentCenter PDFs were opened on 2026-11-06 through the site's CivicPlus origin host (ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com), and Board reports were read through the contra-costa.legistar.com API. The County issues for projects it also lends to (El Cerrito Plaza, Lakeside), which keeps one regulatory agreement and one monitor; bonds are payable solely from project revenue with no County pledge and the sponsor reimburses TEFRA and approval costs. The 0.125% annual issuer fee is in line with CMFA and CSCDA. Tax-exempt bonds alone do not trigger state prevailing wage, but County, HOME or Measure X loans in the same deal do, and Davis-Bacon follows HOME and CDBG. Program overview and 2018 policy appendix are on the County DocumentCenter.
prevailing_wage_basis: False for the County conduit bond issuance itself: DIR Public Works Case No. 2006-001, Horizons at Indio (March 12, 2007), https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf, held that multifamily housing revenue bonds issued by a conduit issuer, with proceeds and repayments assigned to a private trustee and no issuer liability, are not a payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4); same holding in PW 2003-042, UC Irvine East Campus (July 28, 2006), citing PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe. The County program page and Debt Policy state the bonds involve no pledge of County revenues, taxes or assets. Current Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and (b)(4) text (california.public.law) is unchanged in substance. Any County, HOME, CDBG, Measure X or other public loan in the same deal is analyzed separately and may trigger state prevailing wage or Davis-Bacon.
audit_note: Prevailing wage set false on DIR conduit-bond determinations PW 2006-001 and PW 2003-042; covers bond issuance only, not companion public loans; determinations are fact-specific and predate later 1720(c) amendments, which do not affect the 1720(b)(1) holding.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Housing Authority of the County of Contra Costa (HACCC)
administering_agency: Housing Authority of the County of Contra Costa, 3133 Estudillo Street, Martinez; Tony Ucciferri 925-957-8055 (PBV), Robert Moore, Director of Development, 925-957-8025
typical_award_size: HACCC administers about 9,500 Housing Choice Voucher and CoC households and owns 963 public housing units plus two tax credit developments (2025 RFP). Most recent PBV invitation for proposals (REQ-12092025, released Dec 8, 2025, due Jan 8, 2026): up to 15 units for existing properties needing no more than $3,000 per unit of rehab, aimed at properties converting from CoC project-based rental assistance to PBVs. Public housing repositioning underway (Las Deltas main campus developer RFQ due Feb 4, 2025; repositioning financial and legal consultant RFPs in 2025 and 2026).
per_unit_cap: HUD PBV caps (20% of authorized vouchers agency-wide, project cap of 25% of units or 40% in low-poverty or supportive housing projects). Rents at the lower of reasonable rent or 110% of FMR.
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 50% AMI at admission (75% at or below 30% AMI); HAP contracts up to 20 years with extensions. Awards subject to HUD PBV caps and long-term affordability. Jurisdiction is the whole county except Pittsburg; the Richmond Housing Authority and Pittsburg Housing Authority serve their cities (Pass 3).

layering_notes: PBVs are the operating subsidy of choice for Contra Costa PSH and CoC-funded buildings, and the 2025 solicitation shows HACCC converting CoC rental assistance to PBVs to free CoC dollars. Underwrite PBV rents at the HAP contract rent; a PBV HAP contract is not a prevailing wage trigger, but Davis-Bacon applies to PBV new construction or rehab of nine or more contract units. HACCC is not a Moving to Work agency. Public housing repositioning (Las Deltas in North Richmond, El Pueblo, Bayo Vista) may produce RAD or Section 18 PBV units for partner developers. prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (HUD PBV development requirements, labor standards): for development activity (new construction or rehabilitation) involving nine or more PBV contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and the PHA monitors compliance; existing-housing PBV contracts with no development activity do not trigger it. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153 The December 8, 2025 HACCC PBV invitation also states Federal Labor Standards may be applicable.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: HACCC closed solicitations page and the December 8, 2025 PBV invitation confirm up to 15 units, existing properties with no more than $3,000 per unit of rehab, CoC PBRA conversion purpose, jurisdiction excluding Pittsburg, due January 8, 2026. program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Ch. 822-4) and Residential Density Bonus Ordinance (Ch. 822-2)
administering_agency: Contra Costa County Department of Conservation and Development, Community Development Division
typical_award_size: Inclusionary: 15% of units in unincorporated projects of five or more units must be affordable (rental: 20% of those at very low income, remainder lower income; for-sale: 20% lower, remainder moderate), 55-year rental term, with in-lieu fee, off-site units or land dedication as alternatives. Density bonus: up to 15% for providing the required inclusionary units (822-2.402), with state law bonuses under Government Code 65915 for units beyond the requirement, land donation and child care, and incentives or concessions per 65915(d)(2). Incentives for inclusionary compliance (822-4.418(c)) may include fee deferrals or waivers, housing set-aside funds, tax-exempt financing and zoning modifications at County discretion.
affordability_requirement: Inclusionary units: 55 years for rentals; for-sale units owner-occupied with resale controls and County recapture. Density bonus target units: 30 years or longer if required by financing (822-2.410); density bonus housing agreement recorded against the property.
next_deadline: Not applicable; applies by right to unincorporated projects at entitlement. Developer agreements are approved by the Board (for example Grayson Road and Walnut Estates density bonus and inclusionary agreements, April 2026). Confirm current code text with DCD; the County code is hosted on Municode (blocked to automated access), and the mirror read for this record was Zoneomics.
layering_notes: County pages on www.contracosta.ca.gov refuse automated fetches (403); the same pages and DocumentCenter PDFs were opened on 2026-11-06 through the site's CivicPlus origin host (ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com), and Board reports were read through the contra-costa.legistar.com API. The ordinance text itself was read on the Zoneomics mirror of the County Ordinance Code. In-lieu fees from this chapter feed the County's In-Lieu Fee Fund (separate record). A 100% affordable project is exempt from the inclusionary requirement and takes the state density bonus and concessions directly; the County's density bonus submittal checklist and 2025 rent maximums are on the County ordinances page. In-lieu funds cannot be used for units that satisfy inclusionary or density bonus obligations. Density bonus alone does not trigger prevailing wage.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: the source URL host (contracosta.ca.gov) returns 403; the identical page on ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com confirms 15% affordable in projects of five or more units, very low, lower and moderate targets, and in-lieu fee, off-site and land conveyance alternatives, and the May 19, 2026 Board staff report (Legistar 18528) restates the 15% and five-unit rule. Tenure splits and 822-2.402 and 822-2.410 details were not re-read (Municode blocked, Zoneomics page not found).
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this inclusionary and density bonus ordinance provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City or County loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on the project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Welfare Exemption (property tax), Contra Costa County Assessor
administering_agency: Contra Costa County Assessor, Gus Kramer, 2530 Arnold Drive Suite 100, Martinez, 925-313-7400
typical_award_size: Full or partial exemption of property tax on units occupied by households at or below 80% AMI (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)); worth roughly 1.1% or more of assessed value a year depending on the tax rate area (1% base rate plus voter-approved debt). File early; supplemental affidavits are required for every claim year.
per_unit_cap: Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)(1)(C): where a property qualifies only because 90% or more of occupants are lower income households (no bond, government loan or grant financing under (A) and no tax credits under (B)), the total exemption is capped at $20,000,000 of assessed value. Projects financed under (A) or receiving LIHTC under (B) are outside the cap.
affordability_requirement: Nonprofit or LP with eligible nonprofit managing general partner holding a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate; units restricted by recorded regulatory agreement or occupied by households at or below 80% AMI; BOE-267 first filing and BOE-267-L, L1 or L2 supplemental affidavits annually by Feb 15 (late claims receive a reduced exemption under Rev. and Tax. Code 270).
next_deadline: 2027-02-15 (annual claim deadline for the 2027-28 roll). First-year claims can be filed on acquisition; construction-period exemption is available under 214(g) once the OCC is in hand.
layering_notes: County pages on www.contracosta.ca.gov refuse automated fetches (403); the same pages and DocumentCenter PDFs were opened on 2026-11-06 through the site's CivicPlus origin host (ca-contracostacounty3.civicplus.com), and Board reports were read through the contra-costa.legistar.com API. Standard in every tax credit operating budget; underwrite the exemption only for the restricted units and confirm the managing GP's OCC before closing. The Assessor's site has no dedicated welfare exemption page; forms are under the Assessor's Forms link and the BOE county contacts page lists the office. The BOE's assessment practices survey of Contra Costa recommended tighter handling of late-filing provisions, so expect staff to apply the statutory late penalties strictly.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: the Assessor landing page (source_url) carries no welfare exemption detail; statute text read on california.public.law. 214 contains no construction-period language (see 214.1 for property in the course of construction), so the next_deadline note citing 214(g) for that should be checked.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) and (b)(4) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works requires construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, including fees, loans or other obligations normally required in executing the construction contract that are reduced or waived. The welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) reduces property tax on the completed property; it pays no construction cost, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage.

program_name: Orange County 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA (HOME, HOME-ARP, MHSA/BHSA, 15G Reserves, Housing Successor funds)
administering_agency: OC Housing and Community Development (OC Community Resources), 1501 E. St. Andrew Place, Santa Ana; Michelle Zdeba, Housing Development Manager, 714-480-2994; Sherluna Vien 714-480-2936; OCHCD.NOFA@occr.ocgov.com
typical_award_size: Up to $20,900,000 in loans authorized by the Board Feb 10, 2026 and released March 6, 2026 (OpenGov NOFA 2026-01), plus up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream or VASH project-based vouchers. Replaces the 2025 NOFA ($12,050,000 and up to 150 PBVs) and the 2023 NOFA ($67,100,000 authorized, $32,700,000 and 218 PBVs in Amendment 1). Maximum County subsidy per assisted unit: $137,500 (any bedroom size) in the unincorporated area and Urban County participating cities; $95,000 (0BR), $100,000 (1BR), $105,000 (2BR+) in all other cities. MHSA/BHSA capital limit $207,235 per regulated unit plus up to $207,235 per unit for a capitalized operating subsidy reserve. Minimum five assisted units; total development cost above TCAC's $650,000 per unit threshold needs justification.
per_unit_cap: $137,500 per County-assisted unit in unincorporated areas and participating cities; $95,000 to $105,000 elsewhere; HOME units also capped at HUD 221(d)(3) limits; MHSA/BHSA $207,235 per regulated unit (rises 4% a year, locked at application).
affordability_requirement: All County-assisted units restricted to households at or below 30% AMI who are experiencing homelessness, filled through the Coordinated Entry System, with a 55-year regulatory agreement from the qualified project period. MHSA/BHSA units serve adults with serious mental illness and may not exceed 49% of project units. next_deadline: Open on a first come, first served basis as of November 8, 2026 until funds are committed by Board action, the NOFA is replaced, or HCD suspends intake; no fixed deadline. All geographic tiers are now open (any eligible location since the third tier began in June 2026). Allow at least eight months from a complete application to Board approval. PBVs only for sites in OCHA jurisdiction.
layering_notes: The County's only capital program and it is PSH only: every assisted unit must be 30% AMI and CES-referred, so it fits a 4% or 9% deal with a PSH set-aside, not a general affordable project. Terms: 3% simple interest, 55 years, residual receipts split 50% to public lenders pro rata and 50% to the developer, monitoring fees of $500 setup plus $3,795 a year plus $22 per unit, replacement reserves $250 to $500 per unit, partnership management fee up to $25,000. Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units or nine or more PBV units; projects using only MHSA/BHSA or Housing Successor money may avoid Davis-Bacon but state prevailing wage applies to public funds. HOME-ARP, 15G Reserves and Housing Successor dollars are pooled here rather than offered separately. OCHA PBVs can be requested with no capital. Homekey+ projects vetted through the County RFI skip the geographic tiers. NOFA, exhibits and sample loan documents are posted on the NOFA page (opened 2026-11-06).
cycle_notes: 2026 NOFA (OpenGov 2026-01) released March 6, 2026 as an open, first come, first served process; geographic tiers phased in March 6, May 5 and June 4, 2026. Exhibits were revised through October 2026 (PBV acknowledgement dated October 5, 2026), and the NOFA page lists no closure as of November 8, 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).
