prevailing_wage_basis: HOME: 24 CFR 92.354 Davis-Bacon applies to rental projects with 12 or more HOME-assisted units; CDBG: Davis-Bacon under Section 110 of the HCD Act of 1974 applies to residential construction of 8 or more units. The FY 2026-27 Action Plan (housing.oc.gov) also notes State and Davis-Bacon prevailing wage costs.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: FY 2026-27 Action Plan matches CDBG $3,467,220 plus $20,000 program income and $806,834 prior-year ($4,294,054), HOME $1,244,582.84 plus $135,000, ESG $302,608, and remaining ConPlan estimates of $12,882,162 CDBG and $4,138,748 HOME. The FY 2027-28 FAPP (public review October 9 to November 9, 2026) says the one-year Public Facilities and Improvements RFA is anticipated to be released in December 2026; applications were generally due in November in prior cycles. HUD unit thresholds for Davis-Bacon added as the prevailing wage basis.

program_name: MHSA/BHSA permanent supportive housing capital and Capitalized Operating Subsidy Reserve (Orange County Health Care Agency through OC Community Resources)
administering_agency: OC Health Care Agency, Behavioral Health Services (MHSA/BHSA Housing Program), with OC Housing and Community Development administering loans
typical_award_size: BHSA Integrated Plan FY 2026-29 (Board May 19, 2026): Housing Interventions component $73,500,000 a year; planned capital development $18,375,000 a year (the 25% statutory maximum) plus about $990,508 from other sources; rental subsidies $14,000,000 a year; operating subsidies $6,787,829 a year; $36,750,000 a year reserved for chronically homeless people. Named capital pipeline: Mercury Senior Apartments (Brea), Lampson Workforce Housing (Los Alamitos) and projects to be determined in San Juan Capistrano, Anaheim Hills, Buena Park and Fountain Valley, 56 BHSA units of 416 at about $208,000 per BHSA unit. Since June 2018 the County has completed 476 MHSA units with 196 in the pipeline toward a goal of 2,396 PSH units by 2029; each MHSA dollar leveraged about $5.50. HCA also granted $20,500,000 of MHSA and General Fund to the Orange County Housing Finance Trust. Loan limit $207,235 per regulated unit for capital and another $207,235 for COSR under the 2026 NOFA.
per_unit_cap: $207,235 per MHSA/BHSA regulated unit (capital) plus up to $207,235 per unit COSR; BHSA statute caps the housing intervention share at $450,000 per unit.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low income (30% AMI) adults experiencing homelessness with a serious mental disorder (WIC 5600.3(b), BHSA eligibility under WIC 5830(a)), certified by HCA and referred through CES; rents at 30% of the 30% AMI limit or 30% of SSI; no minimum income where PBVs or COSR are provided; MHSA/BHSA units at most 49% of the project; units at least 450 square feet with full kitchens and furnishings; 55-year covenant.
next_deadline: Apply through the 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA (open since March 6, 2026) with an HCA review meeting before submission. The three-year plan runs July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 with annual updates; HCA moves money to OCCR under a three-year spending plan, so NOFA amounts rise when new BHSA allocations post.
layering_notes: Orange County's BHSA program is the deepest county PSH source in the 13 counties researched: $18,400,000 a year in planned capital plus a COSR that replaces PBVs when none are available (zero interest, forgivable over 15 to 20 years, sized to cover MHSA unit operating deficits). Pair the capital with 4% credits and OCHA or city PBVs; use COSR when PBVs are refused. MHSA/BHSA capital alone may avoid Davis-Bacon; the NOFA says state prevailing wage may apply under Labor Code 1720 and is decided per project with counsel input, while HOME (12+ units) or PBVs (9+ units) trigger Davis-Bacon. Terms are in Attachment D of the 2026 NOFA (opened); budget figures from the Integrated Plan PDF on ochealthinfo.com (opened). HCA does not run its own developer NOFA.
prevailing_wage_basis: 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA Section 2.23 and Exhibit 4.03.01 (OC Housing and Community Development, March 6, 2026): projects funded only with local resources such as MHSA/BHSA may be exempt from Davis-Bacon; use of MHSA funds 'may require' state prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720, the County may require the applicant's legal counsel to confirm whether state prevailing wage applies, and an applicant may submit an attorney opinion that it does not (Section 4.03.01). Davis-Bacon applies separately when HOME (12+ HOME units) or PBVs (9+ units) are layered. State prevailing wage therefore depends on Labor Code 1720(b) and 1720(c) project facts.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: Attachment D loan limits ($207,235 capital plus $207,235 COSR per regulated unit), 30% AMI targeting, 49% cap, CES referral and COSR terms match; Integrated Plan (June 11, 2026 version) confirms $73,500,000 Housing Interventions, $18,375,000 plus $990,508 capital, $14,000,000 rental subsidies, $6,787,829 operating subsidies, $36,750,000 chronically homeless, 6 projects with 56 BHSA units of 416, 476 completed and 196 pipeline units, 2,396 goal and $5.50 leverage. NOFA page still lists the 2026 NOFA as open (exhibits updated October 2026); funds first-come, first-served until committed or replaced. The $20,500,000 Housing Finance Trust grant was not found in the Integrated Plan and was not rechecked. Attachment D says units are encouraged (not required) to be at least 450 square feet and one-bedroom.

program_name: Orange County Housing Finance Trust (OCHFT) permanent supportive and affordable housing loans
administering_agency: Orange County Housing Finance Trust, joint powers authority of the County of Orange and 27 cities (9-member board, 4 County and 5 city seats), administered by County staff
typical_award_size: 2024 NOFA (due March 15, 2024, availability extended by Addendum 2 through July 2026, now fully committed): $25,700,502 from County MHSA ($12,371,809), County General Fund ($1,000,000) and state Local Housing Trust Fund matching grants ($12,328,693), split in thirds across North, Central and South service planning areas, project cap $3,500,000. Awards 2020 to 2024: $55,035,131 to 32 project awards funding 441 Trust-restricted units in 2,477 total units (2024 round $22,143,076 for 152 units across 10 projects including Cypress Village Irvine $3,500,000 and Aspan Court Lake Forest $3,490,000). June 30, 2025 audit: notes receivable $25,013,554, net position $54,579,510; FY 2024-25 deposits $4,000,000 MHSA, $1,200,000 County, $3,000,000 CalOptima, $402,747 LHTF. $250,000 federal community project funding presented April 2026. Goal 2,396 PSH units by 2029.
per_unit_cap: 2024 NOFA: $126,000 (0BR), $140,000 (1BR), $154,000 (2BR+) for non-MHSA units; $191,600 per MHSA unit; $3,500,000 per development unless waived by the board.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low, very low and low income households and people experiencing homelessness; MHSA units for homeless adults with serious mental illness; LHTF-funded units at or below 60% AMI per state rules; 55-year covenant. Projects must be in the unincorporated area or a member city, and LHTF dollars only in cities compliant with state housing law; MHSA-only requests may be anywhere in the county.
next_deadline: No open NOFA as of Nov 2026; the 2024 NOFA has no funds remaining and no 2025 or 2026 round was posted. Watch the Trust's NOFA page and board agendas; rounds have opened each spring since 2020 when state LHTF matches were awarded. An Affordable ADU Loan Program is also offered.
layering_notes: Regional JPA recorded at county level because the County seeded it and sits on its board; it is the vehicle that captured $12,300,000 of state LHTF matches for Orange County. Terms mirror the County NOFA: 3% simple, 55 years from conversion, 50% residual receipts, TCAC developer fee limits, $25,000 partnership management fee cap. Awards are small ($500,000 to $3,500,000) and used as last-in gap money on 4% and 9% deals, often alongside County MHSA loans and OCHA PBVs. Member cities: Aliso Viejo, Anaheim, Buena Park, Costa Mesa, Dana Point, Fountain Valley, Fullerton, Garden Grove, Huntington Beach, Irvine, La Habra, Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, Laguna Niguel, Lake Forest, Los Alamitos, Mission Viejo, Newport Beach, Orange, Placentia, San Juan Capistrano, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, Stanton, Tustin, Westminster and Yorba Linda. OCHFT NOFA Section 3.12 makes LHTF-funded projects subject to state prevailing wage unless a Labor Code 1720(c) exception applies (see prevailing_wage_basis). NOFA page, developments page, member list and 2025 audit opened; the 2024 NOFA PDF is hosted on Squarespace.
prevailing_wage_basis: OCHFT 2024 NOFA Section 3.12: projects receiving LHTF Program funds are subject to state prevailing wage law (Labor Code 1720 et seq.) unless a Labor Code 1720(c) exception applies as determined by DIR. https://www.ochft.org/s/OCHFT-2024-NOFA-with-attachments.pdf
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: NOFA page and 2024 NOFA confirm $25,700,502.59 total, $3,500,000 project cap, per-unit limits $126,000/$140,000/$154,000 and $191,600 MHSA, SPA thirds, 55-year covenant, Addendum 2 extension and no remaining funds. Audit and award totals not re-checked.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Orange County Housing Authority (OCHA)
administering_agency: Orange County Housing Authority (OC Community Resources), 1501 E. St. Andrew Place, Santa Ana, 714-480-2700; PBV requests through OC Housing and Community Development NOFA staff
typical_award_size: 26 PBV projects listed on the OCHA site total 693 PBV units (for example Stanton Inn 71, Oasis Huntington Beach 62, Tahiti 59, Ascent 57, Avon River 48, Casa Paloma 48, Crossroads at Washington 43, Salida Del Sol 40). The 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA offers up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream or VASH PBVs (150 under the 2025 NOFA; 218 under the 2023 NOFA Amendment 1). Pipeline as of Feb 2026: Cartwright Irvine (8 PBV, 60 units, May 2026), Avon River Costa Mesa (14 PBV plus 10 VASH, 78 units), Orion Orange (3 PBV, 166 units), Lincoln Avenue Buena Park (13 PBV, 55 units, Nov 2026), Casa Colibri Midway City (30 PBV, 71 units, Dec 2026). Total OCHA voucher count was not confirmed from an opened document.
per_unit_cap: HUD limits: 20% of authorized vouchers plus 10% for homeless, veteran, supportive services, low-poverty or FUP/FYI units; project cap 25% of units (no cap for supportive housing and elderly units). Rents at the lower of reasonable rent or 110% of FMR with OCHA utility allowances.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low income households experiencing homelessness referred through the Coordinated Entry System; VASH units need VA eligibility; many projects are senior (62 plus) or MHSA/NPLH restricted. Tenants pay 30% of income. HAP contracts up to 20 years with a 20-year extension option.
next_deadline: Request PBVs through the open 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA (OpenGov 2026-01); PBVs are available only for sites in OCHA jurisdiction (the county except Anaheim, Santa Ana and Garden Grove, which run their own authorities) and may be limited by federal funding changes. OCHA posts PBV waitlist openings per project; the 2027 payment standards were posted Nov 2026.
layering_notes: OCHA PBVs are the standard operating subsidy for Orange County PSH and are awarded with or without County capital under the same NOFA; the 2026 NOFA lets the County claim part of the NOI the PBVs create for services. A HAP contract is not a prevailing wage trigger but Davis-Bacon applies to new construction or rehab of nine or more PBV units, and PBVs bring NEPA and a HUD subsidy layering review. Four PHAs operate in the county (OCHA, Anaheim, Santa Ana, Garden Grove); their PBV pipelines are tracked by the CoC Housing Opportunities Committee. OCHA is not a Moving to Work agency. Sources opened: OCHA project-based page, 2026 NOFA Section III, Feb 11, 2026 Housing Opportunities Committee slides.
prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2): for PBV development activity (new construction or rehabilitation) involving nine or more contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages; the PHA monitors compliance. Existing-housing PBV contracts with no development activity do not trigger it. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: OCHA project-based page matches the 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA offer of up to 100 HCV, Mainstream or VASH PBVs (150 under the 2025 NOFA) and the pipeline (Lincoln Avenue Buena Park 13 PBV, Avon River 24 plus 10 VASH preferences, Orion 8 senior units, Cartwright 8, Oasis 62). Prevailing wage changed from false to true because the record covers new construction and acquisition-rehab and 24 CFR 983.153(c) requires Davis-Bacon at nine or more PBV contract units in development.

program_name: Apartment Development Revenue Bond Program, County of Orange conduit issuer
administering_agency: County Executive Office, Public Finance (Louis McClure, 714-834-5999, Luis.McClure@ocgov.com) with the Public Financing Advisory Committee (PFAC) and Board of Supervisors
typical_award_size: Tax-exempt multifamily bonds for new construction or acquisition-rehab anywhere in Orange County; a typical bond loan is $7,000,000 or more with issuance costs of about $300,000, 30-year amortization, credit enhanced (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, bank letter of credit) or privately placed at County discretion. Borrower pays all issuance and finance team costs. No recent County issuances were located; most Orange County deals use CMFA or CSCDA (for example Valencia Garden in Orange, CMFA $18,499,022).
affordability_requirement: At least 20% of units for very low income households, or 10% very low plus 30% at 60% AMI, for the longer of 15 years or the life of the bonds (about 30 years); County loans may be added for deeper affordability.
next_deadline: Apply after site control and a lender commitment: PFAC approves the financing concept and team, the Board holds the TEFRA hearing and adopts the inducement resolution, then the County applies to CDLAC; bonds must close within 90 days of the CDLAC award. Call the CEO public finance contact before preparing an application.
layering_notes: The County keeps a conduit program on paper (Attachment H to the 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA, opened) but the pipeline shows cities and developers using CMFA and CSCDA instead; expect PFAC review to add six to eight weeks versus a JPA issuer. Bonds alone do not trigger state prevailing wage; County loans in the same deal do. Confirm current issuer fees with the CEO, as none are published.
prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Public Works Coverage Determination PW 2006-001 (citing PW 2004-016, Rancho Santa Fe Village, Feb 25, 2005) holds that publicly offered conduit multifamily revenue bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and is not a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4), because bond proceeds and repayments flow through a private trustee and never enter public coffers (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf). Applies to the bond loan alone; County OC Community Resources loans or other public funds added to the deal can trigger state prevailing wage. The determination addressed publicly offered bonds; confirm treatment if the County privately places the bonds.
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for the bond financing itself per DIR PW 2006-001; Attachment H reopened and is silent on prevailing wage.

program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), Orange County Urban County entitlement
administering_agency: OC Housing and Community Development (HCD entitlement grantee for the Urban County)
typical_award_size: HCD 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA: Orange County CY 2024 $892,973, CY 2025 $956,505, five-year estimate $5,581,081. The County's amended PLHA Five-Year Plan (Attachment A-C-E, December 2023 NOFA) uses only Sections 301(a)(6) and 301(a)(7): about 88% for homelessness activities (45% Buena Park and Placentia navigation centers via the North SPA collaborative, 32% regional emergency shelters such as the Yale Transitional Center for the unincorporated area and Laguna Hills, 4% Laguna Beach case management and supportive services, 7% Dana Point outreach and rapid rehousing), 7% for accessibility modifications in low-income senior owner-occupied homes in Laguna Woods (3%) and Seal Beach (4%), and 5% administration. The plan marks 301(a)(1) rental housing development and 301(a)(2) workforce housing as not selected, so no PLHA development money is offered to developers.
affordability_requirement: All PLHA-assisted households at or below 60% AMI under the County plan (shelter and navigation center clients counted at 30% AMI; accessibility modification recipients at or below 60% AMI). No rental development covenants because the plan funds no development.
next_deadline: HCD formula allocations arrive annually; no County PLHA NOFA to developers exists. Ask OCHCD whether the plan was amended for the state's 2024 requirement that 40% of new PLHA fund owner-occupied workforce housing, and whether the 11.45% development share is folded into the Supportive Housing NOFA.
layering_notes: Not a capital source in practice: under $1,000,000 a year and almost all of it pays for shelter and navigation center operations. Anaheim, Santa Ana, Irvine and other entitlement cities receive their own PLHA (Pass 3). Plan PDF and community development page opened on housing.oc.gov; amounts from the HCD 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA.
eligible_project_detail: navigation center and emergency shelter capital and operations
homeless supportive services and rapid rehousing
accessibility modifications for low-income senior owner-occupied homes
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports it.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines and Formula Allocation NOFA contain no prevailing wage section (only the Non-Entitlement Competitive NOFA does); Orange County uses its formula share mainly for shelter operations, which are not construction under 1720(a)(1). https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf

program_name: Housing Successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (Orange County Housing Authority as Housing Successor to the Orange County Development Agency)
administering_agency: Orange County Housing Authority as Housing Successor, administered by OC Housing and Community Development
typical_award_size: Housing Asset Fund balance $29,240,000 at June 30, 2024 (FY 2023-24 SB 341 report). Funds are offered only through the County's Supportive Housing NOFAs: $4,000,000 added to the 2016 PSH NOFA in April 2018; 2020 NOFA awards of $2,400,000 to Clara Vista (former Tahiti Motel, Stanton, 60 PSH units, completed Dec 2023) and $453,600 each to Mountain View (Lake Forest, 71 units) and Orchard View Gardens (Buena Park, 66 units); no Housing Successor funds were in the 2023 NOFA, but they are a named source in the 2026 NOFA.
per_unit_cap: Follows the Supportive Housing NOFA limits ($137,500 per unit in unincorporated areas and participating cities).
affordability_requirement: Health and Safety Code 34176.1: households at or below 80% AMI, at least 30% of spending over five years for extremely low income households, 55-year covenants; excess surplus rules force spending when the unencumbered balance exceeds the greater of $1,000,000 or four years of deposits.
next_deadline: No separate round; request Housing Successor funds through the open 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA (first come, first served, no fixed deadline as of November 8, 2026).
layering_notes: A large idle balance (about $29,000,000) that the County must spend to avoid excess surplus findings, so it is the most flexible local money in the NOFA pool: no federal strings, 30% AMI target through the NOFA. Use it for sites outside HOME geography or where Davis-Bacon is a problem. Housing successor funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), but 1720(c)(4) excludes affordable units paid for solely from Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund money; other funds in the deal decide coverage (see prevailing_wage_basis). Housing successor page and FY 2023-24 report PDF opened on housing.oc.gov.
cycle_notes: Offered only through the County Supportive Housing NOFA. The FY 2024-25 SB 341 report link on the Housing Successor page still returned 404 on 2026-11-08; the FY 2023-24 report is the latest readable report.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Local loans can be public funds under 1720(b)(1), (b)(4) or (b)(5), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20 or more years at 80% AMI or below, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy (under $600,000 and under 2% of total project cost). Labor Code 1720(c)(4) also provides that affordable housing paid for solely with former redevelopment Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund moneys (H&S Code 33334.2 and 33334.3) is not paid for out of public funds; whether that carve-out reaches housing successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund money under H&S Code 34176 is not settled in the sources read. No OCHA housing successor prevailing wage rule found. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports it.

program_name: Housing Opportunities Overlay (Zoning Code 7-9-44), Affordable Housing Permit (7-9-124.3) and density bonus (7-9-87)
administering_agency: OC Public Works, OC Development Services, Planning Division (Deysi Munoz, 714-667-8815, Deysi.munoz@ocpw.ocgov.com)
typical_award_size: The 2024 Housing Opportunities Overlay Manual allows 100% affordable rental or ownership projects, emergency shelters, multi-service centers and low-barrier navigation centers by right in the C1, C2, CN, MX, M1, R2, R3 and R4 districts of unincorporated Orange County, approved through an administrative Affordable Housing Permit with no public hearing (the permit process also applies to projects at least 20% affordable in those districts). Qualified projects must be 100% affordable to low and very low income households (at or below 80% AMI), with 70% low income and at least 30% very low income units, a minimum density of 30 units per acre and generally at least 16 units. Density bonus follows Government Code 65915; on-menu incentives include side, front and rear setback reductions, up to 10 feet and one additional story of height, and a lot consolidation density incentive up to 45% total. The County NOFA's Attachment J lists eligible sites. No county inclusionary housing ordinance or in-lieu fee.
affordability_requirement: Overlay projects: 100% affordable, 70% low income and 30% very low income, with recorded covenants; density bonus units per state law (55 years for rental).
next_deadline: Not applicable; ministerial. Unincorporated communities include Midway City, Rossmoor, North Tustin, Ladera Ranch, Rancho Mission Viejo, Silverado and El Modena. Confirm site eligibility with OC Development Services; processing fee deposit applies.
layering_notes: The overlay matters because most of the County's own land-use authority covers small pockets; the 2026 NOFA gives unincorporated overlay sites the first 60-day application window and the higher $137,500 per unit subsidy. Density bonus and by-right approval do not trigger prevailing wage. Manual PDF opened on ocds.ocpublicworks.com; zoning code mirror on Zoneomics shows section headings and overlay affordability terms.
audit_note: Tier 1 audit 2026-11-08: old ocds.ocpublicworks.com URL 307-redirects to pwds.oc.gov; Manual re-read. Manual lists a 10-foot plus one story height incentive, not the 12 feet previously recorded, and lists R2, R3 and R4 residential districts rather than arterial parcels.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Development fee waiver for affordable housing (no countywide program)
administering_agency: OC Public Works, OC Development Services
typical_award_size: None adopted. The County has no impact fee waiver or deferral program for affordable housing in the unincorporated area. The 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA treats city waivers of impact, school, sanitation and mitigation fees as eligible local match, and County loans may pay building permit fees as an eligible cost.
affordability_requirement: Not applicable.
next_deadline: Not applicable. Ask the host city for fee waivers to satisfy the County NOFA match requirement.
layering_notes: Negative finding. Unincorporated projects pay full County, school district and sanitation district fees; the Affordable Housing Permit carries a processing deposit. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) counts any waived fee as public funds for prevailing wage purposes.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: 2026 County NOFA Section 2.16 lists waivers of impact, school, sanitation district and mitigation fees as allowable match and lists building permit and impact fees as eligible costs; no County fee waiver program found.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program exists, so nothing here pays for construction; Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) applies only to construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. Any fee waiver or deferral granted case by case would be public funds under 1720(b)(4) and is tested on the project.

program_name: Welfare Exemption (property tax), Orange County Assessor
administering_agency: Orange County Assessor, Claude Parrish, 500 S. Main Street, Orange; Institutional Exemptions unit 714-834-2779; main line 714-834-2727
typical_award_size: Full or partial exemption of property tax on units occupied by households at or below 80% AMI under Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g); worth roughly 1.1% or more of assessed value a year depending on the tax rate area. The Assessor posts current BOE-267 series forms (2026 BOE-267-R is online).
per_unit_cap: Exemption is the share of value equal to the share of units serving lower income households. Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer only for claims based solely on occupancy (90% or more of occupants lower income at Health and Safety Code 50053 rents) and not by a limited partnership with an eligible nonprofit managing general partner; projects with bond, government loan or grant financing under regulatory agreements (214(g)(1)(A)) or tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are not subject to the cap.
affordability_requirement: Nonprofit or LP with eligible nonprofit managing general partner holding a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate; units restricted by recorded regulatory agreement or occupied by households at or below 80% AMI; BOE-267 first filing and BOE-267-L, L1 or L2 supplemental affidavits annually by Feb 15 (late claims receive a reduced exemption under Rev. and Tax. Code 270).
next_deadline: 2027-02-15 (annual claim deadline for the 2027-28 roll). File the first claim on acquisition so the construction period is covered.
layering_notes: Standard in every tax credit operating budget; underwrite only the restricted units and confirm the managing GP's OCC before closing. The Assessor's institutional exemptions page describes the welfare exemption in general terms only; the exemptions unit phone comes from the Assessor's contact page (both opened). The BOE county contacts page lists the same office.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: OC Assessor Institutional Exemptions page is general (no low-income housing detail); BOE Publication 149 confirms BOE-267 filing by February 15 and partial exemption for late claims. The record misdescribed who is subject to the $20 million cap. Prevailing wage false is uncited.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) and (b)(4) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works requires construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, including fees, loans or other obligations normally required in executing the construction contract that are reduced or waived. The welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) reduces property tax on the completed property; it pays no construction cost, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage.

program_name: Santa Ana, Anaheim/Orange County Continuum of Care (CA-602) and HHAP
administering_agency: County of Orange, County Executive Office, Office of Care Coordination (CoC lead agency and HHAP administrative entity); Orange County CoC Board
typical_award_size: HHAP by round, County of Orange: R1 $7,486,576, R2 $3,422,435, R3 $9,582,817, R4 $7,131,233, R5 $8,346,727, R6 $8,355,062 (agreement through June 30, 2030). Orange County CoC: R1 $8,081,116, R2 $3,823,692, R3 $10,267,304, R4 $7,600,842, R5 $8,699,841, R6 $8,923,350; Anaheim, Santa Ana and Irvine each $5,947,855 in R6 for a regional R6 total of $35,100,000 awarded April 2026. State accountability site: $152,700,000 HHAP rounds 1 to 5 to the Orange County area, $36,000,000 directly to the County ($28,900,000 obligated, $15,300,000 spent by mid-2025); Encampment Resolution Funding $8,700,000 area, $3,600,000 County. HHAP-6 CoC budget: $3,976,421 permanent housing operating subsidies, $592,335 youth operating subsidies, $1,552,663 rapid rehousing, $1,222,663 interim housing operating subsidies, $330,000 youth interim, $624,635 services, $624,635 administration and HMIS. HUD CoC FY 2024 awards to CA-602 included $1,249,326 Permanent Housing Collaborative, $731,787 rapid rehousing and $528,250 Jackson Aisle TRA (partial list). 2024 PIT: 7,322 people, 4,173 unsheltered, 9,751 year-round beds. affordability_requirement: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness per HUD and state definitions; CoC permanent housing through Coordinated Entry; HHAP-6 obligation and expenditure deadlines (75% obligated and 50% spent by June 30, 2027). HHAP-5 regional plan governs HHAP-6 uses.
next_deadline: No open local solicitation as of November 8, 2026. program_name: Measure W Home Together Fund: Multifamily Homelessness Solutions capital and operating subsidy
administering_agency: Alameda County Housing and Community Development Department (HCD), 224 W. Winton Avenue, Room 108, Hayward, 510-670-6417, HCDRFP@acgov.org, with Alameda County Health, Housing and Homelessness Services (H&H)
typical_award_size: Measure W is a half-cent, ten-year general sales tax (Nov 2020) held in escrow until the lawsuit ended in April 2025: $810,000,000 accrued through June 2025 plus about $170,000,000 a year through June 2031. Board framework of July 30, 2025: 80% of ongoing revenue (about $136,000,000 a year) plus $585,800,000 one-time to the Home Together Fund ($1,400,000,000 through 2031), $170,000,000 prudent reserve, 20% to an Essential County Services Fund. FY 2025-26 Home Together Fund allocation $168,900,000 (Housing $96,000,000, Shelter $30,000,000, Access $11,000,000, Prevention $8,000,000, System Foundations $21,000,000); one-time capital acquisition line $180,000,000 for 850 or more housing and shelter units. 2025 New Construction RFP (released Oct 27, 2025, due Dec 8, 2025): about $40,000,000 for capital and operating subsidies; Board awarded $50,000,000 on March 3, 2026 to 10 shovel-ready projects (Liberation Park, 500 Lake Park, 3135 San Pablo, East 12th Circle and Brighter Bancroft Senior in Oakland; Ephesian Legacy Court and People's Park Supportive in Berkeley; 1247 McKay in Alameda; Downtown Livermore, Eden Housing 130 units; Thornton Avenue in Newark, $2,950,000), more than 900 homes with 346 for people exiting homelessness. A separate acquisition and rehabilitation RFP of about $10,000,000 was planned for early 2026, and a one-time $15,000,000 Emergency Stabilization pool for distressed nonprofit owners closed Jan 12, 2026.
per_unit_cap: Capital $175,000 per studio or one-bedroom homeless unit and $200,000 per two-bedroom unit; capitalized operating subsidy reserve up to $225,000 per Coordinated Entry unit sized to a 15-year operating gap; combined per-unit maximum about $225,000 (redlined to $250,000 in the Nov 17, 2025 revision).
affordability_requirement: Assisted units restricted to extremely low income households at or below 30% AMI referred through the Home Together Coordinated Entry System, with supportive services; rents underwritten at the lesser of 50% AMI TCAC rent or 30% of 30% AMI; County regulatory agreement senior to bank documents for 59 years (55 years allowed in tax credit deals).
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The 2025 New Construction RFP closed December 8, 2025 and was awarded March 3, 2026; the planned acquisition and rehabilitation RFP of about $10,000,000 (announced for early 2026) is not posted on the HCD Current Funding Opportunities page. Join the HCD email list for the next Measure W capital round.
layering_notes: The largest new local source in the state outside Los Angeles: a dedicated $1,400,000,000 homelessness fund with a capital line and, unusually, a 15-year capitalized operating subsidy that lets PSH units pencil without PBVs. Loan terms follow Appendix B of the RFP: 3% simple interest, 59-year term, payments amortized, deferred for ELI special needs projects, or from residual receipts with the general partner allowed up to 50% as an incentive management fee. The RFP requires California prevailing wage even where state law would not. The 2026 awards were sized to make 4% and 9% deals and Homekey+ applications competitive, so the realistic ask is $175,000 to $225,000 per homeless unit as last-in money. The services side of the fund (rental subsidies, flexible housing pool, shelter rates) is run by H&H, not HCD. Sources opened: HCD Measure W page, funding opportunities page, the revised RFP PDF, the July 30, 2025 Board presentation and the Home Together FAQ.
cycle_notes: Competitive RFP rounds issued by Alameda County HCD with H&H. 2025 New Construction RFP released October 27, 2025, revised November 17, 2025, due December 8, 2025 (about $40,000,000; $50,000,000 awarded to 10 projects March 3, 2026). Separate one-time Emergency Stabilization pool ($15,000,000) closed January 12, 2026. HCD stated unallocated funds roll to future rounds and an acquisition-rehab RFP would follow; no release found as of November 8, 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Measure W Home Together Fund 2025 New Construction RFP (revised November 17, 2025), Prevailing Wage section: projects not otherwise subject to federal or state prevailing wage must pay wage rates equivalent to California prevailing wage, with reporting and HCD monitoring. https://www.achcd.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Measure-W-Capital-RFP-v2-redline_111725.pdf

program_name: Measure A1 Rental Housing Development Fund (Base City Allocations, Regional Pools, Innovation and Opportunity Fund)
administering_agency: Alameda County Housing and Community Development Department (Measure A1 bond program)
typical_award_size: $580,000,000 general obligation bond approved by 73% of voters in Nov 2016, fully issued by 2021. Rental Development Fund of $425,000,000: a $225,000,000 Base City Allocation (every city and the unincorporated area by housing need) and a $200,000,000 Regional Pool awarded through competitive rounds in four regions, plus the $35,000,000 Innovation and Opportunity Fund ($25,000,000 Acquisition and Opportunity, $10,000,000 Innovation) and $21,500,000 moved from homeownership to the OakDays and Edes Avenue Homekey conversions. Status at June 30, 2026: 56 rental projects and 4,271 homes committed (1,360 for people exiting homelessness), $414,900,000 of A1 capital committed to rental development, 41 projects with 3,139 homes complete, 15 with 1,132 homes under construction or in predevelopment, $486,800,000 (84%) of the bond spent. Annual Report 4 showed only $30,200,000 of rental development funds uncommitted at mid-2022. Current openings are small Innovation and Opportunity pieces: the Tax-Defaulted Property Development Loan program (up to $3,000,000) and the Emerging Developers Predevelopment Loan program ($7,000,000, awards near $500,000, due Dec 2, 2024). A 2026 Program Income plan sets aside $3,100,000 for a senior ADU program.
per_unit_cap: Set by the 2017 Rental Housing Development policies and each city's base allocation; Regional Pool awards typically ran $5,000,000 to $15,000,000 per project. Each A1 dollar leveraged about $6 to $7 of other funds.
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 60% AMI with 20% of A1-assisted units for households at or below 20% AMI; 55-year County regulatory agreement; priority populations include seniors, veterans, people with disabilities, essential workers and people leaving homelessness or incarceration.
next_deadline: Base City and Regional Pool dollars are essentially committed; remaining A1 money is program income and Innovation and Opportunity funds offered through HCD's fall affordable housing RFP and over-the-counter predevelopment loans. Confirm balances with HCD before counting on A1; the County's 2025 Housing Plan is studying a successor revenue measure.
layering_notes: A1 was the backbone of East Bay gap financing from 2018 to 2024 and is now largely spent, which is why Measure W capital matters. Loans use the standard HCD terms (3% simple, 55 to 59 years, residual receipts). Many cities still hold uncommitted base allocation balances they control locally (Pass 3), and the County reporting site lists every project by city. Measure A1 requires state prevailing wage on all construction hours under the County labor compliance program (see prevailing_wage_basis). Figures from measurea1.acgov.org (opened) and Annual Report 4 (opened); the 2017 policies PDF on achcd.org is image-only and was not readable.
prevailing_wage_basis: Alameda County Measure A1 program site (Workforce and Accountability sections, read November 9, 2026): every hour of Measure A1 construction is paid at state prevailing wage under the County labor compliance program, and projects above County size thresholds build under a Project Labor Agreement with the Building Trades Council. https://measurea1.acgov.org/
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: A1 site matches the $580M bond, $225M Base City and $200M Regional Pool, $35M Innovation and Opportunity Fund, $21.5M Homekey transfer, 56 projects and 4,271 homes, $414.9M committed, 84% spent, 60% AMI with 20% at 20% AMI, 55-year term and $3.1M senior ADU set-aside. Prevailing wage basis added from the same page.

program_name: HOME Consortium and Urban County CDBG affordable housing development loans (annual HCD RFP)
administering_agency: Alameda County Housing and Community Development Department, HOME Consortium lead agency and Urban County CDBG administrator; CDBG 510-670-5971, CDBG@acgov.org
typical_award_size: HCD issues one competitive affordable housing development RFP each fall combining HOME (Consortium CHDO and Urban County shares), remaining Measure A1 and other local funds; applications are due about eight weeks after release with a mandatory bidders conference. HOME Consortium: Alameda, Fremont, Hayward, Livermore, Pleasanton, San Leandro, Union City and the Urban County (all cities except Oakland and Berkeley, which are their own participating jurisdictions); the City of Alameda's FY 2026-27 draft Action Plan reports the Consortium's 2025 HOME allocation as $1,475,257, a figure to confirm with HCD. Urban County CDBG covers the unincorporated area plus Albany, Dublin, Emeryville, Newark and Piedmont, which administer their own shares; the unincorporated CDBG RFP runs December or January with applications due March or April and contracts July 1. State ESG to the County for the CoC: $402,650 (2024). Past procurements: 2023 HOME Capital RFP, 2024 CDBG NOFA (due Jan 19, 2024).
per_unit_cap: HOME maximum per-unit subsidy limits (24 CFR 92.250); County loans sized to the gap.
affordability_requirement: HOME: households at or below 80% AMI at HOME rents for 55 years under County documents (59-year regulatory agreement standard, 55 allowed for tax credit projects); CDBG: low and moderate income benefit. 15% of Consortium HOME reserved for CHDOs.
next_deadline: Fall 2026 RFP date not posted as of Nov 6, 2026; HCD's funding opportunities page says the RFP is issued each fall. Unincorporated CDBG applications are due March or April 2027 for FY 2027-28.
layering_notes: Federal money is a small share of Alameda County's stack: the Consortium's HOME is a few million dollars a year spread across eight members, so the County's own awards are typically under $1,000,000 and ride on the same fall RFP as Measure A1 and local funds. Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units or 8 or more CDBG-assisted units; state prevailing wage turns on the local or state funds in the deal and the Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions (see prevailing_wage_basis). HCD also administers HOPWA housing for the Oakland area and runs AC Boost, Renew AC and the AC Housing Secure programs from the same department. The County's own FY 2026-27 Action Plan PDF (47MB Consolidated Plan link) was not opened; figures come from the HCD CDBG page, the funding opportunities page and the City of Alameda's draft plan.
prevailing_wage_basis: HOME: 24 CFR 92.354(a) requires Davis-Bacon wages on construction contracts for housing with 12 or more HOME-assisted units (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354). CDBG-assisted residential construction triggers Davis-Bacon at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds, federal wage rules do not apply and state prevailing wage depends on Labor Code 1720 project facts.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 8, 2026: CDBG page confirms Urban County structure and the unincorporated RFP timing (Dec or Jan release, due Mar or Apr, July 1 contracts); funding opportunities page confirms an annual fall affordable housing RFP with mandatory bidders conference and about eight weeks to apply. No fall 2026 development RFP posted yet. The $1,475,257 HOME figure is from the City of Alameda draft plan and was not re-checked. Prevailing wage true is conditional on the HOME 12-unit and CDBG 8-unit thresholds.

Amounts from the HCD 2024-2028 PLHA formula NOFA (opened this pass); County plan not found.
audit_note: PW pass Nov 9, 2026: true was set from public-funds logic only; PLHA formula guidelines and NOFA are silent on prevailing wage, so changed to unclear.

HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines and Formula Allocation NOFA contain no prevailing wage provision (only the separate non-entitlement competitive NOFA, section VI.C, says awards are subject to Labor Code 1720 unless a 1720(c) exception applies). https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf

program_name: Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds, County of Alameda conduit issuer
administering_agency: Alameda County Housing and Community Development Department (issuer staff) with the Board of Supervisors
typical_award_size: The County issues tax-exempt multifamily housing revenue bonds on request: example, up to $24,000,000 for SAHA's 51-unit 3268 San Pablo Apartments in Oakland (inducement Oct 9, 2018, bond resolution April 23, 2019, CDLAC Resolution 19-011). Issuer fees per that regulatory agreement: an issuance fee at closing and an annual fee of the greater of 0.125% of outstanding principal or $7,500 for the qualified project period. No 2025 or 2026 County bond issuances were located; CMFA issued for Eden Housing in Dublin, RCD in Berkeley and the Housing Authority of the City of Alameda in that period.
affordability_requirement: CDLAC and Section 142(d) minimums (20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI) under a County regulatory agreement; County-financed projects typically carry deeper restrictions.
next_deadline: Tied to CDLAC rounds: TEFRA hearing and inducement resolution by the Board before the CDLAC application, then a bond resolution before closing. Ask HCD whether it will issue; most recent East Bay deals used CMFA or CSCDA.
layering_notes: The County will act as issuer for projects it also funds, which keeps monitoring under one regulatory agreement, but it is not an active conduit shop. Bonds alone do not trigger state prevailing wage; County A1, Measure W or HOME loans in the deal do. Terms read from the April 23, 2019 Board letter and regulatory agreement (opened); confirm current fees with HCD.
prevailing_wage_basis: DIR public works coverage determinations PW 2006-001 (Horizons at Indio, March 12, 2007) and PW 2006-018 (Crossings at Madera), following PW 2004-016 (Rancho Santa Fe Village): publicly offered conduit multifamily housing revenue bonds are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) because proceeds and repayments never enter the issuer's coffers, and are not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4); even if they were, the affordable housing loan exemption (now 1720(c)(5)(E), 40% of units at or below 80% AMI for 20 years) would apply. Current 1720 text contains no conduit bond trigger. Applies to the County bond issuance only; any County A1, Measure W, HOME or other loans in the same deal are analyzed separately.
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for bond issuance alone based on DIR coverage determinations on point (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf, https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-018.pdf). Privately placed bond structures were not separately confirmed; layered public loans can still trigger coverage.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Housing Authority of the County of Alameda (HACA)
administering_agency: Housing Authority of the County of Alameda, 22941 Atherton Street, Hayward, 510-538-8876; developer verifications through Jennifer Cado
typical_award_size: HACA administers 7,145 vouchers (6,973 leased at July 1, 2026): 6,361 Housing Choice, 425 VASH, 289 Mainstream, 15 EHV. HACA's Administrative Plan (Chapter 17) allows project-basing up to 30% of voucher budget authority, allocated over a multi-year period through RFPs. The November 2021 RFP offered up to 160 PBVs for new construction serving seniors, homeless families and veterans and for existing Homekey projects in Albany, Hayward, Newark and the unincorporated area; selected projects were Downtown Hayward Senior, Mission Paradise (Hayward), Albany Family Apartments, Newark Towne Place Suites, Cherryland Place and Timber Senior Housing (Newark). PBV unit totals are not published.
per_unit_cap: HUD PBV caps (20% of authorized units plus 10% for homeless, veteran, supportive services and low-poverty units); rents at the lower of reasonable rent or 110% of FMR with HACA payment standards and utility allowances.
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 50% AMI at admission (75% at or below 30% AMI); HAP contracts up to 20 years with extension; HACA referral and waitlist rules per the Administrative Plan.
next_deadline: No PBV RFP open as of Nov 2026; the last was Nov 18 to Dec 3, 2021. HACA jurisdiction: Albany, Dublin, Emeryville, Fremont, Hayward, Newark, Pleasanton, San Leandro, Union City and all unincorporated areas; Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda and Livermore have their own housing authorities (Pass 3). HACA will issue verification letters for CTCAC, CDLAC and CalHFA applications on request.
layering_notes: HACA PBVs are the operating subsidy for County-funded PSH outside Oakland and Berkeley; Measure W's capitalized operating subsidy reserve is the fallback when PBVs are unavailable. A HAP contract is not a prevailing wage trigger, but Davis-Bacon applies to PBV new construction or rehab of nine or more contract units. HACA is not a Moving to Work agency. Sources opened: HACA developers page, program data at-a-glance, jurisdiction page and the County HCD bulletin announcing the 2021 RFP.
prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (HUD PBV development requirements, labor standards): for development activity (new construction or rehabilitation) involving nine or more PBV contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and the PHA monitors compliance; existing-housing PBV contracts with no development activity do not trigger it. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: HACA Developers page confirms the 30% budget authority cap, Chapter 17 selection, the November 2021 RFP and the six selected projects; At-a-Glance page confirms 7,145 allocated and 6,973 leased vouchers as of July 1, 2026 (6,361 HCV, 425 VASH, 289 Mainstream, 15 EHV). No new PBV RFP posted.

program_name: Unincorporated inclusionary zoning and ministerial approval ordinances (in development) and state density bonus
administering_agency: Alameda County Community Development Agency, Planning Department (unincorporated area)
typical_award_size: No county inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee or affordable housing impact fee exists today. The Planning Department received $280,000 and hired Street Level Advisors to draft an Inclusionary Zoning Ordinance and a Ministerial Approval Ordinance to meet MTC's Transit-Oriented Communities policy (Bay Fair and Castro Valley BART areas) and Housing Element Program 6.J; draft ordinances for public comment early 2027, adoption recommendations spring 2027, completion by July 1, 2027. Working concepts: rental projects averaging 80% AMI or less (units 30% to 120% AMI), ownership averaging 120% AMI or less, ministerial approval for projects of 11 or more units meeting the set-aside, alternatives of in-lieu fee, off-site units or land dedication. Density bonus follows Government Code 65915 (state law), and the County code already allows ministerial approval for ADUs under 800 square feet.
affordability_requirement: Pending; MTC TOC minimums expected (about 10% to 20% affordable depending on tier). State density bonus units: 55 years for rental.
next_deadline: Not yet adopted. Watch the Unincorporated Services Committee and Planning Commission in 2026 and 2027; draft financial feasibility analysis dated July 2026 is posted on the policies page. State density bonus is available now by right.
layering_notes: Alameda County unincorporated areas (Ashland, Cherryland, San Lorenzo, Castro Valley, Fairview, Sunol) have no local inclusionary production or fee revenue, so county-controlled affordable housing there depends on A1, Measure W and HACA. Expect an inclusionary requirement on market-rate projects entitled after mid-2027. Density bonus alone does not trigger prevailing wage. Classified as regulatory requirement because the county-specific content is a pending inclusionary ordinance (a set-aside obligation, not a subsidy); the state density bonus portion is covered by Government Code 65915 and is available now. Sources opened: County affordable housing production policies page (re-read November 8, 2026) and the Jan 26, 2026 staff report.
audit_note: Reclassified from density bonus to regulatory requirement. Policies page re-read November 8, 2026: ordinance not adopted; draft ordinances early 2027, recommendations spring 2027, project completion July 2027; ownership units may range up to 150% AMI.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Development fee waiver for affordable housing (no countywide program)
administering_agency: Alameda County Community Development Agency
typical_award_size: None adopted. The County's 2025 Housing Plan lists an affordable housing impact fee on commercial development as a future unincorporated revenue option and does not describe any fee waiver or deferral program.
affordability_requirement: Not applicable.
next_deadline: Not applicable. Budget full County and special district fees in unincorporated deals; permit fees are an eligible use of County loans.
layering_notes: Negative finding. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) counts waived fees as public funds for prevailing wage purposes. Housing Plan (10-Year Housing Strategy 2025-2035, approved July 2025) opened.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program exists, so nothing here pays for construction; Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) applies only to construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. Any fee waiver or deferral granted case by case would be public funds under 1720(b)(4) and is tested on the project.

program_name: Welfare Exemption (property tax), Alameda County Assessor
administering_agency: Alameda County Assessor, Phong La, 1221 Oak Street, Room 145, Oakland; Other Exemptions Unit 510-272-6587, exemptions@acgov.org
typical_award_size: Full or partial exemption of property tax on units occupied by households at or below 80% AMI under Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g); worth roughly 1.1% to 1.4% of assessed value a year depending on the tax rate area (Alameda County has high voter-approved debt rates). The Assessor posts the full BOE-267 series (267, 267-L, L1, L2, L3, L4, H, R and income worksheets) and asks claimants to contact the exemptions unit before filing with the parcel number.
per_unit_cap: Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer per fiscal year (single or multiple properties), and only where the exemption rests solely on the 90 percent lower income occupancy test for a property not owned by a limited partnership. Projects with tax-exempt bonds, government loans or grants (214(g)(1)(A)) or low-income housing tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are outside the cap; LP-owned projects with a nonprofit managing general partner must have tax credits or government financing to qualify (BOE Publication 149). Not a statewide cap.
affordability_requirement: Nonprofit or LP with eligible nonprofit managing general partner holding a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (and Supplemental Clearance Certificate for LP low-income housing); units restricted by recorded regulatory agreement or occupied by households at or below 80% AMI; BOE-267 first filing and annual supplemental affidavits by Feb 15 (late claims receive a reduced exemption under Rev. and Tax. Code 270).
next_deadline: 2027-02-15 (annual claim deadline for the 2027-28 roll). File the first claim on acquisition so the construction period is covered.
layering_notes: Standard in every tax credit operating budget; underwrite only the restricted units and confirm the managing GP's OCC and SCC before closing. The Assessor's exemptions page (opened) gives the unit contact and forms but no local deadline text; the BOE's Alameda income limit letter governs tenant qualification.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 9, 2026: Assessor exemptions page lists the Welfare Exemption (R&T 214) and the BOE-267, 267-L, L1 and L2 forms; R&T 214(g) text confirms the lower income (80% AMI) test. Fix Nov 9, 2026: the $20,000,000 cap in 214(g)(1)(C) applies only to claims resting solely on the 90 percent occupancy test for property not owned by an LP with a nonprofit managing general partner; the earlier LP wording was wrong. prevailing_wage_trigger false has no cited rule (a tax exemption is not a construction payment), noted only.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) and (b)(4) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works requires construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, including fees, loans or other obligations normally required in executing the construction contract that are reduced or waived. The welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) reduces property tax on the completed property; it pays no construction cost, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage.

program_name: Oakland-Berkeley-Alameda County Continuum of Care (CA-502) and HHAP
administering_agency: Alameda County Health, Housing and Homelessness Services (CoC lead and HHAP administrator for the County and CoC allocations); City of Oakland administers its own HHAP
typical_award_size: HHAP by round, County of Alameda: R1 $8,700,000, R2 $4,000,000, R3 $11,200,000, R4 $12,100,000, R5 $13,463,754, R6 $10,783,302. CoC: R1 $9,400,000, R2 $4,500,000, R3 $12,000,000, R4 $12,900,000, R5 $14,033,347, R6 $11,516,752. City of Oakland: R5 $28,446,566, R6 about $23,000,000; regional R6 total $45,300,000 (awarded March 2, 2026). State accountability site: $210,100,000 HHAP rounds 1 to 5 in the Alameda area, $102,500,000 directly to the County ($78,100,000 obligated, $60,500,000 spent by mid-2025); Encampment Resolution Funding $30,600,000 in the area. HUD CoC program FY 2024 awards to CA-502: $16,901,825 including Shelter Plus Care TRA $9,129,290, Housing Fast Support Network $2,619,550, YHDP $1,934,338 and Linkages $1,734,446. State ESG CoC share $402,650 (2024). 2024 PIT: 9,450 people, 6,343 unsheltered, 9,963 year-round beds. HHAP uses in the County: Coordinated Entry access points, street health and outreach, HMIS, Emerging Leaders, regional interim housing (safe parking, shelters, navigation centers) and local match for Medi-Cal Housing Community Supports.
affordability_requirement: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness per HUD and state definitions; CoC permanent housing through Coordinated Entry; HHAP-6 must obligate 75% and spend 50% by June 30, 2027, and the County needs a compliant housing element for the second half of its Round 6 award.
next_deadline: HHAP-6 regional application was due Aug 29, 2025 and awarded March 2026; HHAP-7 is available to HHAP-6 grantees. The CoC's HUD NOFO competition runs each summer through EveryOne Home; letters of interest are collected by the County. Home Together 2030 (summer 2026) sets system priorities.
layering_notes: HHAP here pays for coordinated entry, outreach, interim housing and services rather than capital; Measure W now dwarfs it and is the County's capital and operating subsidy source for PSH. Oakland and Berkeley projects should look to those cities' HHAP and CoC shares (Pass 3). CoC permanent housing dollars are mostly Shelter Plus Care tenant-based assistance. Figures from the July 17, 2025 County and Oakland HHAP-6 presentation (opened), HCD HHAP allocation lists, the HUD FY 2025 CoC award report and accountability.ca.gov.
prevailing_wage_basis: HUD CoC: 24 CFR 578.99(h) states the Davis-Bacon Act does not apply to the CoC program (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/578.99). HHAP guidance does not state a prevailing wage rule; state prevailing wage would apply to an HHAP- or CoC-funded construction or rehab project only under Labor Code 1720 depending on project facts and 1720(c) exemptions. Most local HHAP spending here is services, outreach and interim housing operations.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 8, 2026: HHAP Rounds 1 to 6 County and CoC allocations, uses, and the Aug 29, 2025 HHAP-6 deadline match the July 17, 2025 presentation. Prevailing wage changed from true to unclear because the CoC rule excludes Davis-Bacon and no HHAP rule imposes prevailing wage. March 2, 2026 award date and HUD CoC FY 2024 figures were not re-checked in this pass.

program_name: Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA) housing interventions, Alameda County Behavioral Health Department
administering_agency: Alameda County Behavioral Health Department (ACBHD), Alameda County Health, with Housing and Homelessness Services for the flexible housing subsidy pool
typical_award_size: Integrated Plan FY 2026-29 approved by the Board of Supervisors June 16, 2026 (public hearing April 20, 2026). BHSA budget authority about $166,188,844 a year; Housing Interventions component $37,306,397 (FY 2026-27), $41,735,347 (FY 2027-28), $44,221,971 (FY 2028-29); 52% dedicated to chronically homeless people; outreach and engagement 5% to 6%. Uses: rental subsidies, operating subsidies for existing and new PSH units (about 990 people a year), flexible housing subsidy pool, landlord mitigation, tenancy sustaining services. Capital development share: 0% in all three years; the plan states the County will consider capital development projects as needed once the BHSA transition is complete.
per_unit_cap: None; no capital program planned. Statute would allow up to 25% of the housing component for capital.
affordability_requirement: Adults, older adults, youth and families with serious mental illness or substance use disorder who are chronically homeless, homeless or at risk; Housing First; ACBHD eligibility and Coordinated Entry referral for PSH units.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. BHSA Integrated Plan FY 2026-29 took effect with the BHSA transition and is updated through Annual Updates; there is no capital NOFA (the plan answers No to using Housing Interventions for capital development). Ask ACBHD and H&H about operating subsidy and Flexible Housing Subsidy Pool commitments for PSH units.
layering_notes: Unlike Orange and Contra Costa, Alameda chose not to put BHSA money into capital, so BHSA is an operating and services partner only: pair a BHSA operating subsidy or flex pool commitment with Measure W capital and HACA or city PBVs. State funds would trigger prevailing wage if capital were ever offered. Figures from the June 16, 2026 Board item (304 pages, opened) and the approved plan PDF and executive summary on acbhsa.org.
cycle_notes: Not a competitive application program. Funds flow through the three-year Integrated Plan (Board approved June 16, 2026; submitted to DHCS for the July 2026 start) with Annual Updates and Intermittent Updates. Housing Interventions fund rental subsidies, PSH operating subsidies, the Flexible Housing Subsidy Pool and tenancy services; capital development share is 0% in all three years.
prevailing_wage_basis: No prevailing wage rule found in the FY 2026-29 Integrated Plan (Board item BHCS_405776, June 16, 2026). The plan funds no capital development, so no construction contract is financed; earlier value of true was inferred from state funding and had no cited rule. https://www.alamedacountyca.gov/board/bos_calendar/documents/DocsAgendaReg_06_16_26/HEALTH%20CARE%20SERVICES/Regular%20Calendar/BHCS_405776.pdf
audit_note: prevailing_wage_trigger reset from true to unclear in Tier 2 audit because no cited rule supported true and the program funds no capital.

program_name: County boomerang funds for housing and homelessness (former redevelopment residual property tax)
administering_agency: Alameda County Board of Supervisors through Housing and Community Development and Health, Housing and Homelessness Services
typical_award_size: 2017 policy: 20% of the prior year's boomerang receipts, $5,000,000 minimum and $7,500,000 maximum a year, as a five-year commitment starting FY 2016-17 ($5,000,000 in FY 2016-17 and FY 2017-18) for housing resource centers and coordinated entry ($2,000,000 a year), anti-displacement crisis services ($3,500,000 initial) and other Home Together system costs; a one-time $9,800,000 boomerang allocation seeded Measure A1 implementation.
