prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or Labor Code 1720 provision; the HCD PLHA FAQ (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/cycle-2-nofa-faq.pdf) says only that HCD programs require compliance with applicable law including prevailing wages unless the project meets a Labor Code 1720(c) exception as determined by DIR. PLHA loans and grants are public funds under 1720(b)(1) and (b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), but 1720(c)(5)(E) (below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI), 1720(c)(5)(C) (mortgage, down payment or single-family rehab aid to a household) and 1720(c)(3) de minimis can apply. Davis-Bacon applies only if HOME (12+ HOME units, 24 CFR 92.354) or CDBG (8+ units, 24 CFR 570.603) is layered. The County first PLHA plan funded renovations at the County-owned Live Oak Apartments; renovation of a publicly owned building paid with public funds is public works under 1720(a)(1), and the 1720(c)(5) exemptions cover only privately owned residential projects. The 2024 competitive application funds rental assistance and services, which involve no construction.

program_name: Density bonus (Chapter 20.234, Inland Zoning Code) after repeal of the inclusionary ordinance; 2027-2035 Housing Element
administering_agency: Mendocino County Planning and Building Services (Julia Krog, Director, (707) 234-6650)
typical_award_size: Ordinance 4538 (September 10, 2024) rewrote the Inland Zoning Code: Chapter 20.234 grants density bonuses, incentives and concessions exactly as provided in Government Code 65915-65918 in all residential zones, requires a recorded density bonus agreement, and repealed the former Chapter 20.238 inclusionary housing ordinance so the County now defers entirely to state law (2025 Housing Element APR, Action 3.1d). The one large subdivision, Bella Vista near Ukiah (166 lots, modified February 3, 2026), keeps 36 moderate-income for-sale units and 42 senior lots under a development agreement and inclusionary housing plan approved before the repeal. The County hired PlaceWorks ($334,925, March 24, 2026) to prepare the 2027-2035 Housing Element (regional RHNA 6,456 units, adoption due August 2027) and the Ukiah Valley Area Plan mixed-use rezone of 192 parcels is expected in 2026.
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 thresholds with recorded restrictions; equity-sharing payments on for-sale bonus units go to the County Affordable Housing Trust Fund.
next_deadline: Requested with the land use application; expect new Housing Element programs and possible incentive changes in 2027.
layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on September 10, 2024, has no housing trust fund money, no NOFA and no impact fee waiver; County capital help has come from state pass-through grants (CDBG-DR, Homekey) and small HOME program income balances. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. With the inclusionary ordinance gone there is no local affordability requirement or in-lieu fee outside the coastal zone; the County's land use posture is permissive but offers no local financial incentive. Source is the County's clean Inland Zoning Code PDF (Chapter 20.234); repeal confirmed in the 2025 Housing Element APR.
eligible_project_detail: multifamily and mixed-income housing in residential and mixed-use zones
motel conversions (Golden Rule approved with a water concession)
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

typical_award_size: Integrated Plan approved July 7, 2026: rental subsidies for up to 150 people a year (80 permanent, 90 interim; 80 units), operating subsidies for about 350 people (80 units), participant assistance and outreach for 50; no capital development projects; FSP exemptions requested as a county under 200,000 population; housing delivered through contracts such as Redwood Community Services Haven House ($400,000 FY 2026-27), Harmony House sober living interim housing ($300,000) and Mendocino Coast Hospitality Center shelter services, alongside Behavioral Health Bridge Housing and Transitional Rent. Measure B (2017 Mental Health Treatment Act sales tax) funds facilities; $7 million was used for the jail behavioral health unit in 2024.
affordability_requirement: BHSA eligible adults and youth with serious mental illness or substance use disorder; Medi-Cal eligible.
next_deadline: Behavioral Health issued an RFP for BHSA housing service providers in 2026; contact the department about subsidy agreements for new PSH units.
layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. BHSA will not fund capital in Mendocino; its value is a project-based rental or operating subsidy on a small number of PSH units. Source is the 2026-2029 Integrated Plan PDF (Legistar attachment to the July 7, 2026 item). funding_type is grant because the Integrated Plan funds rental subsidies (up to 150 people a year, 80 permanent and 90 interim) and operating subsidies for housing; the plan answers No to capital development projects.
eligible_project_detail: project-based and tenant-based rental subsidies (80 units)
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) covers only construction, alteration, demolition, installation or repair paid for with public funds. The BHSA 2026-2029 Integrated Plan (https://mendocino.legistar1.com/mendocino/attachments/16a82dac-7041-49d0-a22d-f3f414222b80.pdf) answers No to using BHSA Housing Interventions for capital development projects and funds rental subsidies, operating subsidies and master-leased units, which pay no construction cost. The BHSA statute section read (W&I Code 5830, https://california.public.law/codes/welfare_and_institutions_code_section_5830) has no prevailing wage provision.
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: false kept for housing interventions. The plan separately lists a County-owned BHRS Wellness Center remodel as a capital facilities project; that is not housing but would be public works.

affordability_requirement: PBV households at or below 50% AMI (75% extremely low income); PSH units filled through Coordinated Entry.
next_deadline: No open RFP as of November 8, 2026 (CDC Project Bids and Awards: none at this time); a LIHTC or HOME project competitively selected within the prior three years can request PBVs without a new competition.

audit_note: Tier 4 spot check 2026-11-08: Board item 25-1070 (Resolutions 25-200 to 25-204, adopted December 16, 2025) matches the parcel list; only 120 W. Fir St. is non-exempt surplus. Affordability note: 25% lower income applies to housing sponsors seeking SLA priority (Gov. Code 54222.5); if no agreement is reached and 10+ units are built, Gov. Code 54233 requires at least 15% lower income for 55 years rental or 45 years ownership.

program_name: Welfare exemption from property tax for nonprofit-owned affordable housing, Mendocino County Assessor
administering_agency: Mendocino County Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder (501 Low Gap Road, Ukiah)
typical_award_size: Standard state welfare exemption for low-income housing owned by nonprofits or limited partnerships with a nonprofit managing general partner holding a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate; the Assessor's services page lists review and application of exemptions among its functions.
affordability_requirement: Units restricted to lower income households by a recorded regulatory agreement or deed restriction, with tax savings used to maintain affordability or reduce rents; property must have state or federal LIHTC or government financing, or (nonprofit-owned, BOE-267-L) 90% or more qualified low-income tenants (BOE Publication 149). Lower income means up to 80% AMI under state law; exemption applies to qualifying units.
next_deadline: File BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual) with the BOE-267-L or BOE-267-L1 supplemental affidavit with the Assessor by 5:00 p.m. February 16, 2027 for the 2027-28 roll (the February 15 deadline falls on Presidents Day, so it moves to the next business day per BOE Publication 149).
layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on September 10, 2024, has no housing trust fund money, no NOFA and no impact fee waiver; County capital help has come from state pass-through grants (CDBG-DR, Homekey) and small HOME program income balances. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. Confirmation needed: the Assessor's page does not publish welfare exemption instructions or a contact; the exemption itself is state law.
cycle_notes: Annual claim filing, not a NOFA: claims are due each year on or before February 15 for full exemption (next business day if a weekend or holiday); late claims may receive partial exemption. The managing general partner needs a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate and, for limited partnerships, a Supplemental Clearance Certificate.
eligible_project_detail: LIHTC rental housing with nonprofit managing general partner
audit_note: The Assessor page opened via WebFetch (curl gets an Akamai 403); it lists review and application of exemptions but no welfare exemption instructions. Filing rules verified on BOE Publication 149 (December 2018). The 80% AMI definition is from Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g), which returned 403 and was not re-read.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) and (b)(4) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works requires construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, including fees, loans or other obligations normally required in executing the construction contract that are reduced or waived. The welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) reduces property tax on the completed property; it pays no construction cost, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage.

audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: HCD 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA tables re-read; Merced County ($371,543 CY 2024, $407,167 CY 2025, $2,322,144 estimated 2024-2028) and City of Merced figures match. Affordability corrected from 80% AMI to the guideline limits (moderate up to 120% AMI, 60% AMI priority, 55-year deferred loan for rentals). The County five-year plan was not found (countyofmerced.com 403; the County homebuyer guidelines found are CalHome, CDBG and HOME funded), so eligible activities remain unconfirmed.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or Labor Code 1720 provision; the HCD PLHA FAQ (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/cycle-2-nofa-faq.pdf) says only that HCD programs require compliance with applicable law including prevailing wages unless the project meets a Labor Code 1720(c) exception as determined by DIR. PLHA loans and grants are public funds under 1720(b)(1) and (b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), but 1720(c)(5)(E) (below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI), 1720(c)(5)(C) (mortgage, down payment or single-family rehab aid to a household) and 1720(c)(3) de minimis can apply. Davis-Bacon applies only if HOME (12+ HOME units, 24 CFR 92.354) or CDBG (8+ units, 24 CFR 570.603) is layered. The County PLHA plan and uses were not found, so whether any PLHA dollars fund construction is unknown.

prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Chapter 18.40), in-lieu fees and the 2026 fee-based restructuring proposal
administering_agency: Monterey County Housing and Community Development Department; Housing Advisory Committee
typical_award_size: Current ordinance (first adopted 1980, revised 2003): 20% of units in residential projects affordable, analyzed by Keyser Marston as 6% very low, 6% low and 8% moderate income plus a 5% Workforce I component, with in-lieu fees for fractional units and small projects; in-lieu fees collected at building permit 2021-2025 are tabulated in the September 2026 workshop packet. The 2026 KMA In-Lieu Fee Analysis found maximum supportable fees of $73.90 to $305.60 per square foot of saleable area by product type. Staff recommended (Housing Advisory Committee workshops September 2 and 11, 2026) converting to an entirely fee-based program for projects under 250 units, charging 33 to 35 percent of the maximum fee on habitable square footage above the first 1,500 square feet, exempting all multifamily (duplex to fourplex and ADUs under 1,200 square feet), encouraging land donation for 20% affordable units on projects of 250 or more units, indexing the fee annually and allowing fee revenue to be spent countywide.
affordability_requirement: Very low (50% AMI), low (80% AMI), moderate (120% AMI) and Workforce I (to 150% AMI) for-sale and rental units with long-term resale and rent restrictions; inclusionary units are calculated on base plus density bonus units.
next_deadline: Board action on the restructured ordinance and new fee schedule expected late 2026 or 2027 after Housing Advisory Committee recommendations; LeSar and KMA remain under contract (Amendment 10, April 2026) to complete the fee studies. Until adoption the 2003 ordinance and existing in-lieu fees apply.

program_name: Welfare exemption from property tax for nonprofit-owned affordable housing

audit_note: Old Assessor URL /1876/Assessor now redirects to the Clerk of the Board; current page is /163/Assessor (phone 530-265-1232). layering_notes: San Luis Obispo County's Department of Social Services Homeless Services Division (HSD, Devin Drake, Director; George Solis, Principal Administrative Manager; HSDgrants@co.slo.ca.us) runs one combined annual Action Plan NOFA each fall for CDBG, HOME, ESG, HHAP, PLHA, Title 29 and County General Fund Support on the Neighborly portal, and is the Continuum of Care collaborative applicant and administrative entity (CA-614). The Urban County covers the unincorporated area plus Arroyo Grande, Atascadero, Morro Bay, Paso Robles, Pismo Beach and San Luis Obispo (Grover Beach is outside). The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on June 7, 2022 and replaced it in October 2025 with a voluntary Regional Housing Incentive Program and Regional Housing Fund. slocounty.ca.gov opens directly but rate-limits bursts (HTTP 429); Legistar web API is not enabled for the County. Scoring (100 points) weights scope and expertise (40), funding readiness (15), cost effectiveness and unit count (20), entitlement readiness (10), site standards, vulnerable population targeting and alignment with the Countywide Plan to Address Homelessness (15). HOME awards are small ($400,000 to $900,000) and are typically layered with Title 29, PLHA, SB 1090 and Housing Trust Fund loans under TCAC. Apply through Neighborly; attend the October information session.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: San Luis Obispo County Housing Trust Fund revolving loans (private CDFI)

program_name: SHRA Multifamily Lending Program (City of Sacramento gap financing: HOME, Housing Trust Fund, Mixed Income Housing fund, PLHA)
administering_agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (SHRA) on behalf of the City of Sacramento and the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
typical_award_size: Gap loans sized to the gap after all other sources, no stated per-project cap. City funds posted June 1, 2026: HOME $5,000,000, Housing Trust Fund/Workforce Housing $1,000,000, Mixed Income Housing/Workforce Housing $2,500,000, PLHA $680,000 (about $9.2M). Applicants request gap funds without naming a source. January 2026 City pre-applications: Hotel Berry (Jamboree, preservation, $5.1M) invited; Florin Family Apartments (CCH, $5.1M) and Q Street Apartments (Community HousingWorks, $2.0M) invited; requests of $6.5M to $12M (Mercy 2601 5th Street, Danco 6779 Q Street, TWG 1220 H Street, Dos Rios) declined for insufficient funds. Projects must have 12 or more units.
per_unit_cap: No published cap; subsidy per restricted unit cannot exceed HUD Section 234 limits for the Sacramento area; HOME units capped by 24 CFR 92.250. Annual SHRA monitoring fee charged per assisted unit.
affordability_requirement: 55-year regulatory agreement (HOME units per federal rules). SHRA minimum: at least 15% of units at or below 50% AMI and 5% at or below 30% AMI based on feasibility; regulated share at least proportional to SHRA share of total development cost; restricted rents at least 10% below market. Housing Trust Fund and Mixed Income fund money is limited to workforce households (up to 80% AMI, jobs-housing nexus). Priorities: preservation at risk, then new construction and nonresidential conversion (PSH and homeless housing, veterans, workforce 30% to 60% AMI, other), then rehab of regulated stock, then market-rate to affordable conversion.
next_deadline: 2027 SHRA Multi-Family Loan and Mortgage Revenue Bond schedule (proposed): Pre-application January 4, 2027, full application March 1, 2027, environmental clearance May 3, 2027, SHRC June 23, 2027, Board/Council June 29, 2027; second round pre-application July 1, 2027, full application September 1, 2027, environmental clearance November 16, 2027, SHRC January 19, 2028, Board/Council January 25, 2028. 2027 schedule is Exhibit B to the 2027 SHRA budget item (SHRC heard Nov 4, 2026; County Board agenda Nov 3, 2026; City Council and Housing Authority hearing Nov 10, 2026); final adoption not yet confirmed. As of 2026-11-10 the SHRA multifamily page still says SHRA is not accepting pre-applications and links only the 2026 schedule and the June 1, 2026 funds-available notice; no 2027 funds-available notice or NOFA is posted. Phone (916) 440-1393.
layering_notes: This is the City-side pool parallel to the County SHRA record (Pass 2); a project uses one or the other based on location, both run on the same schedule and policies (2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies, amended July 29, 2026). Terms: up to 3% simple interest or the AFR, term up to 40 years from conversion or 55 years when senior public lenders require, 1.10x to 1.20x combined DSCR, payments deferred during construction and deferred developer fee repayment, residual receipts allowed; nonprofit managing general partner required; developer fee limited to $25,000/$15,000/$12,000 per unit tiers for non-tax-credit deals and deferred maximum fee for LIHTC deals. Federal HOME (12 or more units) and CDBG (8 or more units) trigger Davis-Bacon; SHRA treats state prevailing wage as applying unless the below-market loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years) fits. Stack with the City Zero-Dollar Rate impact fee reduction, Housing Impact Fee exemption at 40 du/acre, SacSewer fee waivers (County record) and Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento bonds. SHRA does not expect a project-based voucher RFP in 2026. SB 802 moves SHRA into the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency by Jan 1, 2028, so confirm the lender entity on 2027 and later commitments.
cycle_notes: Two rounds a year aligned to CTCAC 9% and CDLAC rounds; pre-applications through Builder's Patch, then invited full applications; a separate funds-available notice lists City and County sources. 2026 rounds: pre-applications Jan 2 and July 1, 2026; full applications March 2 and Sept 1, 2026; Council approvals June 16, 2026 and Jan 19, 2027 (SHRC Jan 13, 2027). The Nov 4, 2026 SHRC packet also lists 2027 unfunded pipeline projects (for example 1220 H Street, Danco, $15.7M request; 16th and O, Eden Housing, $5.0M), and SHRC approved a $2M conditional loan commitment for Q Street Apartments on Nov 4, 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).
audit_note: Nov 10, 2026: 2027 application schedule found as Exhibit B to the 2027 SHRA budget (SHRC Nov 4, 2026 packet; City Council hearing Nov 10, 2026); not yet posted on shra.org and no 2027 funds-available notice. Recheck the multifamily page in December 2026 for the funds notice.

program_name: City of Sacramento Housing Trust Fund (commercial linkage fee, City Code Chapter 18.56 Article IV)
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee assessment); SHRA (fund administration and lending)
typical_award_size: Fee source for SHRA City gap loans. Nonresidential rates effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: office $3.35, hotel $3.19, commercial $2.69, manufacturing $2.09, warehouse $0.92 per square foot, a 0.49% San Francisco construction cost index adjustment from the FY 2025-26 rates ($3.33, $3.18, $2.68, $2.08, $0.91). Table H in the FY27 notice sets use-specific rates (for example major medical facility $5.22, laboratory $2.84, K-12 and college $2.79). The FY27 notice is attached to the City Fees and Charges database entry (fee ID 3798); the City Housing Trust Fund page still links the FY 2025-26 notice as of 2026-11-10. 2024 fund: $411,805 fees collected, $140,000 spent, $4.85M ending balance of which $807,861 uncommitted; $1.0M posted as available June 1, 2026.
per_unit_cap: None published; SHRA policies apply (HUD Section 234 limit per restricted unit).
affordability_requirement: Fund is restricted to housing for workforce households up to 80% AMI (very low and low income wage earners) under the 1989 jobs-housing nexus; 55-year SHRA regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Deployed through the SHRA two-round schedule. Proposed 2027 SHRA schedule: pre-applications January 4, 2027 and July 1, 2027; full applications March 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027. Fee is paid at building permit on nonresidential projects; contact Ryan Dodge, (916) 808-8044, rdodge@cityofsacramento.org for fee questions.
layering_notes: Adopted 1989 (Chapter 17.708), moved into the Development Impact Fee chapter 18.56 on Feb 14, 2017; Council raised the fee 81.3% in 2004 (phased) and allows changes by resolution. Small and lumpy: about $0.4M to $0.6M a year in fees, so it is the smallest of the four City pools and is usually blended into a single SHRA loan with HOME and Mixed Income money. Parallel County Housing Trust Fund covers the unincorporated area (County rates $3.26 office to $1.08 warehouse since March 28, 2025). Annual report posted each May by SHRA.
cycle_notes: Fee rates reset every July 1 by the San Francisco CCI (March to March). Fund money is lent through SHRA Multifamily Lending rounds; 2027 schedule is Exhibit B to the 2027 SHRA budget item (SHRC heard Nov 4, 2026; County Board agenda Nov 3, 2026; City Council and Housing Authority hearing Nov 10, 2026); final adoption not yet confirmed. No 2027 funds-available notice posted on shra.org as of 2026-11-10.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Housing Trust Fund loans through SHRA are local fee money with no federal Davis-Bacon trigger; SHRA 2026 Multifamily Lending Policies, City (https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-City-final.pdf), Section 6.1 restates state law and the 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
audit_note: Nov 10, 2026: FY 2026-27 Housing Trust Fund notice found (City Fees and Charges database attachment) and rates updated; SHRA 2027 application schedule found in the Nov 4, 2026 SHRC packet.

program_name: Mixed Income Housing Ordinance and Housing Impact Fee (City Code Chapter 17.712)
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee); SHRA (Mixed Income Housing fund and 100-acre housing strategies)
typical_award_size: Requirement and fee, not a subsidy. Housing Impact Fee effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: $3.58 per square foot for single-unit, duplex and multi-unit dwellings below 20 and 40 dwelling units per net acre respectively; $0.00 for single-unit or duplex at 20 du/acre or more, multi-unit at 40 du/acre or more, and nonresidential-to-residential conversions; $1.55 per square foot in the Housing Incentive Zone. Fee revenue (about $1.7M in 2024, $4.2M lent to projects that year) goes to the SHRA-administered Mixed Income Housing fund; $2.5M posted available June 1, 2026. Projects over 100 gross acres must adopt a Council-approved mixed income housing strategy.
affordability_requirement: Exempt from the fee: developments with 10% regulated low-income units (80% AMI), room additions, second units, owner-builder single homes, mobilehome parks, projects with pre-ordinance development agreements or pre-November 2015 entitlements. No mandatory inclusionary requirement citywide.
next_deadline: Fee assessed at building permit, adjusted every July 1. The Housing Element Program H1 review ended Dec 9, 2025 when Council voted to make no changes, so the current structure holds through at least 2027. Contact Greta Soos, (916) 808-2027.
layering_notes: Most 4% and 9% multifamily deals in Sacramento pay nothing: at 40 du/acre or more the rate is $0, and any project with 10% low-income units is exempt, so the fee mainly hits single-family subdivisions and low-density apartments. The fund it feeds is the largest City gap pool after HOME ($2.5M June 2026). Compare the County Affordable Housing Ordinance ($3.91 per square foot with on-site credit) for unincorporated sites. A 2023 to 2025 study considered mandatory inclusionary and higher fees; Council declined, so no inclusionary units are required citywide.
audit_note: Nov 10, 2026: FY27 Housing Impact Fee notice linked from the City fee page re-read; $3.58, $0.00 and $1.55 per square foot effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 confirmed. The City Fees and Charges database entry (fee ID 5700) attaches the same FY27 notice. Contact on the fee page is Ryan Dodge, (916) 808-8044.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Reduced Residential Development Impact Fees for Affordable Dwelling Units (Zero-Dollar Rate Program)
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (Form CDD-0410); affordability confirmed by SHRA or CADA
typical_award_size: Reduction of City-controlled development impact fees to a $0 rate for deed-restricted affordable units, capped at $10,000 per qualifying unit, funded by a $3 million annual General Fund/Measure U appropriation (reauthorized July 2025). Eligible fees: park development impact fee (Ch. 18.56 Art. II), sewer, combined sewer, water system and storm drainage development fees (Ch. 13), and the 65th Street, Central City, Jacinto Creek, North Natomas, Railyards, River District and Willowcreek area fees. School fees and SAFCA fees are not City-controlled and still apply.
per_unit_cap: $10,000 per qualifying affordable dwelling unit; mixed-income projects receive a proportional reduction.
affordability_requirement: Rental: occupied by low or moderate income households (80% or 120% AMI per H&S 50093) at affordable rent (H&S 50053), restricted at least 30 years by a recorded regulatory agreement with the City, SHRA or another public agency. For-sale: low income (80% AMI) at an affordable price, 30 years.
next_deadline: Rolling, first come first served against each fiscal year's $3 million allocation; no application deadline. Apply with Form CDD-0410 before permit issuance.
layering_notes: Worth roughly $5,000 to $10,000 per unit depending on area fees; stackable with the SacSewer impact fee waiver (County record) which covers the regional sanitation fee the City program does not touch, and with the Housing Impact Fee $0 rate. Because Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats waived fees as public funds, a fee reduction can by itself trigger state prevailing wage for a project that is otherwise exempt; most LIHTC projects already pay prevailing wage. The 2018 version waived fees without a cap; the 2024 modification added the $10,000 cap and the $3M budget, so large projects should not assume full waivers. Deferral of remaining impact fees to final inspection is available separately (CDD-0330).
cycle_notes: Funded by a $3 million annual General Fund/Measure U allocation. LIHTC and Homekey projects may ask to reserve funds when they receive their award. Contact City staff early because funding is limited. Program resolutions 2018-0428, 2019-0185 and 2024-0233 (adopted June 25, 2024).
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(b)(4) defines payment out of public funds to include fees that are reduced or waived by a political subdivision, so the fee reduction counts as public funds; an otherwise private project is exempt only if the subsidy is de minimis in the context of the project under 1720(c)(3), and the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption covers below-market loans, not fee waivers. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: City of Sacramento Development Impact Fee Deferral Program
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Building Division (Form CDD-0330)
typical_award_size: Deferral, not waiver: City impact fees may be paid at final inspection instead of permit issuance, useful for phased or multi-building projects. No cost figure published. Fee estimates available for a low-cost application. The Statewide Community Infrastructure Program (CSCDA SCIP) is also accepted for financing eligible City impact fees.
affordability_requirement: None; open to all residential projects.
next_deadline: Apply with CDD-0330 before permit issuance; fees due at final inspection.
layering_notes: Carries impact fees through construction so they can be paid from permanent loan proceeds; pair with the Zero-Dollar Rate reduction on the affordable units and SCIP bond financing of remaining fees. The County runs a separate deferral program for unincorporated projects (County record).
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Fees reduced, waived, deferred or reimbursed are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); whether a project is covered depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis (under $600,000 and 2% of project cost) and other 1720(c) exemptions. No program rule stating prevailing wage was found.
audit_note: PW citation pass 2026-11-09: false was uncited and no rule supports it; set unclear per Tier 3 rule.

program_name: Density bonus (City Code Chapter 17.704) and ministerial infill housing permits (Chapter 17.860 and SB 35/SB 423)
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: State density bonus law as implemented in Chapter 17.704 (no local enhancement beyond state minimums identified): e.g., 5% very low income units earns a 20% bonus plus one concession and unlimited waivers; up to 50% bonus and the 100% affordable 80% bonus per Government Code 65915. City ministerial permit (CDD-0428, adopted Aug 27, 2020) covers 2 to 200 unit residential or mixed-use infill projects meeting objective standards, no affordability or prevailing wage requirement, no CEQA, 60 to 90 day review; the state SB 35 permit (CDD-0427) requires 10% lower-income units at 11 or more units. Density bonus requests can be processed ministerially with either permit.
affordability_requirement: Per state law for the bonus; none for the City ministerial permit.
next_deadline: Rolling at entitlement. Parking: none required within a quarter mile of light rail, 50% reduction within a half mile.
layering_notes: Sacramento is the state's first Prohousing jurisdiction (renewed Dec 23, 2025 with the top score) and already has high base densities, so the bonus is mostly used for height, parking and setback waivers rather than unit count. Combining the City ministerial permit with a density bonus avoids hearings and CEQA for 100% affordable infill without the SB 35 prevailing wage trigger. Missing Middle zoning (2024) allows multi-unit on former single-family lots citywide.
prevailing_wage_basis: Value set false for consistency with other density bonus records: the density bonus itself provides no public funds (Labor Code 1720(a)(1), (c)(1)), so it does not trigger prevailing wage. Condition: a project that uses the streamlined path described below must pay prevailing wages under that statute. Government Code 65913.4(a)(8) and (a)(9) (https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_65913.4): projects approved through the SB 35/SB 423 ministerial path must pay prevailing wages unless the project has 10 or fewer units; 50 or more units add apprenticeship and health care requirements. Trigger is conditional: a density bonus (Gov. Code 65915) or the City ministerial permit (CDD-0428) alone pays no public funds and does not trigger prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
audit_note: PW citation pass 2026-11-09: set true because the record includes the SB 35/SB 423 path (prevailing wage above 10 units); density bonus or City ministerial permit alone does not trigger it.

program_name: Multifamily Mortgage Revenue Bonds, Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento (SHRA conduit issuance)
administering_agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency for the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
typical_award_size: Tax-exempt and taxable conduit bonds for rental projects of 12 or more units in the City; no minimum or maximum issue size (cost-effectiveness usually sets a floor). Applications for bonds without an SHRA loan are accepted year round; bond-plus-loan requests follow the SHRA pre-application schedule. Private placements require accredited or qualified institutional buyers in $250,000 denominations with investor letters.
affordability_requirement: Federal minimum 20% at 50% AMI or 30% at 60% AMI plus 10% at 50% AMI (H&S 34312.3); CDLAC and CTCAC rules govern; SHRA adds its 15% at 50% AMI and 5% at 30% AMI policy when an SHRA loan is included; non-competitive CTCAC deals averaging above 60% AMI must average at or below 59% AMI. Refundings that extend maturity require at least 10% of units at 50% or 60% AMI for 15 more years.
next_deadline: Bond-only applications any time; bond-with-loan applications follow the proposed 2027 SHRA schedule: pre-applications January 4, 2027 and July 1, 2027, full applications March 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027, approvals June 29, 2027 and January 25, 2028. SHRA Commission then City Council and Housing Authority approval, then CDLAC allocation.
layering_notes: SHRA prefers to be the issuer for City projects and pairs bonds with its gap loan; CSCDA or CMFA remain alternatives if timing does not fit. Bond policy requires the nonprofit owner to have material day-to-day involvement for projects claiming the welfare exemption, matching BOE scrutiny of managing general partners (see County Assessor record). Policies: 2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies (Section 9).
cycle_notes: 2027 schedule is Exhibit B to the 2027 SHRA budget item (SHRC heard Nov 4, 2026; County Board agenda Nov 3, 2026; City Council and Housing Authority hearing Nov 10, 2026); final adoption not yet confirmed. Schedule not yet posted on shra.org as of 2026-11-10.
prevailing_wage_basis: False for the bond financing itself. DIR coverage determinations PW 2006-001 Horizons at Indio (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf) and PW 2006-020(A) Heber (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe, hold that conduit multifamily revenue bonds, where the issuer assigns its rights to a private trustee that advances proceeds to the borrower and receives repayments directly, are not payment of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4). SHRA's structure matches: 2026 SHRA City Multifamily Lending and Bond Policies Section 9.1.3 state there is no liability to or pledge of the City's, the Housing Authority's or SHRA's faith, credit or taxing power, repayment is limited to private project revenues, and the program is self-supporting with the developer paying all costs; Section 9.4.11 provides a bank bond trustee as custodian of funds. Caveat: SHRA gap loans, HOME, CDBG or other public funds in the same deal are tested separately under SHRA policy 6.1 and Labor Code 1720 (1720(c)(5)(E) exemption; Davis-Bacon for HOME at 12+ or CDBG at 8+ units). Sources: https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-City-final.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: Nov 10, 2026: replaced the estimated early January 2027 pre-application with the dates in the proposed 2027 Multi-Family Loan and Mortgage Revenue Bond Application Schedule (SHRC Nov 4, 2026 packet).

program_name: Prohousing Designation (state scoring preference for City of Sacramento projects)
administering_agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department (designation held by the City; HCD administers the program)
typical_award_size: Not a direct subsidy. Projects in a Prohousing jurisdiction receive priority processing or bonus points in state programs including AHSC, Infill Infrastructure Grant, TCC, TIRCP and related transportation programs, and the City may apply to the Prohousing Incentive Program for added funds. Sacramento was the first designated city (Feb 10, 2022) and renewed Dec 23, 2025 with 108 points, the highest score in the state as of June 2026.
affordability_requirement: None at the project level; benefit flows to any eligible affordable project in the City.
next_deadline: Designation runs on HCD's renewal cycle; next renewal due around 2029. Contact Angel Anguiano, (916) 808-5519.
layering_notes: Relevant to layering: AHSC and IIG applications for City sites score Prohousing points that unincorporated-county and most other Sacramento-area cities (Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, Citrus Heights, Folsom were not confirmed as designated this pass) do not get. Check HCD's designated-jurisdictions tracker before assuming points for a non-City site.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 8, 2026: City page confirms first designation Feb 10, 2022, renewal Dec 23, 2025 with 108 points (highest in state as of June 2026), listed program benefits, PIP eligibility and staff contact. The 2029 renewal estimate is not stated on the page. prevailing_wage_trigger false has no cited rule; a designation funds nothing directly, so wage obligations come from the funding programs used.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) requires construction paid for out of public funds; Prohousing designation is a scoring preference that pays no funds to a project, so wage obligations come only from the funding programs used.

program_name: City of Elk Grove Affordable Housing Fund and Affordable Housing Impact Fee (Municipal Code Chapters 16.88 and 16.89)
administering_agency: City of Elk Grove Housing and Public Services Division (fund and RFPs); Finance Department (fee collection)
typical_award_size: Fee-funded local gap loan fund. New fees adopted September 23, 2026 (Resolution 2026-202, adopting the June 30, 2026 EPS nexus study) and Ordinance 09-2026 (second reading October 14, 2026), effective January 1, 2027, replacing the 2013 per-unit fees ($6,396 per single or two-unit dwelling and $3,837 per multi-unit dwelling in 2025): residential $3.59 per square foot single-unit, $3.29 owner-occupied multi-unit and $1.46 renter-occupied multi-unit; nonresidential $2.15 shopping center, $2.29 office (was $0.00), $0.39 industrial (manufacturing and warehouse merged), $1,146.75 per hotel room, plus per-unit rates for other uses, all including the 3% administrative fee. Fees were set at roughly 7.5% of the maximum justifiable fee. The City releases an RFP when the fund balance can support a project (generally about $5 million); the City reports $84 million lent to sixteen projects since inception (developer page, not opened).
per_unit_cap: None published; set in each RFP and loan agreement.
affordability_requirement: Ordinance 09-2026 expands fund uses to very low, low and moderate income households (previously very low and low) and adds EGMC 16.88.080 authorizing a local preference policy for deed-restricted rental and ownership units, consistent with fair housing law. Deed-restricted affordable housing is exempt from the residential fee.
next_deadline: New fee schedule effective January 1, 2027. No open RFP found as of 2026-11-10; watch elkgrove.gov/affordable-housing/developers and the City's purchasing RFP page. Contact Joshua Tovar, Management Analyst, jtovar@elkgrove.gov, or the Housing and Public Services Division, (916) 683-7111.
layering_notes: Elk Grove is an impact-fee jurisdiction (like the City and County of Sacramento) with no inclusionary option, so market-rate rental projects pay the fee rather than build units; the 2026 renter-occupied rate was deliberately set low ($1.46 per square foot recommended) because the nexus study found multifamily infeasible at higher fees. Elk Grove is outside the SHRA lending area (SHRA finances in other cities only under cooperation agreements), so this fund, state sources and Elk Grove's own PLHA are the local layer. Past RFPs tied fund loans to City-owned sites (Sheldon Farms North and Old Town, 2023). elkgrove.gov HTML pages and codepublishing.com return 403 to automated access, but council attachment PDFs open; facts here come from the Sept 23, 2026 staff report (item 8.2), Ordinance 09-2026 (Oct 14, 2026 item 7.5) and the Sept 23 and Oct 14 minutes. The North State BIA supported the staff recommendation at the hearing.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Affordable Housing Fund loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); 1720(c)(5)(E) may exempt below-market loans with 40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years. No Elk Grove fund guideline stating prevailing wage was found.
audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: hearing outcome confirmed. Sept 23 minutes: Ordinance 09-2026 introduced 4-0 (Suen absent) and Resolution 2026-202 adopted at staff-recommended rates; Oct 14 minutes: Ordinance 09-2026 adopted on second reading. Fees effective Jan 1, 2027.

program_name: Density bonus and developer incentives (Elk Grove Municipal Code Chapter 23.50) and streamlined housing approvals (Chapter 23.17)
administering_agency: City of Elk Grove Development Services, Planning Division
typical_award_size: State density bonus law implemented in Chapter 23.50 (eligibility at 10% lower income, 5% very low income, senior, 10% moderate for-sale, special needs, 100% affordable), one bonus with concessions per Government Code 65915; Section 23.50.080 (Ord. 12-2022) exempts affordable units built under the chapter from the Chapter 16.88 affordable housing fee. Chapter 23.17 provides ministerial streamlined approvals for infill affordable projects, affordable housing in commercial zones, mixed-income projects along commercial corridors, middle-class housing, adaptive reuse, faith and higher-education land, and urban subdivisions (titles confirmed; detailed standards not read this pass).
affordability_requirement: Per state law; fee exemption applies only to the deed-restricted affordable units.
next_deadline: Rolling at entitlement.
layering_notes: No local enhancement beyond state minimums identified. The fee exemption in 23.50.080 is the useful local layer: a density bonus project avoids the per-unit affordable housing fee on its affordable units, and the 2026 fee update proposed keeping the renter multi-unit fee low. Elk Grove adopted its Chapter 23.17 streamlining menu in response to the 2021-2029 Housing Element.
prevailing_wage_basis: Value set false for consistency with other density bonus records: the density bonus itself provides no public funds (Labor Code 1720(a)(1), (c)(1)), so it does not trigger prevailing wage. Condition: a project that uses the streamlined path described below must pay prevailing wages under that statute. Elk Grove Municipal Code Chapter 23.17 (read on the gocodebook mirror, https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/elk-grove/title-23-zoning/division-ii-administration-and-permit-procedures/chapter-23.17-streamlined-housing-approvals): Article II implements Gov. Code 65913.4, which requires prevailing wages for projects over 10 units (https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_65913.4); Articles III and IV implement Gov. Code 65912.100 to 65912.124, and 65912.130(b) requires prevailing wages (https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_65912.130); Article V requires the 65852.24(b)(8) and (b)(9) labor standards. Trigger is conditional on using those streamlined paths; a Chapter 23.50 density bonus alone pays no public funds and does not trigger prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
audit_note: PW citation pass 2026-11-09: set true because Chapter 23.17 streamlining paths carry state prevailing wage rules; density bonus alone does not. Chapter 23.17 text read only on a third-party mirror.

program_name: Elk Grove Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) and CDBG entitlement funds for affordable housing
administering_agency: City of Elk Grove Housing and Public Services Division
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 Action Plan (public review draft): CDBG $948,393 annual allocation plus $448,348 prior-year funds; HOME $357,251 annual allocation plus $698,628 prior-year funds ($1,055,880 available), as Elk Grove is its own HOME participating jurisdiction; Affordable Housing Fund (impact fee on new residential and nonresidential development) $405,158 available, earmarked as HOME match. The Plan says development and acquisition are expected to be funded mainly from the Affordable Housing Fund and/or PLHA, with HOME use for development still under consideration and a TBRA program being evaluated. PLHA: $2,541,598 awarded for 2019-2023 allocations; the original 2022 plan put most funds toward multifamily rental development, but the December 11, 2024 amendment shifted funds to homelessness activities and Affordable Ownership Worker Housing (40% of 2022-2023 funds, $266,401) after a planned use in the $5,436,000 Cornerstone Village loan fell through.
affordability_requirement: HOME: 24 CFR Part 92 rent and income limits; CDBG: low and moderate income per HUD; PLHA AOWH: up to 120% AMI ownership.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026; contact Housing and Public Services.
layering_notes: Elk Grove is a CDBG entitlement city since 2003 and a HOME participating jurisdiction, not a Sacramento County HOME Consortium member. The City reported the PLHA expenditure deadline does not fit multifamily timelines and redirected PLHA away from rental development; the Affordable Housing Fund and HOME are the realistic city capital sources. elkgrove.gov/affordable-housing pages return 403; grants pages and PDFs open.
cycle_notes: No developer NOFA found on the City site. CDBG and HOME are programmed through the annual Action Plan (2026-27 draft public hearing notice September 4, 2026); multifamily projects appear to be funded by direct negotiation, including on City-owned sites.
eligible_project_detail: City-owned sites (about 326 affordable units on two sites with developer partners)
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal funds: HOME projects with 12 or more assisted units trigger Davis-Bacon under 24 CFR 92.354; CDBG-assisted residential projects with 8 or more units trigger Davis-Bacon under Section 110 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974. PLHA alone does not set a federal wage rule.
audit_note: Original source_url (elkgrove.gov/affordable-housing/developers) returns 403; replaced with the City's 2026-27 Action Plan PDF. Prior text saying amounts unknown and that PLHA funds multifamily was superseded.

program_name: Rancho Cordova Housing Trust Development Impact Fee (Municipal Code Chapter 16.89) and city affordable housing gap financing
administering_agency: City of Rancho Cordova Housing Division (Community Development)
typical_award_size: Rancho Cordova Local Housing Trust Fund (LHTF), carried over from Sacramento County at incorporation and funded by the Housing Development Impact Fee on nonresidential development, paid per square foot at building permit. Rates listed in the City's March 2021 draft Housing Element: office $0.97, hotel $0.92, R&D $0.82, commercial $0.77, manufacturing $0.61 per square foot (current rates not confirmed). The Housing Element names the LHTF as a local source for new construction support, preservation of at-risk units and acquisition-rehabilitation by nonprofits. No fund balance, loan terms or NOFA found. The City's PLHA plan reportedly directs its allocation to gap financing for new affordable and permanent supportive housing (not opened).
affordability_requirement: The fee is a linkage to demand for very low-income housing created by nonresidential jobs (Housing Element); loan affordability terms not published.

program_name: Affordable Housing Plan requirement for new growth areas (Housing Element policy, south of Highway 50)
administering_agency: City of Rancho Cordova Planning Department and Housing Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Per the May 6, 2026 Keyser Marston survey prepared for Sacramento County, Rancho Cordova has no formal inclusionary ordinance but its Housing Element requires new residential projects in newly developing areas (generally south of Highway 50, mostly high-resource areas) to include an Affordable Housing Plan showing how the project contributes to affordable housing production; compliance options are on-site units, land dedication, rehabilitation of existing affordable units, or in-lieu fees negotiated through development agreements for master plans and specific plans.
affordability_requirement: No fixed percentage. Housing Element Policy H.1.5 and Action H.1.5.1 require an Affordable Housing Plan approved at the earliest entitlement (Specific Plan, Development Agreement or other primary entitlement) projecting units by extremely low, very low, low and moderate income and the ownership and rental split, set case by case by City Council.
next_deadline: Applies at specific plan or development agreement approval.
layering_notes: For affordable developers the practical effect is land: master plan developers (Rio del Oro, Suncreek, Arboretum, Westborough, etc.) often satisfy the plan by dedicating sites or paying per-door in-lieu fees, which creates site opportunities and sometimes developer contributions for 9% and 4% deals. Per Action H.1.5.1, contributed land may be used by the City and its nonprofit partners, and the City will pursue supplemental funding to reach below 50% AMI. Sources: May 6, 2026 Keyser Marston memo for Sacramento County, and the HCD-hosted 2021-2029 Housing Element draft (March 24, 2021); the City site itself blocks automated access.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Housing incentives and density bonus (Rancho Cordova Municipal Code Chapter 23.710)

affordability_requirement: Per state law.
next_deadline: Rolling at entitlement.

program_name: Citrus Heights Affordable Housing Fee on commercial development (Resolution 2022-048) and City Housing Trust Fund
administering_agency: City of Citrus Heights Housing and Grants Division (fund); Building Division (fee collection)
typical_award_size: Fee source, not a subsidy program with published terms. Per the July 9, 2026 development impact fee sheet (Resolution 2022-048): office (including medical and assisted living) $1.95, hotel $2.35, commercial and retail $1.77, industrial (flex and R&D) $1.67 per square foot on new commercial development or added commercial square footage, applying to commercial projects both under and over 5,000 square feet; residential is exempt. Rates were raised in June 2022 to the regional average after no update since 1992. Revenue goes to the City Housing Trust Fund administered by the Housing and Grants Division; fund balance and any lending terms not published.
affordability_requirement: Unknown; linkage fee funds are for very low income housing per the original 1992 ordinance title (Nonresidential Construction Fees for Funding Very Low Income Housing).
next_deadline: No NOFA found; projects should approach the Housing and Grants Division directly, (916) 727-4830, housing@citrusheights.net.
layering_notes: Citrus Heights has no inclusionary ordinance and no residential affordable housing fee, and no city fee waiver program for affordable units was found; the fee sheet also lists multimodal ($1,591 per multifamily unit), park, Measure A transportation, drainage, sewer, school and fire fees that apply to apartments. The trust fund is small because the city is built out with little new commercial construction; the realistic city layer is the CDBG, HOME Consortium and PLHA record below plus SHRA bonds under a cooperation agreement.
audit_note: Kept as other: the source documents show only fee collection into the Housing Trust Fund, with no published loan or grant program, terms or awards to classify as deployable. Fee table corrected: the affordable housing fee applies to commercial construction of any size, not only 5,000 square feet or more.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The July 2026 Development Impact Fees brochure lists the commercial Affordable Housing fee and states no wage rule (https://www.citrusheights.net/DocumentCenter/View/21440/Development-Impact-Fees-brochure_July2026), and no Citrus Heights Housing Trust Fund lending guidelines or wage rule were found on the City site. The fee is a cost to commercial developers and provides no public funds to the payer; trust fund money lent or granted to a housing project would be public funds under 1720(b), where below-market residual receipts loans may fall under the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption (below-market loan, at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI; see DIR PW 2019-018, https://dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2020/2019-018.pdf). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Citrus Heights CDBG entitlement, Sacramento County HOME Consortium share, and Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA)
administering_agency: City of Citrus Heights Housing and Grants Division (CDBG and PLHA); SHRA administers the HOME Consortium
typical_award_size: CDBG: about $600,000 a year in entitlement funds plus about $50,000 program income (2024 Action Plan), used mostly for public improvements, public services (15% cap, competitive round each summer) and a housing rehabilitation revolving loan fund. HOME: the City is a member of the Sacramento County HOME Consortium with the County, City of Sacramento and Rancho Cordova; its consortium share funded $3,580,000 to the 47-unit Sunrise Pointe permanent supportive housing project (approved 2018, completed August 2023). PLHA: $1,876,554 five-year allocation from HCD, partly for the Sayonara Drive redevelopment project and a navigator program.
affordability_requirement: Per federal and PLHA rules; HOME at or below 60% AMI with 20% of HOME units at 50% AMI.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The 2027 CDBG public service application deadline was August 4, 2026 and the 2027 Annual Action Plan went to Council October 28, 2026; the next public service NOFO is expected around July 2027. Multifamily HOME requests go through SHRA's two-round schedule with a Citrus Heights consortium set-aside, confirm with SHRA (916) 440-1393.
layering_notes: The HOME Consortium share is the only meaningful city-level capital source: Citrus Heights directed its share to Sunrise Pointe via SHRA rather than running its own NOFA. CDBG is largely spent on infrastructure and services. Federal funds trigger Davis-Bacon (HOME at 12 or more units, CDBG at 8 or more) and NEPA. Sayonara Drive is a City-led acquisition and redevelopment site that may seek a development partner.
cycle_notes: CDBG public service NOFO released each July with an early August deadline; Annual Action Plan hearings each October for the following calendar program year. No city capital NOFA for multifamily.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: Folsom Affordable Housing Loan (AHL) Program (Folsom Housing Fund 238 and Housing Trust Fund 221)
administering_agency: City of Folsom Community Development Department, Housing Services (loan consultant TDA, Inc.)
typical_award_size: Gap loans from the City's inclusionary in-lieu fee fund (Fund 238) and commercial housing trust fund (Fund 221). FY 2025-26 Mid-Year Budget (March 10, 2026): Fund 238 cash $23,960,396 at July 1, 2025, projected $23,850,147 at June 30, 2026; Fund 221 cash $951,872, projected $858,319. FY 2024-25 AB 1600 report: Fund 238 available balance $24,487,971 after $29.7M in loans receivable; Fund 221 available $978,809. Draws since mid-2025: $615,000 from Fund 238 to the General Fund for the Habitat for Humanity 300 Persifer Street sale (Res. 11467, Oct 14, 2025) and a $1.55M Fund 238 appropriation to buy two vacant Historic District housing sites on Leidesdorff Street, APNs 070-0046-026 and 070-0042-002 (Res. 11659, CEQA exemption filed June 24, 2026). Since 2019 the Council approved $13.7M in long-term loans for over 550 units in six projects; the last loan commitment was Harrington Grove, $2.7M for 52 units (2024). Guidelines adopted by Res. 11427 on August 26, 2025.
per_unit_cap: None published; sized by the City's consultant review of the pro forma against TCAC underwriting.
affordability_requirement: Minimum 55-year income, rent and affordability restrictions recorded senior to foreclosable liens; serves extremely low, very low and low income households; priority to sites outside concentrations of existing regulated housing and to Housing Element goals (seniors, large families, special needs). Fund 238 must spend at least 50% on construction or major rehab of multifamily rentals affordable to low and very low income households (Sacramento Housing Alliance settlement).
next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. No AHL NOFA or new loan award found in Council records from mid-2026 through November 2026; the 2025 guidelines allow strategic NOFAs when resources are available. Contact Housing Services via the Community Development Department, (916) 461-6000.
layering_notes: The largest city-controlled pool in Sacramento County outside the City of Sacramento (about $23M) with few competing applicants, because Folsom's rental projects are scarce and the Folsom Plan Area south of Highway 50 generates most in-lieu revenue. Loans are repaid from 50% of residual cash flow after allowed expenses; operating and replacement reserves required for the 55-year term; underwriting and compliance aligned to TCAC and LIHTC rules. Folsom is outside the SHRA lending area (cooperation agreement needed), so this fund plus state sources is the local layer; a Folsom Plan Area MOU committing to 890 deed-restricted affordable units (2024 General Plan amendments, not opened this pass) creates sites. Chapter 17.104.070 also allows fee waivers or deferrals and density bonuses for inclusionary units. folsom.ca.us returns 403 to automated access; the staff report and resolution were read from the City's public agenda host.
cycle_notes: Rolling, developer-initiated requests under the AHL guidelines (Res. 11427); NOFAs contemplated but none issued as of November 10, 2026. In 2026 the City used Fund 238 for land acquisition (Res. 11659, $1.55M, Leidesdorff Street sites designated for housing at a minimum of 20 units per acre and listed for lower-income RHNA), consistent with Housing Element Program H-17, which the 2025 APR says the City would explore in 2026. The FY 2026-27 budget was adopted June 9, 2026, but its fund-level housing figures were not found (folsom.ca.us returns 403).
prevailing_wage_basis: Unresolved. The August 26, 2025 staff report on the AHL Program Guidelines (Resolution 11427) and the housing funds staff report state no prevailing wage rule for City loans (the latter notes only that Homekey and Infill Infrastructure require it). City loans are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b); the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption for below-market loans with 40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years may apply depending on loan terms. Davis-Bacon applies only if City HOME (12+ units) or CDBG (8+ units) is layered. Sources: https://mccmeetingspublic.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/folsomca-meet-20667254009747e4aa5f68a4d63539d6/ITEM-Attachment-001-3c80e00338b5420aafa72ac45dae4a5d.pdf ; https://mccmeetingspublic.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/folsomca-meet-20667254009747e4aa5f68a4d63539d6/ITEM-Attachment-001-54dff11a603148f68a0203d4b6b13245.pdf ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Folsom Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 17.104) and in-lieu fee (Ordinance 1359, Resolution 11510)
administering_agency: City of Folsom Community Development Department, Housing Services
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. For-sale residential projects of 10 or more units (and rental projects of 10 or more units receiving City assistance) must make 10% of units affordable: 3% very low income and 7% low income; market-rate rental apartments are exempt. In-lieu fee effective February 12, 2026 (replacing 1% of the lowest sales price): $3.00 per square foot for single-family for-sale units and $2.50 per square foot for multifamily for-sale units of 1,500 square feet or less, paid at building permit into the Folsom Housing Fund (Fund 238); at least 50% of fee revenue must go to lower-income rental development. Prior-year collections exceeded $3.8M, mostly from the Folsom Plan Area. Alternatives: land dedication, off-site units, acquisition-rehab or conversion of market-rate units, inclusionary credits, combinations.
affordability_requirement: Rental inclusionary units restricted at least 30 years (or longer if state law requires); for-sale units resale-restricted; projects of nine or fewer market-rate units exempt.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; fee per unit in effect at permit issuance. Council adopted Ordinance 1359 on January 13, 2026 (first reading December 9, 2025) and set fees by Resolution 11510 the same night; next review expected with the Housing Element cycle. Developers paying fees only need a letter of intent, not a full inclusionary housing plan.
layering_notes: Nearly all Folsom Plan Area builders pay the fee, which is why Fund 238 holds about $22.8M and funds the AHL Program (record above). Rental multifamily was kept exempt in 2026 despite AB 1505 authority, so apartment developers owe no inclusionary units or fee. Developers who provide more than 10% can bank and sell inclusionary housing credits for five years (17.104.070). The ordinance text was read from the City Council's January 13, 2026 agenda packet on the City's public agenda host and the zoneomics code mirror.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

Chapter 3.90 text itself was not opened (codepublishing.com and folsom.ca.us return 403).
