program_name: Rohnert Park Density Bonus (Municipal Code Section 17.08.020) and affordable housing concessions under Section 17.08.010(E)
administering_agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Regulatory. Section 17.08.020 adopts state density bonus law (Government Code 65915 et seq.) by reference with no local increase beyond the state schedule; it sets application contents (project summary table, base and bonus unit counts, replacement housing compliance, parking) and ministerial processing without separate Planning Commission action. Section 17.08.010(E) lets the City Council grant for-sale projects exceeding the inclusionary requirement, and rental projects that include affordable units, additional concessions: an extra density bonus or incentives of equal financial value, waiver of City standards, direct financial assistance (loan or grant) from trust funds, and deferral of all City fees on market-rate units until certificate of occupancy. Projects making all inclusionary units affordable at median, low or very low income get an additional 5% density bonus.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable) for the state bonus; Council discretion for the local concessions, tied to on-site affordable units.
next_deadline: Submitted with the entitlement application; Council concessions requested through the project approval or a development agreement. Housing Element Program HO-3.B (City Density Bonus Program) and HO-2.E (Workforce Housing Overlay, to be presented by January 2026 and adopted by December 2026 if directed) may add local bonuses; status not confirmed.
layering_notes: Rohnert Park relies on development agreements and specific plans rather than a formal local bonus, so negotiate fee deferral, rental fee relief and gap funding together. The Workforce Housing Overlay would be the first local density tool beyond state law; check Planning for its status. The County's density bonus chapter applies only in unincorporated areas. Read from the zoneomics mirror of Title 17 (Ordinance 991, January 27, 2026 version).
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; the density bonus (Section 17.08.020, adopting Gov. Code 65915) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any public loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on a project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Rohnert Park affordable housing funds (Rental Affordable Housing Fee and Housing In-Lieu Fee account, Housing Fund) and Essential Housing Bond Financing Program (Housing Element Programs HO-3.F and bond program)
administering_agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department and City Manager's office; City Council approves assistance
typical_award_size: No NOFA; the City provides gap loans or grants and land through development agreements and Council action, drawing on the segregated affordable housing fee account (budget Funds 4220 Affordable Housing Rental Fee and 4225 Affordable Linkage Fee) and the Housing Fund named in the 2023-2031 Housing Element as a funding source for Programs HO-1.B and HO-3.F (affordable housing on underutilized City sites, including extremely low income units). The Housing Element's Essential Housing Bond Financing Program commits the City to authorize CSCDA or another JPA to issue an estimated $191.3 million in governmental-purpose bonds for acquisition-conversion of market-rate apartments and new deed-restricted housing, forgoing about $337,346 in property tax and targeting at least 222 units (99 very low, 57 low, 66 moderate). Current fund balances and any adopted lending guidelines were not found; the City's budget and Housing Successor (LMIHAF) reports could not be located online.
affordability_requirement: Fee revenue must serve very low, low and moderate income households (Section 17.08.010(J)); bond program units for very low to moderate income; City-site projects target extremely low income units.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. No NOFA; assistance is negotiated through development agreements and Council action. Contact Development Services (707-588-2231, Planning@rpcity.org).
layering_notes: Rohnert Park was Prohousing designated August 4, 2023 (42 points), which gives projects in the city AHSC and IIG scoring preferences. Local money is thin, so the practical stack is County CFH, County PLHA (Rohnert Park is a non-entitlement city within the County PLHA), RED Housing Fund and County PBVs (county records) plus LIHTC, with the City contributing fee deferrals, land (Program HO-3.F) or a modest gap loan. Rohnert Park's former Community Development Commission was a redevelopment agency, so a Housing Successor LMIHAF may exist; no annual report was found (flag for follow-up). The CivicPlus agenda search on rpcity.ca.gov returned no results for affordable housing and the old rpcity.org pages 404, so recent council actions could not be verified. Source is the adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element on the City's DocumentCenter.
cycle_notes: No NOFA cycle. The Housing Element set July 2023 to establish or join a JPA for the Essential Housing Bond Financing Program, with implementation through 2031; a Council and Planning Commission joint housing meeting was held February 5, 2026. Bond program and fund status not confirmed.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element (https://www.rpcity.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/355/Housing---RP-Adopted-Housing-Element-31723-PDF) states no prevailing wage rule for the affordable housing fee accounts, the Housing Fund, Program HO-3.F City sites or the Essential Housing Bond Financing Program, and no City lending guidelines were found. Gap loans and grants from fee revenue are public funds under 1720(b)(1), and City sites conveyed below fair market value are public funds under 1720(b)(3) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); below-market loans can be exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) (at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI), as DIR PW 2019-018 applied (https://dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2020/2019-018.pdf). Under the Essential Housing bond model a JPA buys and owns the property, so any rehab or construction it pays for needs its own coverage review.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element re-read on rpcity.ca.gov DocumentCenter; Essential Housing Bond Financing Program figures ($191,264,100 bonds, $337,346 forgone property tax, 222 units: 99 very low, 57 low, 66 moderate; JPA by July 2023; progress report to Council in 2027), Program HO-3.F and Housing Fund as funding source all match. Budget fund numbers (4220, 4225) and Section 17.08.010(J) were not re-read (codepublishing 403, rpcity.ca.gov search returns nothing); no evidence found that the City joined a JPA bond program.

program_name: City of Sonoma Inclusionary Housing requirement and in-lieu fee, Development Code Chapter 19.44 (Sections 19.44.020 and 19.44.030, Ordinance 06-2021)
administering_agency: City of Sonoma Planning Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects of five or more parcels or units must make at least 25% of units affordable: rental projects 5% extremely low, 10% very low and 10% low income (sequenced ELI, VLI, LI, then middle income); ownership projects 5% low, 10% moderate and 10% middle income. Projects of four or fewer units pay an in-lieu fee per Section 19.44.030; fractions below 0.5 may be paid as a fee. In-lieu fees are paid before building permit into the City's housing trust fund. Fee amount is set by Council resolution (amount not opened); Housing Element Program 1 called for a nexus-supported in-lieu fee by December 2023 and a July 2024 amendment requiring perpetual affordability. Units of 850 square feet or less, ADUs and additions under 850 square feet are exempt. Affordability is in perpetuity under Section 19.44.060.
affordability_requirement: Rental: 25% of units split 5% ELI, 10% VLI, 10% LI; ownership: 25% split 5% LI, 10% moderate, 10% middle income; restricted in perpetuity by recorded affordability agreement; affordable units must average at least 75% of market-rate unit floor area with the same bedroom count.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Housing Element Program 1 schedules a review of the inclusionary provisions and Development Code amendments by 2026; Program 15 Development Code amendments were noticed under CEQA in January 2026. Check with Planning (707) 938-3681 for the current in-lieu fee resolution.
layering_notes: At 25% with deep targeting, this is the strictest inclusionary rule among the Sonoma County priority cities, and the City says it has produced about 293 inclusionary and density bonus rental units inside 40 market-rate projects (about six units a year). Because the required ELI and VLI units can also qualify a project for a state density bonus (Chapter 19.44 counts inclusionary units when calculating the bonus), most market-rate rental projects in Sonoma pair the two. In-lieu revenue feeds the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (separate record). Growth management (Chapter 19.94 Housing Allocation Process) exempts affordable and density bonus units from the annual allocation. Code read from the zoneomics mirror (codepublishing.com returns 403); the City's Housing Policies page confirms the 25% rule.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: City of Sonoma Affordable Housing Trust Fund (established May 2019, funded by 1% of Transient Occupancy Tax and inclusionary in-lieu fees)
administering_agency: City of Sonoma City Manager's office and Planning Department; grants approved by City Council
typical_award_size: Small, case-by-case grants and loans approved by Council. Most recent award: $250,000 grant approved June 18, 2025 (agreement authorized July 16, 2025) to Burbank Housing toward acquisition and 55-year preservation of 18 units at Setzer Senior Apartments (8 units, 673 First St West) and Maysonnave Apartments (10 units, 270 First St East), leveraged with a $4.5 million BAHFA Housing Preservation Loan Pilot loan and San Francisco Housing Accelerator Fund financing; closed fall 2025. Revenue: Council approved on June 10, 2019 the final 1% of the Measure S TOT increase (TOT now 13%) effective September 1, 2019 to address affordable housing, estimated at the time at about $350,000 to $400,000 per year, plus in-lieu fees under Section 19.44.030. Press accounts put the balance at roughly $1.4 million to $1.9 million in 2025-2026; no City balance figure was opened.
affordability_requirement: Grant terms set per project; the 2025 preservation deal requires affordability for at least 55 years with rents averaging 30% of 80% AMI and tenants protected on modest income increases. The fund is earmarked for very low, low and moderate income housing (Section 19.44.030).
next_deadline: No NOFA. Requests go to City Council; the Council's 2026 priorities include creating a funding plan and policy for use of the Housing Trust Fund, so an allocation policy may be adopted in 2026-2027 (verify with the City Manager's office, (707) 938-3681).
layering_notes: Sonoma is a non-entitlement city inside the County's Urban County and County PLHA area, so projects in the city should combine this fund with County CFH, County HOME and CDBG, County PLHA, RED Housing Fund and County PBVs (county records); the 2025 Burbank deal shows the pattern with BAHFA regional preservation money. Housing Element Program 7 commits the City to pursue a Prohousing Designation and to request RED JPA membership in 2024 (status not confirmed). The City also runs an ADU fee waiver program (housing strategies page) and lists Policy H-4.6 fee waivers for affordable housing, but no multifamily fee waiver ordinance was found. Council staff reports on the civicweb portal could not be reached by meeting date; the City's press release and TOT page were used as sources.
prevailing_wage_basis: No City of Sonoma Housing Trust Fund rule on prevailing wage found. City grants are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1), but coverage of a private residential project depends on 1720(c) exemptions, notably 1720(c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost, which recent $250,000 awards may meet) and on other funding sources. Source: https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: no program rule; only the general Labor Code 1720 definition applies and the result depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

program_name: City of Sonoma Density Bonus and incentives, Development Code Sections 19.44.040 through 19.44.080 (Housing Element Program 19)
administering_agency: City of Sonoma Planning Department and Planning Commission (reductions in standards); City Council for other incentives

Adopts state density bonus law (Government Code 65915 through 65918) by reference; bonus percentage calculated under 65915(f), inclusionary units count toward the bonus, one bonus per project, Planning Commission may waive or modify standards to fit bonus units, incentives include reduced standards, mixed-use zoning, other cost-reducing incentives and state parking ratios. Density bonus and inclusionary units are exempt from the Chapter 19.94 growth management allocation.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds; affordable units restricted in perpetuity under Section 19.44.060 (2016 amendments raised the term from 30 to 55 years and 2021-2023 amendments made it perpetual).
next_deadline: Density bonus request filed with the first entitlement application; Housing Element Program 19 schedules an update of Chapter 19.44 to current state law (Program 15 code amendments noticed January 2026).
layering_notes: Past projects using the bonus include Firehouse Village and Maysonnave Apartments. In a city with low base densities and an urban growth boundary, the state bonus plus the 25% inclusionary rule is the main production tool; pair with the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and County sources. Read from the zoneomics mirror of the Sonoma Development Code (codepublishing.com and sonoma.municipal.codes return 403).

Code 65915) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any public loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on a project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

administering_agency: City of Sonoma Planning Department

The City's FY 2023-24 AB 1600 fee report shows the Affordable Housing Impact Fee account (732-00000-000-30120) collected $7,452.98 in FY 2023-24 with an ending balance of about $104,000 to $137,000 at June 30, 2024 (the report's summary and detail pages differ), no projects yet identified, and a plan to earmark funds in the FY 2025-26 budget. next_deadline: Unknown, verify with agency. Confirm whether the residential impact fee (due December 2023) and the expanded nonresidential fee (due December 2025) were adopted and at what rates; the City's 2026 Fee Study and Master Fee Schedule Update is underway and may carry them.
layering_notes: Any new fee revenue would flow to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (separate record) and expand the City's gap capacity, which is now mostly TOT-based. The County's Affordable Housing Program fees (county record) do not apply inside the city. Source is the adopted Housing Element on the City's ProudCity storage; Resolution 12-2020 and council fee resolutions could not be opened on the civicweb portal.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this nonresidential affordable housing fee (Resolution 12-2020) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. program_name: Fairfield Housing Trust Fund and Low/Moderate Income Housing (Housing Successor) funds, developer NOFA (August 2024 round)
administering_agency: City of Fairfield Housing Services Department (Fairfield Housing Authority as Housing Successor), 1000 Webster Street, Fairfield, 707-428-7392
typical_award_size: Gap loans from the City's Housing Trust Fund and former redevelopment Low/Mod funds. The August 2024 NOFA (Council goal HS 3.1, estimated $2,100,000) drew four proposals; Council approved financing for two. The March 2026 Council Goals report shows Danco approved for $1,500,000 with a Homekey+ application for a combined $23,500,000. A 2024 City press release (not opened, fairfield.ca.gov returns 403) described the round as about $1,000,000 of Local Housing Trust Fund money plus CDBG, applications due September 24, 2024. Closing of the 1600 Woolner site generated $1,121,000 in Low/Mod funds; the City also obtained a $700,000 state HOME grant and applied for an $800,000 MORE grant. Disposition of Successor Agency properties (Sem Yeto school site, Highway 12 parcel) is meant to replenish Low/Mod funds; an LOI for Sem Yeto was under review in December 2025. Council has also approved project-based voucher and housing trust fund financing for a multifamily preservation deal (Dec 2025 report).
per_unit_cap: None published. Danco approval equals $1,500,000 for one project.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low to moderate income households; Housing Element Action 3.1 requires long-term covenants (45 to 55 years) on City-assisted units.
next_deadline: No NOFA open as of November 2026. The City issues NOFAs when funds accumulate (last August 2024). Housing Element Action 3.2 commits to a NOFA a year before any tax credit compliance period ends for at-risk projects. Contact Housing Services before the next TCAC round.
layering_notes: Fairfield is the only Solano city with a working local trust fund plus Low/Mod successor money, so it is the first local gap source after the Solano County Housing Trust Fund (county record; the County put $4,500,000 ARPA through Fairfield for an EAH project in 2022 and proposed $400,000 for EAH's Tabor Commons in Aug 2026). Stack order for a Fairfield 9% deal: TCAC credits, City trust fund or Low/Mod loan, County SCHTF, Fairfield Housing Authority PBVs, fee deferral (separate record). Housing Element Action 1.1 says the Trust Fund is fed by a Housing Trust Fund fee and the City will study increasing it, dedicating excess property transfer tax, and a housing bond. Low/Mod funds carry Health and Safety Code 34176.1 spending rules (80% to 30% AMI and below once excess surplus triggers). Fairfield submitted a Prohousing Designation application in 2024 and was resubmitting for more points in 2025 (designation not confirmed), which would add scoring preference in state programs. Local and state funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so state prevailing wage applies unless a 1720(c) exemption fits the deal, such as 1720(c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (see prevailing_wage_basis). fairfield.ca.gov and its showpublisheddocument PDFs return 403 to scripts and WebFetch; the City's ClearPoint Council Goals reports on transparency.fairfield.ca.gov were the opened record.
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true rested on public-funds logic only; no program or local rule found, changed to unclear.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. No Fairfield Housing Trust Fund or Low/Mod NOFA, guideline, resolution or loan term requiring prevailing wage was found (the March 2026 Council Goals report contains no wage term; fairfield.ca.gov NOFA documents return 403). Loans are public funds under 1720(b)(1) or (b)(4), but qualifying below-market loans may be exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) and small subsidies under 1720(c)(3). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720 Low/Mod money is a housing successor asset fund, which 1720(c)(4) does not cover. Any CDBG in the round triggers Davis-Bacon at 8 or more units (24 CFR 570.603), and any state LHTF money is subject to prevailing wage unless a 1720(c) exception applies (2024 LHTF NOFA section V.D). https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/570.603 ; https://hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/lhtf/2024-lhtf-nofa.pdf

An adopted inclusionary fee would capitalize the Housing Trust Fund (record above) and change underwriting for mixed-income rentals. program_name: Fairfield affordable housing Fee Deferral Program (Municipal Code Chapter 5, Article I), Fee Credit Bank and Train Station Specific Plan fee reduction
administering_agency: City of Fairfield Community Development Department (Director approves deferrals and fee credits)
typical_award_size: Deferral, not waiver: affordable projects defer certain building and development fees to certificate of occupancy or permanent financing. Fee Credit Bank: credits from demolished buildings (water and sewer connection fees, not school or Solano County public facilities fees) can be applied to affordable projects. Train Station Specific Plan area: 25% reduction in development fees for multifamily units above 24 units per acre. ADUs under 750 square feet exempt from park, Cordelia open space, sewer connection and County public facilities fees; all ADUs exempt from a long list of City fees. No published dollar value of deferrals.
affordability_requirement: Deferral: multifamily must be at least 50% moderate-income and 25% low-income units, 55-year rental covenant (45 years ownership). Fee credits: low- and moderate-income units with a covenant of up to 55 years.
next_deadline: Apply to the Community Development Department with the building permit; no cycle. The City was updating its AB 1600 traffic and Northeast (TSSP) fees in 2022-2023; confirm current fee schedule.
layering_notes: Deferral improves construction-period cash flow but fees are still paid, so budget them. Fee credits are a real reduction when a demolition site has banked credits; ask the Director for the current bank balance. Solano County public facilities fees cannot be deferred or credited by the City (County record: no County waiver program). A fee credit or reduction is public funds under Labor Code 1720(c) if above de minimis, hence unclear. Source is the HCD-posted October 2022 review draft of the 2023-2031 Housing Element (adopted February 7, 2023, certified April 10, 2023 per the City's housing element site, not opened); Chapter 5 of the Municipal Code itself is on a blocked code host.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. The source (Fairfield 2023-2031 Housing Element review draft, Chapter 5 fee discussion) describes the Fee Deferral Program (Municipal Code Ch. 5, Art. I), Fee Credit Bank and Train Station Specific Plan fee reduction but says nothing on prevailing wage. Under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) fees reduced, waived or forgiven by a city are public funds; an interest-free deferral may also count. Coverage then depends on 1720(c) facts: (c)(3) de minimis test (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost) and (c)(5) affordable housing exemptions. Outcome depends on project facts, so left unclear (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public-funds definition, and coverage turns on the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and 1720(c)(5) exemptions for the specific project. Note: layering_notes cites 1720(c) for public funds; the operative definition is 1720(b)(4).

program_name: Fairfield Density Bonus (Zoning Code Section 25.38, Ordinance 2021-02)
administering_agency: City of Fairfield Community Development Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: State Density Bonus Law as implemented locally: 5+ unit projects with 5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate (for-sale), senior or other qualifying categories get bonus units, incentives and concessions, waivers and parking ratios per Government Code 65915; childcare facility adds bonus or concession. Density bonus application fee set by Council resolution. Applications processed concurrently with the project entitlement and decided by the same review authority (Section 25.41).
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 set-asides; 55-year rental covenants.
next_deadline: Not applicable; file with the planning entitlement.
layering_notes: No local enhancement beyond state law; the ordinance states Section 65915 supersedes any conflicting local text. Fairfield also offers priority processing for affordable projects (Housing Element Action 2.4) and lot consolidation incentives in the Heart of Fairfield and Train Station plan areas. Read on the zoneomics code mirror because the City's code host returns 403. Pair with the Fee Deferral Program and Trust Fund records.
audit_note: Fairfield's official code host (codepublishing.com Fairfield25) returned 403 to WebFetch and fairfield.ca.gov is blocked, so Section 25.38 could only be read on the zoneomics mirror.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Fairfield CDBG and HOME, multifamily rehabilitation NOFAs and PLHA formula allocation
administering_agency: City of Fairfield Housing Services Department (HUD CDBG entitlement; state HOME and CalHome grantee; HCD PLHA formula recipient)
typical_award_size: CDBG multifamily rehabilitation NOFAs: about $475,000 CDBG offered in 2024 (due September 24, 2024) and about $400,000 offered July 22, 2026 (due September 4, 2026, rehab complete by June 30, 2027, minimum score 75) per City news releases found in search but not opened. FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan reportedly budgets $115,120 for multifamily rehabilitation. State HOME grant of $700,000 obtained (2024-2025) and $800,000 MORE grant applied for. PLHA formula: Fairfield CY 2024 $274,392, CY 2025 $293,914, five-year 2024-2028 estimate $1,714,950 (HCD NOFA); Housing Element dedicates 20% of PLHA to homeownership, and three PLHA down payment loans closed in FY 2025-26.
per_unit_cap: HOME per-unit subsidy limits (24 CFR 92.250) for HOME-funded units.
affordability_requirement: CDBG rehab: at least 51% of units at or below 80% AMI. HOME: 20% at 50% AMI, balance at 60% AMI, 55-year HCD covenant. PLHA: per the City's five-year plan (not opened).
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The City has not posted its next CDBG multifamily rehabilitation NOFA; prior rounds were released in summer.
layering_notes: Small money. CDBG rounds are rehab-only (no new construction or acquisition) and sized at $400,000 to $475,000. program_name: Vallejo Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 16.216, Affordable Housing Requirements; Housing Element Program B 2.1.1)
administering_agency: City of Vallejo Planning and Development Services Department, Long Range Planning (Hector Rojas, 707-553-7283)
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Introduced October 27, 2026; Council directed the Planning Commission version: applies to residential projects of 10 or more units; rental projects provide 4% affordable (2% very low, 2% low); ownership projects of 10 to 100 units 7% (4% low, 3% moderate), over 100 units 10% (6% low, 4% moderate). Staff had proposed a 20-unit threshold with 5% rental (1% VLI, 4% LI). In-lieu fee may be paid for some or all units, set by a later Council resolution and deposited in a separate City affordable housing fund; fractional units under 0.50 may be paid as fee. Alternatives: off-site units in the same census tract, rental units in ownership projects. EPS feasibility (March 13, 2026) found a subsidy gap of about $369,000 per very low-income apartment and $471,614 per low-income single-family unit, which are the equivalent in-lieu fee ceilings. Effective 90 days after final passage. Exemptions: disaster rebuilds, ADUs, residential care facilities, applications complete before the effective date.
affordability_requirement: Rental units at 30% of HCD income limits less utilities (2026 Solano three-person limits: VLI $61,850, LI $98,950, MOD $134,550); 55-year minimum covenants for rental and ownership units; Affordable Housing Plan and recorded Affordable Housing Agreement required; one-for-one replacement of demolished deed-restricted units.
next_deadline: Second reading and adoption scheduled November 10, 2026; in-lieu fee resolution to follow before the effective date (about February 2027). Planning Commission asked for annual reports and a new feasibility study about two years after enactment. A Commercial Linkage Fee ordinance is to be drafted after adoption.
layering_notes: Vallejo's RHNA is 2,900 units with 1,446 lower and moderate units still unmet after 2025. This is the first inclusionary ordinance in Solano County; its in-lieu fund will be a new, small local gap source alongside the Housing Successor LMIHAF (separate record). Developers of 10+ unit rentals should model 4% affordable units or the fee once set. Underwriting in Vallejo is weak (EPS found rental yields of 4.7% to 5.0% against a 5.5% threshold), so the fee is expected to be modest. Staff report and draft ordinance opened on the City's inclusionary project page.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this inclusionary ordinance (Chapter 16.216) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any public loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on a project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

Any public loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on a project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720 Section 16.214.08 states financial and certain other incentives may require prevailing wages if state law requires. Section 16.214.14 also offers the Gov. Code 65913.4 (SB 35) streamlined path, and 65913.4(a)(8) requires prevailing wages for projects using that path unless they have 10 or fewer units and are not otherwise public works (65913.4(a)(9)). https://california.public.law/codes/government_code_section_65913.4
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: confirmed against the zoneomics mirror of Chapter 16.214 because the official code host (codepublishing) is blocked; sections 16.214.03, .07, .08, .09 and .14 match.

program_name: Suisun City Housing Authority Project-Based Vouchers (2023 RFP, up to 96 PBVs) and Almond Gardens Apartments
administering_agency: Suisun City Housing Authority (City Council plus two tenant commissioners), 701 Civic Center Boulevard; Jason Goltiao, Housing Program Manager, 707-421-7332, jgoltiao@suisun.com
typical_award_size: October 4, 2023 RFP (proposals due October 25, 2023) offered up to 64 project-based vouchers plus 32 for exception categories (seniors, persons with disabilities receiving services), 96 total; a project may receive the greater of 25 units or 25% of units (100% for exception projects); contract rents capped at 110% of FMR or an approved exception payment standard; 100-point scoring. The vouchers went to Almond Gardens Apartments (707-815 Almond Street, Harbor Park LLC): 97 new units (96 restricted at 30% to 50% AMI) replacing a condemned 51 to 52 unit complex, total cost about $66,126,000, estimated HUD PBV funding about $3,274,484 a year, CDLAC allocation of $30,276,660 in tax-exempt bonds through CMFA plus $2,917,820 annual federal and $5,994,579 state credits (December 11, 2024). NEPA FONSI June 26, 2025, release of funds about July 15, 2025; construction June 2025 to January 2027.
per_unit_cap: HAP contract rent capped at 110% of FMR or exception payment standard.
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 50% AMI at admission (75% at 30% AMI); Almond Gardens units at 30% and 50% AMI with 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: The 2023 PBV allocation is fully committed to Almond Gardens. A new 5-Year PHA Plan (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2030) was heard March 18, 2025. Ask the Housing Program Manager whether any PBVs remain or a new RFP is planned; HCV waitlist is closed.

Almond Gardens shows the Suisun stack: CMFA bonds, 4% and state credits, PBVs, City land and impact fee waiver (separate record). PBVs alone do not trigger state prevailing wage; Davis-Bacon applies to PBV new construction of 9+ contract units. suisun.com returns 403 to scripts; the Housing Authority page was opened with WebFetch and the CTCAC staff report (treasurer.ca.gov) supplied the financing figures.

The Suisun City Housing Authority page says the 2023 PBV RFP covers existing, new or rehabilitated units and that Federal Labor Standards will apply to eligible projects; Almond Gardens (97 new units replacing a condemned complex) is new construction, so Davis-Bacon applies. https://www.suisun.com/Departments/Development-Services/Suisun-City-Housing-Authority https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153

program_name: Suisun City Residential Density Bonus and Density Incentives (Municipal Code Chapter 18.47, Ordinance 743 of March 21, 2017)
administering_agency: City of Suisun City Development Services Department, Planning Division, 707-421-7335
typical_award_size: Applies to multifamily, live-work and mixed-use projects of five or more units; implements Government Code 65915 to 65918 set-asides and bonuses; 15% to 35% additional bonus for land donation (18.47.065); childcare facility bonus or concession (18.47.070); parking ratios on request (18.47.080). Section 18.47.075 lets the Planning Commission or Council grant a bonus greater than the chapter requires for qualifying projects.
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 set-asides; 55-year rental covenants; density bonus agreement.
next_deadline: Not applicable; file with the planning application.
layering_notes: The 2017 chapter predates AB 1287 and other state changes; state law governs where the chapter is less generous, but 18.47.075 is a useful local hook for asking for more than the state formula. Housing Element Program 1.B adds priority processing, fee deferrals and density and intensity bonuses for residential and mixed-use projects in the Downtown Waterfront Specific Plan area, and Program 3.A promotes the density bonus and fee deferrals for special-needs housing. Read on the zoneomics code mirror; the City's code host returns 403.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage.
