program_name: Auburn Density Bonus ordinance (Municipal Code Sections 159.330 to 159.342, ministerial density bonus permit)
administering_agency: City of Auburn Planning and Public Works Department (1225 Lincoln Way, Auburn)
typical_award_size: Regulatory incentive, not a subsidy. Implements Government Code 65915 to 65918 through a ministerial density bonus permit processed with other entitlements: bonuses per state tables for very low, lower and moderate income units, 20% for senior, foster youth, disabled veteran and homeless housing, 80% for 100% affordable projects (no density limit within one half mile of a major transit stop), incentives and concessions by threshold with a three-story or 33-foot height increase when four concessions apply near transit, unlimited waivers of standards that physically preclude the project, land donation bonus, parking ratios per state law, and a recorded density bonus housing agreement. The Director must determine completeness and the eligible bonus within 30 days. Filing fee set by Council resolution.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds; affordable units governed by Section 159.340 (affordable rent and housing cost per Health and Safety Code 50053 and 50052.5) with 55-year rental covenants.
next_deadline: Processed with entitlements; no deadline.
layering_notes: Auburn (population about 14,000) has no local housing trust fund, inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee fund, housing successor fund or city NOFA; this chapter and the negotiated fee reductions in the Housing Element (next record) are the City's only tools. The Housing Element credits past density bonuses (one project received a 400% bonus with apartments in an R-1 zone and a 50% parking reduction) and Placer County land donation and Housing Trust Placer money for a 79-unit project. Gap funding for Auburn projects comes from Placer County in-lieu fee loans, County PLHA, Housing Trust Placer and PCHA PBVs. Chapter read on the zoneomics mirror (Auburn's code publisher is blocked); auburn.ca.gov DocumentCenter PDFs open directly.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Auburn 2021-2029 Housing Element Program A and Program I: case-by-case fee reductions or deferrals, alternative development standards and state CDBG and HOME applications for affordable housing (adopted May 24, 2021)
administering_agency: City of Auburn Planning and Public Works Department, with participating nonprofit and for-profit housing providers
typical_award_size: Negotiated, not codified. Program A commits the City to consider fee reductions or deferrals sized to the financial need of each affordable development, to negotiate alternative standards (parking, street improvements, density, lot coverage), to apply for state-administered CDBG, HOME and other funds on behalf of affordable developers or support their applications, and to meet at least twice in the planning period with housing providers; Program I adds land write-downs, expedited processing, identification of impact fee reductions and incentives beyond the density bonus for extremely low income housing, with priority in high resource areas and the Baltimore Ravine Specific Plan. Track record: 2010 and 2014 state HOME grants for owner rehabilitation and first-time buyers (completed November 2017); the City did not apply for 2018 HOME funds due to staff turnover and no new award was found. No dollar amounts or fee schedule exist.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low, very low, low and moderate income housing as defined in the Housing Element; terms set per project.
next_deadline: Request during entitlement; Council action is needed for any fee reduction. Auburn is a non-entitlement city, so state CDBG and HOME NOFAs (HCD) are the vehicles, with the City as applicant or supporter; check HCD NOFA calendars and the City's annual NOFA review.
layering_notes: Because Auburn is non-entitlement, Placer County's PLHA and the County's in-lieu fee gap loans (county records) are the nearest local money; the County's Priority Applicant Policy (effective July 1, 2026) would apply to County-funded units. Fee deferral for residential projects is now mandated statewide by SB 937 (to final inspection), so the Housing Element's deferral promise mainly adds the possibility of a reduction. Verified from the adopted 2021 Housing Element PDF on auburn.ca.gov; no 2024 or 2025 Annual Progress Report could be located (CivicPlus Agenda Center and search pages are script-rendered).
prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The adopted 2021 Housing Element (Programs A and I) does not address prevailing wage. Negotiated fee reductions or land write-downs are reduced fees or below-market land under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and (b)(3), with coverage depending on the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and 1720(c)(5) exemptions. If the City secures state CDBG or HOME for a project, those programs carry their own federal rules (Davis-Bacon for CDBG at 8+ units, HOME 24 CFR 92.354 at 12+ HOME units), but those are separate awards.
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition and the outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

program_name: Measure U Affordable Housing Bond: New Construction Notice of Funding Availability (NC NOFA), Resolutions 90419, 90552, 90894 and 91377 C.M.S.
administering_agency: City of Oakland Housing and Community Development Department (HCD), Housing Development Division, 250 Frank H. Ogawa Plaza, Suite 5313; Fay Darmawi, Deputy Director, fdarmawi@oaklandca.gov, (510) 238-3714
typical_award_size: Measure U (Nov 2022, $850,000,000 bond, $350,000,000 for affordable housing in three tranches). Tranches 1 and 2 committed $248,000,000 to 32 projects (New Construction 15 projects, 1,172 units, $167,035,412; R2H2/Homekey 6 projects, $31,564,588; ACAH 11 projects, $37,000,000; 5% admin $12,400,000), leveraging about $5 outside per $1 City. 2024 NC NOFA: 24 applications requesting $424,000,000; January 2025 awards $80,500,000 to 5 projects (583 units); November 2025 pipeline awards $63,500,000; 13 unfunded pipeline applications (919 units, $246,000,000 requested) remain. Tranche 3: $50,000,000 appropriated in the FY 2026-27 midcycle budget and authorized by Resolution 91377 C.M.S. (October 2026), about $35,000,000 of it for the NC NOFA. Typical City loans run roughly $8,000,000 to $20,000,000 per project, 55-year residual receipts.
per_unit_cap: Maximum City loan is 40% of the total residential development cost of the project's affordable units, with the value of any City land donation counted toward that cap; HOME-assisted units are also limited to HUD Region IX per-unit subsidy limits ($181,488 studio to $359,263 four bedroom as of February 13, 2024). Within the cap, awards are sized by gap underwriting to the minimum City subsidy needed (2024 NC NOFA terms; the Tranche 3 NOFA may revise them). Oakland Housing Authority has indicated up to $8,000,000 in operating, predevelopment or capital assistance for NC NOFA and R2H2 projects with PSH or deeply affordable units (OHA Board action pending).
affordability_requirement: 2024 NC NOFA: 100% of City-assisted units restricted to low income households at or below 60% AMI with rents no more than 30% of 60% AMI (and at least 10% below market rents within one mile); threshold of at least 20% of affordable units at rents no more than 30% of 30% AMI reserved for extremely low income households, with points for deeper ELI and homeless or special needs targeting; no more than 15% of unassisted affordable units may be moderate income; 55-year regulatory agreement; loans typically 3% simple interest, 55-year term, repaid from residual receipts. Scoring favors public land, ministerial approvals, readiness for tax credits, emerging developer joint ventures, displacement-risk neighborhoods.
next_deadline: Next NC NOFA planned for late 2026 or early 2027 after state HDFC rules settle; awards timed to the spring 2027 tax credit round. Existing pipeline applicants may be advanced ahead of a full round. Confirm release date with HCD (NOFA mailing list).
layering_notes: Oakland is the largest city funder in the county (42% of Alameda County affordable permits 2024-25). Stacks with Alameda County Measure A1 Oakland base allocation and Measure W Home Together New Construction RFP (five Oakland projects won Measure W in March 2026: Liberation Park, 500 Lake Park, 3135 San Pablo, East 12th Circle, Brighter Bancroft), county PBVs via OHA, and state HDFC/TCAC. City commitment is intended as the first local layer so projects can show match for county and state rounds. Measure U loans carry Oakland local hire, First Source and prevailing wage requirements; a Project Labor Agreement debate for Measure U projects occurred in 2024. Measure KK (2016, $100,000,000 housing) is fully committed and reported with Measure U. Non-bond sources commingled in the same NOFA: Affordable Housing Impact Fee Fund 1872, Jobs/Housing Impact Fee Fund 1871, boomerang Fund 1870, LMIHAF 2830, HOME 2109, PLHA 2145, excess redevelopment bond funds. oaklandca.gov returns 403 to scripts; all material read from Oakland Legistar attachments and the City's OpenCities prelive host.
cycle_notes: pipeline NOFA with supplemental awards as funds arrive
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Oakland HCD Development Loan Program Requirements (Contract Compliance section) require City-funded projects to comply with Payment of Prevailing Wages and state that the general contractor must comply with Davis-Bacon if applicable and State of California prevailing wage as determined by DIR; City requirements apply regardless of fund source. https://oaklandca.prelive.opencities.com/files/assets/city/v/1/housing-comm-dev/documents/development-loan-program-requirements.pdf Same requirement in the 2019 New Construction NOFA program description. https://cao-94612.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/NOFA-2019-New-Construction_Program-Description.pdf
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: per_unit_cap said no fixed cap published; the 2024 NC NOFA program description caps the City loan at 40% of the affordable units' total residential development cost plus HOME per-unit limits. affordability_requirement omitted the 60% AMI ceiling on all City-assisted units; added it with the 20% ELI threshold at 30% of 30% AMI. Award totals, Tranche 3 amounts and NOFA timing (late 2026 or early 2027) match the October 13, 2026 CED report.

program_name: Acquisition and Conversion to Affordable Housing (ACAH) Program and Housing Accelerator Fund partnership (rolling ACAH NOFA, Resolutions 90308 and 90118 C.M.S.)
administering_agency: City of Oakland HCD, Housing Preservation Services, with the San Francisco Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) as program administrator; applications go to HAF
typical_award_size: Since 2017 ACAH has awarded $59,800,000 to preserve 339 units, with set-aside pools for community land trusts and cooperatives. Current structure (June 2024): $10,000,000 unsecured City loan to HAF pooled with private capital (HAF targets 2.5 to 1 leverage, $25,000,000) for short-term bridge acquisition loans, plus $20,000,000 to $30,000,000 of Measure U committed for City take-out permanent loans that revolve the pool. Rolling ACAH NOFA of $22,000,000 released December 2025. 2025 preserved 48 units (1432 12th Avenue co-op with St. Mary's Center, 1534 29th Avenue with Bay Area Community Land Trust).
per_unit_cap: None published; bridge loans sized to acquisition price, permanent take-out sized to residual receipts capacity.
affordability_requirement: 55-year regulatory agreement; all units rented to households averaging 80% AMI and below; priority to naturally occurring affordable housing in displacement-risk neighborhoods, CLTs and co-ops.
next_deadline: Rolling; the December 2025 $22,000,000 NOFA remains open through HAF until funds are committed. Confirm balance with HAF or Oakland HCD.
layering_notes: Oakland's preservation layer. Comparable to Berkeley's Small Sites Program but much larger. Pairs with Measure W acquisition-rehab RFP planned by the County (about $10,000,000) and county boomerang funds. Rehab scopes over bridge period are modest; larger rehabs can later use 4% credits and bonds. Measure U is the primary capital source so City labor standards apply. Source documents are the October 2026 HCD funding authorization report (Legistar) and the 2025 HCD Annual Impact Report (OpenCities prelive host); the ACAH NOFA itself sits on the 403-blocked oaklandca.gov site.
eligible_project_detail: small sites (single family to mid-size apartments)
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Oakland HCD Development Loan Program Requirements (Contract Compliance section) require City-funded projects to comply with Payment of Prevailing Wages and state that the general contractor must comply with Davis-Bacon if applicable and State of California prevailing wage as determined by DIR; City requirements apply regardless of fund source. https://oaklandca.prelive.opencities.com/files/assets/city/v/1/housing-comm-dev/documents/development-loan-program-requirements.pdf The 2019 Acquisition-Rehab-Preservation NOFA program description carries the same Contract Compliance requirement. https://cao-94612.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/NOFA-2019-Acquisition-Rehab-Preservation_Program-Description.pdf

program_name: Rapid Response Homeless Housing (R2H2) and local Homekey program (Resolutions 89977 and 90419 C.M.S.)
administering_agency: City of Oakland HCD, Homeless Housing Development unit
typical_award_size: Program capitalized in 2023 with boomerang Fund 1870 and LMIHAF: $10,400,000 capital plus $19,600,000 operating subsidy; $21,000,000 Measure U Tranche 2 capital added September 2024 for $31,400,000 total capital. Four awards to date (Mandela House, Friendly Manor, Covenant House, the Holland), leveraging over $87,000,000 outside funds (about $4 to $1). About $7,000,000 of Measure U Tranche 2 remained available for new applications as of September 2026; Tranche 3 may add more. City also co-applies for state Homekey+: 2025 awards $7,100,000 The Maya (23 units), $33,000,000 Mark Twain Homes (109 units), $6,500,000 34th and San Pablo (15 PSH units).
affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing or permanent transitional housing for people experiencing homelessness; quick-build, ready to house residents within 12 months of award and fully operational within 15 months; Housing First.
next_deadline: Rolling RFP since November 2023; apply any time while capital remains. Confirm remaining balance with HCD.
layering_notes: Oakland analog to state Homekey; projects typically combine R2H2 capital with Homekey+, county Measure W Housing dollars, HHAP and county BHSA. Operating subsidy is the binding constraint; the Prohousing Incentive Program award ($2,390,000 in 2023, up to $1,600,000 requested in Round 4, 2026) is dedicated to capitalized service reserves for R2H2 and NC NOFA PSH units. OHA may add project-based vouchers or operating subsidy.
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Oakland Homekey and R2H2 RFP pre-application presentation: teams must comply with Payment of State prevailing wages (Homekey and City requirement) plus the Living Wage Ordinance and certified payroll. https://www.oaklandca.gov/files/assets/city/v/1/housing-comm-dev/documents/r2h2/final-homekey-r2h2-rfp-pre-app-presentation-v.2-1.pdf

program_name: Affordable Housing Impact Fee, OMC Chapter 15.72 (2025 amendments, Ordinance 13853 C.M.S.), with exemption for affordable housing projects and Fund 1872
administering_agency: City of Oakland Planning and Building Department (collection, impactfees@oaklandca.gov) and HCD (expenditure through NOFAs)
typical_award_size: Requirement on market-rate housing and a funding source for affordable housing. July 15, 2025 amendments converted the fee from per unit to per square foot (AB 602): multifamily Zone 1 $36.17 per sq ft (was $29,658 per unit), Zone 2 $29.18 (was $23,929), Zone 3 $19.73 but set at 0% through FY 2027-28; townhome $14.98 / $10.97 / $5.99 (Zone 3 at 0%); single family $12.66 / $9.08 / $4.40 (Zone 3 at 0%). Annual Marshall and Swift inflation adjustment each July 1. Exempt: 100% affordable projects, projects providing the on-site or off-site affordable units specified in 15.72.100-110, ADUs, 2 to 4 unit projects, single-family homes under 1,750 sq ft, SB 684 projects, and the first four smallest units in larger projects. All impact fee payments deferred to certificate of occupancy for 100% affordable and density bonus projects (SB 937 alignment). FY 2024-25 AHIF fund: start $18,162,106, end $10,737,051, $6,577,455 spent, $5,893,752 committed, $4,843,299 being committed to NOFA pipeline projects.
per_unit_cap: Not applicable (exemption). Mixed-income option: provide on-site affordable units at the percentages in 15.72.100 to zero out the fee.
affordability_requirement: Exemption requires 100% affordable (manager units excepted) or the on-site mix in 15.72.100 (chosen to align with state density bonus thresholds); fee revenue funds 100% affordable developments for extremely low to moderate income households through the NC NOFA.
next_deadline: Fee due at building permit (installments) or deferred to certificate of occupancy for affordable and density bonus projects; rates adjust each July 1. Zone 3 zero rate expires June 30, 2028 unless extended.
layering_notes: Oakland has no general permit or impact fee waiver program; the AHIF exemption plus SB 937 deferral of transportation and capital improvement fees is the relevant relief. Affordable projects still pay the Transportation Impact Fee (Ch. 15.74) but are exempt from the Capital Improvements Impact Fee. AHIF revenue (Fund 1872) is one of the non-bond sources commingled with Measure U in the NC NOFA, so this record both reduces developer cost and feeds the Oakland NOFA record. No county impact fee exists for comparison. Fee rate schedule read in the July 2025 Master Fee Schedule exhibit on Legistar; the annual report FY 2024-25 (November 2025) supplied balances.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. A fee waived or reduced by a political subdivision is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), but whether a categorical AHIF exemption is a waiver, and whether coverage follows, depends on 1720(c)(3) de minimis limits (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost) and project facts; the 1720(c)(5)(E) affordable housing exemption covers below-market loans only, not fee waivers. AHIF revenue spent through Oakland NOFA loans is governed by the NOFA terms, not this record.
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear. Only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public funds definition, with outcome dependent on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. No DIR determination on an affordable housing impact fee exemption was located.

program_name: Jobs/Housing Impact Fee (commercial linkage fee), OMC Chapter 15.68, Fund 1871
administering_agency: City of Oakland Planning and Building Department (collection) and HCD (expenditure)
typical_award_size: Linkage fee on office and warehouse projects over 25,000 sq ft: $7.87 per sq ft for permits applied July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025 per Table 4 ($8.05 for July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024), inflation adjusted; paid 25% at permit, 50% at certificate of occupancy, 25% eighteen months later. The 2025 amendments extended the fee to additional nonresidential categories. FY 2024-25 JHIF fund (Fund 1871): start $13,964,433, end $12,546,460, fee revenue $0 in FY 2024-25, $12,060,074 committed to affordable developments, $486,386 being committed to pipeline projects. Past JHIF awards include $2,500,000 (2700 International, 75 units) and $3,472,130 (34th and San Pablo, 60 units).
affordability_requirement: Revenue restricted to acquisition, new construction, substantial rehabilitation and preservation of affordable housing, awarded through HCD NOFAs.
next_deadline: Fee collected continuously; funds flow to the NC NOFA pipeline (next round late 2026 or early 2027).
layering_notes: Oakland is one of only two priority cities in the county with a commercial linkage fee (Fremont also has one). Classified as loan because the fund balance is deployed as City development loans through HCD NOFAs (New Construction and ACAH); the fee itself is a cost to commercial developers, not to affordable housing sponsors. Revenue is modest relative to Measure U (FY 2024-25 JHIF fee revenue was $0) but is flexible local money with no bond restrictions, which HCD uses for early predevelopment commitments. Developers do not apply to this fund directly; it is part of the NOFA sources table.
audit_note: Reclassified from other to loan per audit rule for trust funds that deploy loans. Impact Fee Annual Report FY 2024-25 (CED Committee February 10, 2026) shows JHIF committed to projects through City loans.
prevailing_wage_basis: The FY 2024-25 Impact Fees Annual Report shows JHIF revenue is released through Oakland HCD NOFAs (Resolution 90419 C.M.S., 2024 New Construction NOFA) and lent to projects such as 2700 International and 34th and San Pablo (https://oakland.legistar1.com/oakland/attachments/cbff9d9a-7710-4842-8968-0b288ef0fcb4.pdf). Those loans are made under the City of Oakland HCD Development Loan Program Requirements, whose Employment and Contracting section requires Payment of Prevailing Wages and states the general contractor must comply with Davis-Bacon if applicable and State of California prevailing wage as determined by DIR; City requirements apply regardless of fund source (https://oaklandca.prelive.opencities.com/files/assets/city/v/1/housing-comm-dev/documents/development-loan-program-requirements.pdf). Because the funding program itself requires wages, the 1720(c)(5) affordable housing exemptions do not remove the requirement (1720(c)(5) applies unless otherwise required by a public funding program, https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).

program_name: Density Bonus and Incentive Procedure, Oakland Planning Code Chapter 17.107 (Ordinance 13684 C.M.S., 2022), and S-13 Affordable Housing Combining Zone
administering_agency: City of Oakland Planning and Building Department, Bureau of Planning
typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Implements Government Code 65915 with the state tables (20% to 50% bonus for 10% to 24% low income; 20% to 50% for 5% to 15% very low; 80% bonus for 100% affordable projects). Local additions: 100% affordable projects within one-half mile of a major transit stop may waive all density maximums and receive up to three additional stories or 33 feet; condominium conversions with 33% moderate or 15% lower income units get a 25% unit bonus or equivalent incentive; incentive counts of one, two, three or four follow state tiers; parking ratio reductions per 65915(p) and no parking required for qualifying transit-adjacent 100% affordable projects; incentives expressly exclude fee waivers and City land.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds (10% low, 5% very low, 10% moderate for sale, 100% affordable with up to 20% moderate); 55-year restriction for rental.
next_deadline: Submitted concurrently with the planning application; no deadline.
layering_notes: Oakland does not offer a local bonus above state law except the transit-adjacent height add for 100% affordable projects. Fee relief comes separately through the AHIF on-site exemption (Ch. 15.72), which was deliberately keyed to density bonus thresholds so a mixed-income project can satisfy both with one affordability mix. Code read on the zoneomics mirror because the City's codepublishing site blocks scripts.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this density bonus procedure (Planning Code 17.107) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City or County loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on the project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Prohousing Designation (renewed 2025, Resolution 90836 C.M.S.) and Prohousing Incentive Pilot Program grants
administering_agency: City of Oakland HCD, Housing Policy Unit
typical_award_size: Oakland was the first Bay Area jurisdiction designated Prohousing (December 2022); renewal for a 3-year term authorized September 16, 2025. Prohousing Incentive Program awards: $2,390,000 (Round 1, 2023) dedicated to capitalized service reserves for deeply affordable housing; Rounds 2 and 3 unsuccessful ($1,390,000 requests); Round 4 application for up to $1,600,000 authorized March 2026 for capitalized service reserves for PSH units in R2H2 or NC NOFA projects.
per_unit_cap: None; grants are sub-awarded to projects by HCD as grants or loans.
affordability_requirement: Capitalized service reserves for permanent supportive housing and deeply affordable units identified through City NOFAs.
next_deadline: HCD PIP Round 5 NOFA released October 13, 2026 (about $8 million statewide); applications due March 31, 2027, Prohousing Designation required by March 31, 2027, awards expected June 2027. Oakland Round 4 result not confirmed.
layering_notes: Developers benefit indirectly: Oakland projects receive Prohousing scoring points in AHSC, IIG, TCC and other state programs, and PIP dollars are routed to service reserves that make PSH projects feasible. Hayward and San Leandro also hold or expect Prohousing status. No county equivalent.
cycle_notes: State PIP rounds funded from SB 2 Building Homes and Jobs Trust Fund collections; Round 5 NOFA October 13, 2026 with March 31, 2027 due date.
prevailing_wage_basis: HCD Prohousing Incentive Program guidelines (Round 4 and October 2026 final guidelines) and the Round 4 and Round 5 NOFAs contain no prevailing wage provision. PIP funds pass to projects as City grants or loans for capitalized service reserves, so coverage depends on the general Labor Code 1720(b) public funds definition, 1720(c) exemptions (including 1720(c)(5)(E) for qualifying below-market loans) and project facts.
audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; PIP guidelines and NOFAs were searched and state no prevailing wage rule. Deadline updated from the HCD Round 5 NOFA.

program_name: Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF, Fund 2830), boomerang Affordable Housing Trust Fund (Fund 1870) and HOME program income authorizations (Resolution 90894 C.M.S., 2025)
administering_agency: City of Oakland HCD (housing successor to the Oakland Redevelopment Agency) and Community Development Division (HOME entitlement)
typical_award_size: Program income from residual receipts and payoffs: LMIHAF collected $5,634,227 (FY 2021-22), $5,820,444 (FY 2022-23), $2,132,775 (FY 2023-24) and $2,309,139 (FY 2024-25); HOME program income reallocated through the budget. October 2025 resolution authorized HCD to commit accumulated and future LMIHAF and HOME program income to NOFA pipeline projects without returning to Council, alongside an additional $40,000,000 of Measure U Tranche 2 and just under $30,000,000 from other sources. Boomerang Fund 1870 (former RDA residual property tax) seeded the R2H2 program and remains an eligible NOFA source for predevelopment, acquisition, new construction, operating subsidies and homeless prevention.
per_unit_cap: HOME per-unit subsidy limits apply to HOME-assisted units.
affordability_requirement: LMIHAF (Fund 2830): up to 80% AMI, at least 30% of units at or below 30% AMI and no more than 20% at 60% to 80% AMI (Health and Safety Code 34176.1); HOME: up to 80% AMI with at least 90% of rental units at or below 60% AMI and at least 20% at or below 50% AMI in rental projects of 5 or more units, HOME rents; boomerang AHTF funds: rental up to low income with priority for very low income, ownership assistance up to 120% AMI.
next_deadline: No separate application; funds are awarded within the NC NOFA, R2H2 RFP, ACAH and Rehab NOFA processes.
layering_notes: Oakland is a HOME participating jurisdiction and CDBG entitlement city in its own right (not in the Alameda County HOME Consortium), so its HOME dollars are separate from the County's consortium RFP recorded at county level. County boomerang funds (county record) and City boomerang Fund 1870 are distinct pots from the same RDA dissolution. These sources are the most flexible local money for predevelopment and operating subsidy where Measure U bond proceeds cannot be used.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: affordability_requirement changed from 'LMIHAF majority to 60% AMI and below; HOME 80% AMI and below; boomerang locally restricted to affordable housing' to the income rules in Attachment A of the September 2025 staff report: LMIHAF 30% minimum at 30% AMI and 20% maximum at 60-80% AMI, HOME 90% of rental units at 60% AMI and 20% at 50% AMI, boomerang rental up to low income with very low income priority. Program income figures and the $40,000,000 Measure U Tranche 2 allocation match.

program_name: Rehabilitation of Existing Affordable Housing NOFA (Rehab NOFA, planned 2027) and Health and Safety Rehabilitation Loan Program (Resolutions 86126, 86366, 89605 C.M.S.)
administering_agency: City of Oakland HCD, Asset Management Services unit
typical_award_size: Rehab NOFA: last issued FY 2019-20; $7,000,000 of Measure U Tranche 2 earmarked in 2024 and a competitive round planned for 2027 using already authorized Tranche 2 funds plus Tranche 3. Health and Safety Loan Program: over-the-counter emergency loans to owners of City-subsidized multifamily housing, generally up to $250,000 per project, 0% interest, 55-year term; balance fully committed ($250,000 Christian Church Homes, $100,000 Coliseum Connections) and a $2,000,000 recapitalization was recommended in October 2026.
per_unit_cap: Health and Safety loans generally limited to $250,000 per project.
affordability_requirement: Existing City-regulated affordable portfolio properties; affordability restrictions extended or maintained for 55 years.
next_deadline: Rehab NOFA expected 2027; Health and Safety Program accepting requests once the $2,000,000 recapitalization is funded. Verify with HCD Asset Management.
layering_notes: Covers Oakland's aging City-funded portfolio, the same need Berkeley addressed with its 2024 HTF rehab RFP. Larger recapitalizations pair with 4% credits and tax-exempt bonds (City of Oakland or CMFA conduit). Not a source for third-party acquisition; see ACAH.
cycle_notes: Rehab NOFA irregular; Health and Safety loans rolling when funded
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Oakland HCD Development Loan Program Requirements (Contract Compliance section) require City-funded projects to comply with Payment of Prevailing Wages and state that the general contractor must comply with Davis-Bacon if applicable and State of California prevailing wage as determined by DIR; City requirements apply regardless of fund source. https://oaklandca.prelive.opencities.com/files/assets/city/v/1/housing-comm-dev/documents/development-loan-program-requirements.pdf The 2019 Acquisition-Rehab-Preservation NOFA program description carries the same Contract Compliance requirement. https://cao-94612.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/NOFA-2019-Acquisition-Rehab-Preservation_Program-Description.pdf

program_name: Berkeley Housing Trust Fund (HTF) development, acquisition and predevelopment loans (BMC 21.28; 2021 HTF Guidelines; 2024 HTF RFP)
administering_agency: City of Berkeley Health, Housing and Community Services Department, Housing and Community Services Division, 2180 Milvia Street; housingdevelopment@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-5400
typical_award_size: Single application pools Measure O bond, inclusionary in-lieu and Affordable Housing Mitigation Fee revenue, Measure U1 general funds, HOME, PLHA and state pass-throughs. Current reservations: new construction $26,500,000 BUSD educator housing (110 units, Measure O), $11,996,669 1740 San Pablo (54 units), $11,996,669 St Paul Terrace (50), $14,531,301 Ephesian Legacy Court (80), $14,359,593 People's Park supportive housing (119), North Berkeley BART Lot B $11,563,636 plus EBALDC $5,926,364 plus Insight PSH $9,010,000 ($21,500,000 reserved); renovation $500,000 to $8,500,000. 2024 rehab RFP: about $5,800,000 available (including $1,200,000 HOME), $11,500,000 requested, awards $2,990,000 Adeline Street Apartments and $2,868,571 Ashby Lofts (June 2025). Standard terms: 55 years at 3% simple interest, annual payments from residual receipts; predevelopment loans 5 years at 3%. Fees: 1% origination, $600 subordination or assumption, $3,000 modification, $130 per hour project management.
per_unit_cap: City subsidy normally capped at 40% of total development cost (Guidelines IV.C.1, waivable); HOME per-unit limits apply to HOME-assisted units.
affordability_requirement: At least 60% of units restricted to households at or below 30% and 60% AMI (BUSD educator housing up to 120% AMI by waiver); 55-year minimum regulatory agreement; portion of units to Section 8 and Shelter Plus Care voucher holders; Berkeley housing preference policy applies to lottery units.
next_deadline: Predevelopment requests may be submitted any time; development funds released by RFP when Council allocates money (last new construction RFP 2019-2021 Measure O rounds, rehab RFP November 2024). No development RFP open as of 2026-11-08; Ashby BART East Lot developer selection underway (October 2026). Funding reservations expire after 24 months and were extended to January 2028 for SHiPP, Ephesian and NBB in late 2025.
layering_notes: Berkeley's HTF is the second largest city pool in the county and the gateway to Measure O, U1 and in-lieu revenue. Reservations above show how the City layers Measure O (capital only), AHMF or in-lieu fees and U1 (operating reserves and predevelopment, which Measure O cannot fund). Stacks with Alameda County Measure A1 Berkeley base allocation and regional pool, Measure W (Ephesian Legacy Court and People's Park won Measure W in March 2026), Berkeley Housing Authority project-based vouchers, and state LHTF match (City applied for NBB projects). HTF Guidelines require state prevailing wage on all City-funded construction and a First Source hiring agreement (BMC 13.26). FY 2026 budget deficit left no U1 available for unfunded rehab requests, so near-term capacity depends on in-lieu fee collections (about $9,000,000 a year average).
prevailing_wage_basis: Berkeley HTF and Small Sites Program Guidelines (2021), Labor Requirements item 2: funded projects must pay the State General Prevailing Rate of Per Diem Wages per Resolution 54,533-N.S. (1988), which requires State prevailing wage on all City-funded construction; HOME or CDBG funds may also trigger federal Davis-Bacon. https://berkeleyca.gov/sites/default/files/2021%20HTF-Approved-Guidelines%20for%20website.pdf
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: reservations, fees, 60% of units at 30%/60% AMI, 40% TDC cap and 55-year 3% terms match the HTF page and Guidelines. The page now shows Ashby Lofts at $3,718,571 (PLHA, contract pending) versus the $2,868,571 June 2025 award, and lists 2207 Haste Street ($500,000 PLHA). The Small Sites Program NOFA ($3,800,000) is open and tracked in record ba8d1a84de.

program_name: Small Sites Program (SSP) NOFA 2025, $3,800,000 (HTF subset, created 2018)
administering_agency: City of Berkeley Health, Housing and Community Services Department, Housing and Community Services Division, 2180 Milvia Street; housingdevelopment@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-5400
typical_award_size: $2,500,000 NOFA released August 18, 2025 and increased to $3,800,000; applications accepted on a rolling basis from August 25, 2025 and reviewed in order received (first three applications or twice the available funding). Three projects funded since 2018 under four NOFAs, including Bay Area Community Land Trust at 2627 California Street ($3,599,948 with U1 general funds) and Northern California Land Trust sites. No dedicated funding source; Council allocates by budget.
per_unit_cap: Maximum City subsidy per Small Sites Program guidelines (Exhibit D of the NOFA): $300,000 per unit for buildings of 10 to 25 units, $375,000 per unit for buildings of 2 to 9 units, or $175,000 per bedroom for group living or SRO housing; loan sized to need within these limits and not subject to the HTF 40% cap.
affordability_requirement: Acquisition and rehabilitation of rent-controlled or vacant multifamily rental buildings with 2 to 25 units under a 55-year loan and regulatory agreement; building-level average of 80% AMI (City may instead cap all incomes at 80% AMI); must accept Section 8 and Shelter Plus Care vouchers; 66% of existing households must income-certify and 75% agree to participate; requires a bank or CDFI loan; LIHTC projects not eligible; cooperatives subject to additional requirements (Exhibit H).
next_deadline: Rolling with no fixed deadline; still listed under Open funding opportunities on the Housing Trust Fund page as of November 8, 2026. Applications reviewed in order received until the $3,800,000 is committed; once three applications or twice the available funds are received, later applications are held, not actively reviewed.
layering_notes: Berkeley's analog to Oakland ACAH at much smaller scale. Pairs with the Bay Area Community Land Trust and Northern California Land Trust pipelines, county Measure A1 acquisition funds and private CDFI bridge debt. Over-the-counter approval by the City Manager, no Council action, so timing is fast relative to the HTF RFP. SSP projects follow HTF loan terms (55 years, 3% simple, residual receipts) and the City prevailing wage requirement.
cycle_notes: Small Sites Program NOFA released August 18, 2025 ($2,500,000, increased to $3,800,000); rolling intake since August 25, 2025. NOFA application document updated July 20, 2026; the August 3, 2026 date was only a suggested deadline for written questions, not an application deadline. Status list of applications posted on the HTF page.
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Berkeley SSP NOFA Application (updated July 20, 2026): All City-funded projects are required to pay California prevailing wages; construction pricing must be based on State prevailing wage. https://berkeleyca.gov/sites/default/files/2026%20Updated_November2026%20SSP%20NOFA%20Application%20and%20exhibits.pdf
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: per_unit_cap changed from 'no hard cap published' to the NOFA guideline maximums of $300,000 per unit (10-25 units), $375,000 per unit (2-9 units) and $175,000 per bedroom (group living or SRO). affordability_requirement now states the 80% AMI building average, 2 to 25 unit range, existing-tenant certification thresholds and required bank or CDFI loan, which the record omitted. Rolling status and $3,800,000 still listed as open on the HTF page.

program_name: Measure O Affordable Housing General Obligation Bond (November 2018, $135,000,000)
administering_agency: City of Berkeley HHCS with the Measure O Bond Oversight Committee and Housing Advisory Commission
typical_award_size: Voter-approved $135,000,000 GO bond (November 2018) for development, rehabilitation and preservation of affordable housing for extremely low through middle income households. The City has completed three of four planned issuances. First issuance about $30,000,000 (2019-20) funded Berkeley Way and 1601 Oxford and a 2019 HTF RFP of about $14,500,000. Completed projects include Jordan Court ($3,500,000), Berkeley Way (over $13,800,000) and The Grinnell ($7,300,000). In progress: BUSD workforce housing ($26,500,000, under construction since June 2025), St Paul Terrace ($12,000,000, under construction since April 2026), 1740 San Pablo ($7,500,000 Measure O). Council reserved $40,000,000 of Measure O for the BART sites: up to $20,000,000 for Ashby BART (still in planning) and $20,000,000 within a $26,500,000 City subsidy for North Berkeley BART. Supportive Housing in People's Park and Ephesian Legacy Court reservations will likely include some Measure O. Measure O cannot fund predevelopment or capitalized operating reserves, which the City covers with U1 or fee revenue.
per_unit_cap: None published; awards made through HTF RFPs.
affordability_requirement: HTF Guidelines (60% of units at or below 30% to 60% AMI) with Council-approved exceptions up to 120% AMI for BUSD educator housing; 55-year restrictions.
next_deadline: No open Measure O round as of November 9, 2026; remaining proceeds are reserved for pipeline projects (Ashby BART up to $20,000,000, North Berkeley BART, SHiPP, Ephesian Legacy Court). On February 10, 2026 Council extended the SHiPP, Ephesian and North Berkeley BART reservations for 24 months (to about February 2028). Verify unreserved balance with HHCS or the Measure O Bond Oversight Committee.
layering_notes: Measure O is Berkeley's counterpart to Oakland Measure U and County Measure A1; it is permanent capital only, so projects pair it with AHMF or in-lieu funds and U1 for predevelopment and reserves, Berkeley Housing Authority PBVs for operating support, and Measure A1 or Measure W for the balance. Oversight by the Measure O committee acts in place of the HAC for bond-funded RFPs. The 2019 Council report and the November 2025 HAC packet were the documents opened; a current bond balance statement was not found on berkeleyca.gov.
cycle_notes: remaining authorization reserved to named projects; new rounds only if reservations lapse
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Berkeley Housing Trust Fund and Small Sites Program Guidelines (2021), Labor Requirements item 2: funded projects must pay the General Prevailing Rate of Per Diem Wages (8 CCR 16000) to all workers covered by a State-published determination, per Resolution 54,533-N.S. (1988) requiring State prevailing wage on all City-funded construction; the guidelines note HTF projects are usually exempt from DIR registration under Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) but the City requirement still applies. https://berkeleyca.gov/sites/default/files/2021%20HTF-Approved-Guidelines%20for%20website_0.pdf Measure O bond capital is awarded through the HTF guidelines.
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: the record omitted the up to $20,000,000 Measure O reservation for Ashby BART and listed 1740 San Pablo at $11,996,669 (total City funds) where the City Measure O page shows $7,500,000 Measure O; reservation extension changed from January 2028 to about February 2028 (24 months from the February 10, 2026 resolution). The 2019 source report still supports the $135M authorization, first issuance and HTF affordability facts.

program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, BMC Chapter 23.328, and Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee (Resolution 71,674-N.S.; successor to the Affordable Housing Mitigation Fee, BMC 22.20.065)
administering_agency: City of Berkeley Planning and Development Department (compliance plans) and HHCS (BMR program and HTF)
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects over 5,000 sq ft of residential unit floor area must provide 20% of units as BMR (rental: half at 50% AMI, half low income, with Section 8 and Shelter Plus Care set-asides; ownership: all at 80% AMI) or pay an in-lieu fee of $62.83 per sq ft of residential unit floor area effective July 1, 2025 (up from $56.25; biennial California Construction Cost Index adjustment, next July 1, 2027), or a prorated mix. Full-fee payers deduct 5,000 sq ft (2,500 for single family); density bonus projects pay on the base project area. Fee due before certificate of occupancy. Revenue to the HTF: AHMF collections $3,112,000 (FY 2021), $16,208,000 (FY 2022), $14,224,000 (FY 2023), $10,716,000 (FY 2024), $831,000 (FY 2025); FY 2025 pipeline of 22 projects, 2,482 units, 214 BMR units and $22,600,000 projected fees. BMR portfolio 605 units in 61 properties.
affordability_requirement: 20% BMR for life of project (rental half at 50% AMI, half at 80% AMI; ownership at 80% AMI); projects with building permit or preliminary application before April 1, 2023 remain under the AHMF ordinance.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement (preliminary Affordable Housing Compliance Plan) and building permit (final AHCP); fee indexed July 1, 2027.
layering_notes: This fee is Berkeley's primary dedicated affordable housing revenue (about $9,000,000 a year average) and funds the HTF record above, so BMR unit production and fee collections move inversely. Revenue is lagging while the IHO pipeline moves from AHMF to IHO entitlements, which matters for near-term HTF capacity. Developers using the state density bonus must still meet the 20% inclusionary requirement; 23.330.070 ties qualifying bonus units to 23.328 standards. Compare Oakland's per-square-foot AHIF ($19.73 to $36.17) and Fremont's $44 per sq ft for-sale in-lieu fee.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Density Bonus, BMC Chapter 23.330 (Ordinance 7787-NS, 2021; 7853-NS, 2023)
administering_agency: City of Berkeley Planning and Development Department, Zoning Officer and Zoning Adjustments Board
typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Incorporates Government Code 65915 and 65917.2 by reference with administrative regulations; incentives and concessions counted per dimensional or quantitative standard; City bears the burden of proof to deny; waivers negotiated through Use Permit and Design Review; regulatory agreement required before certificate of occupancy; qualifying units must meet Chapter 23.328 standards.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds; bonus units count toward the base for the 20% inclusionary requirement only as provided in 23.328.
next_deadline: Concurrent with the housing development permit application; no deadline.
layering_notes: No local enhancement beyond state law; Berkeley's leverage for affordable projects is instead the Southside and transit-corridor rezonings and the Housing Element Program upzonings. Inclusionary in-lieu fee applies to the base project only, which modestly favors bonus projects. Code read on the zoneomics mirror because berkeley.municipal.codes is script-blocked.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Measure U1 general fund allocation to the Housing Trust Fund (2016 rental housing business license tax increase) and CHDO operating support
administering_agency: City of Berkeley HHCS; allocation set by City Council in the biennial budget
typical_award_size: Measure U1 raised the business license tax on rental property owners (2016) with the stated intent of funding affordable housing and homelessness programs; Council allocates a share to the HTF each budget. Recent U1 uses: California Street Apartments $3,599,948 (BALCT, with HTF), University Homes Homekey $8,500,000, 2321-2323 10th Street $3,324,225, MLK House $2,000,988, Ephesian Legacy Court (with Measure O and AHMF), capitalized operating reserves and predevelopment loans that Measure O cannot fund, and CHDO operating grants of up to $30,000 per organization per year FY 2026 to FY 2030 (with HOME). The HAC recommendation in 2025 to add U1 to the rehab RFP was withdrawn because the FY 2026 budget projected a deficit with limited U1 available.
affordability_requirement: When loaned through the HTF, HTF Guidelines apply: at least 60% of units rent restricted, with at least 20% of all units at or below 30% AMI and the remaining restricted units (about 40%) at or below 60% AMI, rents at TCAC limits; flexible general fund otherwise.
next_deadline: Dependent on the FY 2027-28 biennial budget; no set-aside guaranteed. Verify with HHCS.
layering_notes: U1 is the only Berkeley source usable for operating reserves and predevelopment, which makes it the critical complement to Measure O and county capital for PSH deals (Berkeley Way needed up to $14,000,000 in operating reserve until BHA project-based vouchers reduced it). Competes with homelessness services for the same general fund. Documented in the 2021 HTF Guidelines, the June 2025 RFP reservations report and the November 2025 HAC packet.
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Berkeley Housing Trust Fund and Small Sites Program Guidelines (2021), Labor Requirements item 2: funded projects must pay the General Prevailing Rate of Per Diem Wages (8 CCR 16000) to all workers covered by a State-published determination, per Resolution 54,533-N.S. (1988) requiring State prevailing wage on all City-funded construction; the guidelines note HTF projects are usually exempt from DIR registration under Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) but the City requirement still applies. https://berkeleyca.gov/sites/default/files/2021%20HTF-Approved-Guidelines%20for%20website_0.pdf U1 allocations are deployed through the Housing Trust Fund.
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: affordability_requirement changed from '60% of units at or below 30% to 60% AMI' to the HTF Guidelines rule of at least 60% restricted units with at least 20% of all units at or below 30% AMI and the rest at or below 60% AMI. U1 awards listed on the HTF page (California Street $3,599,948, University Homes $8,500,000, 10th Street $3,324,225, MLK House $2,000,988) match.

program_name: Fremont Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee Fund 196, Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund 111, commercial linkage fees)
administering_agency: City of Fremont Community Development Department, Housing Division, 39550 Liberty Street; housing@fremont.gov, (510) 494-4500
typical_award_size: Periodic NOFAs: November 2021 round awarded $14,000,000 to MidPen (Osgood, with up to $11,500,000 more), $6,000,000 to TPC/Maracor (Osgood South) and $7,600,000 to RCD (3900 Thornton, with up to $9,700,000 more). August 2023 NOFA (about $30,000,000 estimated, $35,000,000 available) awarded $34,850,000 on March 19, 2024: $12,850,000 USA Properties Centerville Station Phase 1 (150 units; $8,850,000 Fund 196 plus $4,000,000 Fund 111), $12,000,000 TPC/Maracor Warm Springs (240 units, $50,000 per unit; $9,500,000 redirected to acquisition in March 2025), $10,000,000 Community Development Partners 39340 Fremont Blvd (96 units, $104,000 per unit). Loans are 55 years at 3% simple interest, capital and predevelopment only (no operating subsidy or services). City contributed $30,700,000 of restricted funds to the 560 units opened in 2025 and funded four of the six developments (918 units) breaking ground in fall 2026.
per_unit_cap: No formal cap; staff benchmark recent City subsidy at about $110,000 per unit and favored requests of $50,000 to $104,000 per unit.
affordability_requirement: Households at or below 80% AMI with a target mix including extremely low (under 30% AMI), very low (under 50% AMI) and low income units; all-electric construction; site control required at application; 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: No NOFA open as of 2026-11-08; prior rounds were 2021 and August 2023 (due October 31, 2023). Next round expected when Fund 196 rebuilds; verify with the Housing Division.
layering_notes: Second largest city pool in the county after Oakland and Berkeley, funded almost entirely by developer fees (for-sale in-lieu fee, rental AHO fee, commercial linkage) plus LMIHAF program income. Awards are timed so projects can apply to CDLAC/TCAC (Warm Springs waited for enhanced credits in a Small DDA). Stacks with Alameda County Measure A1 Fremont base allocation and regional pool, Measure W, and HACA project-based vouchers (Fremont is in the HACA jurisdiction and the County HOME Consortium). fremont.gov returns 403 to scripts, so the NOFA page could not be opened; terms were read from the March 19, 2024 and March 18, 2025 Council staff reports on the City's IQM2 agenda host and City GovDelivery bulletins.
cycle_notes: NOFA issued roughly every two years as fund balance allows
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The Fremont NOFA (fremont.gov) returns 403 and the 2024 award resolutions on the City IQM2 host carry no wage term. Below-market loans to projects with 40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) unless the program requires prevailing wage, and LMIHAF-only work may fall under 1720(c)(4).
audit_note: PW pass Nov 9, 2026: true not supported by a located program rule; Fremont NOFA text could not be opened (403), so changed to unclear pending the NOFA.

program_name: Fremont Affordable Housing Ordinance, FMC Chapter 18.155 (2021 update, effective 2022) with in-lieu fees and live/work preference (2022)
administering_agency: City of Fremont Community Development Department, Housing Division and Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. October 12, 2021 update: for-sale projects 15% inclusionary (5% moderate, 10% low) or in-lieu fee phased to $44 per sq ft by January 2024 (stacked flat rates unchanged); rental projects 10% low income or an alternative of 7.5% low plus 7.5% very low (15%); hybrid option of on-site moderate units plus partial fee; mixed for-sale and rental projects may satisfy the obligation with affordable rental units. Rental in-lieu fee and the separate commercial linkage (jobs-housing) fee remained unchanged. Fee revenue goes to Fund 196 and funds the Affordable Housing Fund NOFA. New affordable housing processing fees for BMP resales, refinances and loan modifications were adopted January 2026.
affordability_requirement: For-sale 15% (5% moderate, 10% low); rental 10% low or 15% split low and very low; long-term affordability agreements with the City.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; fee set by the Master Fee Schedule (updated January 5, 2026). Verify current per-square-foot amounts with the Housing Division.
layering_notes: Fremont is the only priority city in the county besides Oakland with both a residential inclusionary fee and a commercial linkage fee, which is why Fund 196 could support $34,850,000 of awards in 2024. The ordinance text (FMC 18.155) on fremont.gov and the code publisher are script-blocked; summary read from the City's 2021 GovDelivery notice and the November 2025 Master Fee Schedule staff report on IQM2. 2021 fee increase phasing and any 2024 to 2026 indexing should be confirmed.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this inclusionary ordinance (FMC 18.155) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City or County loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on the project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720 In-lieu fees collected under it are deployed through the separate Affordable Housing Fund NOFA.

program_name: State Density Bonus Law implementation in Fremont (no local bonus chapter; Lopes Road determination, November 2025)
administering_agency: City of Fremont Community Development Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Fremont applies Government Code 65915 directly; all three 2024 NOFA awardees used concessions or waivers to reduce ground-floor commercial, open space or setbacks in TC-P, WSI-8 and Downtown zones, and AB 2097 removed parking minimums near transit. In November 2025 the Council upheld staff and Planning Commission denial of a concession to reduce the 50 unit per acre minimum density for a 127-townhome project at Lopes Road near Warm Springs BART, consistent with an HCD technical assistance letter. Commercial density bonus (Gov Code 65915.7) is available but unused.
affordability_requirement: State thresholds (10% low, 5% very low, 10% moderate for sale, 100% affordable).
next_deadline: Concurrent with the entitlement application.
layering_notes: No local enhancement; the City's incentives for affordable projects are fee based. Fremont adopted a development impact fee deferral and a 50% impact fee reduction for affordable housing projects under FMC 18.290 (2021 and later actions) according to City notices, but the fremont.gov pages describing them were blocked (403) this pass and the zoneomics 18.290 text defines affordable housing (up to 120% AMI) without stating the reduction; treat the fee reduction as needs_confirmation. Fremont also adopted a Streamlined Affordable Housing overlay through Housing Element Program implementation ordinances in 2025 (PLN2025-00065 and PLN2025-00074) that were not opened.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Development impact fee reduction and deferral for affordable housing projects, FMC Chapter 18.290
administering_agency: City of Fremont Community Development Department, Building and Housing Divisions
typical_award_size: 50% reduction of three development impact fees (Parkland Acquisition, Park Facilities and Transportation/Traffic) for qualifying deed-restricted affordable housing units, adopted with the 2021 Comprehensive Development Impact Fee Update (Council item June 1, 2021, effective August 2, 2021 or 60 days after adoption). Capital Facilities and Fire Facilities fees are paid at the full rate. Staff estimated the reduction at about $9 million of CIP funding ($7 million parks, $2 million transportation). The FY 2024-25 Development Impact Fee Annual and Five-Year Report (December 9, 2025) fee schedule still carries the 50% rate (note 6). A separate City affordable housing fee deferral program was not confirmed in these documents; state law deferral (Government Code 66007) still applies.
per_unit_cap: Not applicable; 50% of the per-unit Parkland, Park Facilities and Traffic fee rates for each qualifying deed-restricted unit.
affordability_requirement: Applies per deed-restricted unit (the project does not need to be 100% affordable). Deed-restricted affordable housing means units whose deed restricts occupancy by maximum income, in no case above moderate income as defined in FMC 18.155.020 (generally 120% AMI).
next_deadline: No deadline; reduced rates apply when impact fees are paid at building permit.
layering_notes: Fee relief stacks with Fund 196 loans and state fee deferral; school (FUSD), water (ACWD) and sewer (USD) fees are outside the City resolution. Alameda County has no countywide fee waiver (county record). fremont.gov returns 403; the 2021 staff report, implementing resolution and the 2025 fee report were read on fremontcityca.iqm2.com.
cycle_notes: Rolling. Rates set by the 2021 implementing resolution and adjusted annually by construction cost index.
eligible_project_detail: new construction with deed-restricted affordable units
mixed-income projects (reduction applies to the deed-restricted units)
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: earlier text overstated the relief as a 50% cut of all impact fees under FMC 18.290 at 120% AMI. The 2021 implementing resolution (IQM2 item 4360, Exhibit A-1 note 6) limits the 50% reduction to Parkland, Park Facilities and Traffic fees for deed-restricted units up to moderate income; the 2025 fee report confirms it is still in effect. City fee deferral program not found.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule is recorded for this program; the 2021 implementing resolution and staff report contain no wage term. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees reduced or waived by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.

program_name: Fremont CDBG entitlement and HOME Consortium allocations (FY 2025/26 to 2029/30 Consolidated Plan)
administering_agency: City of Fremont Human Services Department (CDBG and ESG) and Housing Division; HOME through the Alameda County HOME Consortium
typical_award_size: FY 2025/26 CDBG: entitlement $1,579,819 plus $121,143 program income and $408,685 reprogrammed funds, total $2,109,647; about $1,008,291 available for capital projects. FY 2025/26 capital awards ranged from $50,000 to $465,280 (MidPen Century Village rehabilitation $465,280). ESG entitlement $146,207. Fremont also receives a formula share of the Alameda County HOME Consortium allocation; the HOME dollar amount was not stated in the staff report.
affordability_requirement: CDBG: low and moderate income benefit (80% AMI); HOME: 80% AMI with HOME rents, 15 to 20 year federal affordability plus City regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Based on the FY 2025/26 schedule, the next CDBG capital proposal round is expected to open in winter with proposals due around February 2027; confirm with Human Services.
layering_notes: Small relative to Fund 196 but useful for acquisition and rehab. The County's HOME Consortium RFP (county record) is the vehicle for larger HOME development loans; the County proposed centralizing HOME administration for FY 2027-2029, which may change how Fremont's share is awarded. Source is the July 8, 2025 Council agenda on IQM2 listing the Consolidated Plan hearing; the staff report itself was not opened.
cycle_notes: CDBG and ESG are allocated in two-year funding cycles with an annual capital proposal round. FY 2025/26 round: proposal workshop January 9, 2025, proposals due February 6, 2025, Citizens Advisory Committee recommendations March 27, 2025, Council adoption July 8, 2025. RFP advertised in the newspaper, City web page and cable channel.
audit_note: Staff report for the July 8, 2025 Consolidated Plan hearing opened and read November 8, 2026. HOME share amount still unconfirmed.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: Hayward Affordable Housing Ordinance (HMC Chapter 10, Article 17; Ordinance 17-20, amended April 11, 2023), in-lieu fees (Resolution 17-167 as amended 2023) and Affordable Housing Trust Fund
administering_agency: City of Hayward Development Services Department, Housing Division, 777 B Street, Hayward; housing@hayward-ca.gov, (510) 583-4454
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to all projects of two or more net new units: on-site units, in-lieu fee, off-site units or alternatives. In-lieu fees (10 or more units, per sq ft of habitable space, 2023 schedule): high-density condominiums 35 units per acre or more $19.35; lower-density ownership under 35 units per acre $26.00; all other dwelling types including rental $23.46; plus 10% if paid at occupancy; projects of 2 to 9 units pay 50% to 89% of the calculated fee. Fees fund the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, used solely to increase and preserve housing for extremely low to moderate income households (land acquisition and development subsidies). Collections 2020 to mid-2026 total $8,926,851: $3,599,171 (2020), $2,193,532 (2021), $2,013,770 (2022), $199,507 (2023), $489,948 (2024), $378,237 (2025), $52,687 (2026 YTD).
affordability_requirement: 2023 amended AHO (Ordinance adopted April 11, 2023): on-site ownership units 7.5% of units at moderate income for high-density condominiums (35 units per acre or more) and 12% for other ownership projects (half moderate, half low income; 10% moderate for plans pending before the amendment); on-site rental units 6% of units, half low income and half very low income, first unit very low income; affordable units restricted in perpetuity; local tenant preference policy in 10-17.805.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; fee per the annual Master Fee Schedule (FY 2027 schedule adopted June 2026). Verify current indexed amounts with the Housing Division.
layering_notes: Hayward's trust fund is small and shrinking because most recent developments provided on-site units rather than paying fees (City's December 2024 competitiveness analysis), so the City lacks local match for state applications. The AHO text on municode is script-blocked; requirements were read from the City's affordable housing page, Resolution 17-167 and the 2023 in-lieu fee resolution on Hayward Legistar. Compare Fremont ($44 per sq ft for-sale) and Berkeley ($62.83).
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: on-site percentages and term taken from the AHO text attached to the March 2023 introduction (PH 23-016, Attachment III), adopted April 11, 2023 per Legistar CONS 23-186 and the City page. In-lieu rates ($19.35, $26.00, $23.46 per sq ft, plus 10% at occupancy) and 2020 to 2026 collections match. The 2 to 9 unit fee reduction was not re-read.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this inclusionary ordinance provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City or County loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on the project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Hayward Affordable Housing NOFA (local housing funds with Alameda County Measure A1 base allocation; last round 2018)
administering_agency: City of Hayward Development Services Department, Housing Division, 777 B Street, Hayward; housing@hayward-ca.gov, (510) 583-4454
typical_award_size: 2018 NOFA: about $7,000,000 in local housing funds plus recommendations for Hayward's Measure A1 base allocation ($18,200,000 available at the time) and local match to position projects for the A1 regional pool. Maximum City loan 10% of total residential development cost of the affordable units; HOME per-unit limits for HOME-assisted units ($144,050 studio to $285,149 four bedroom in 2018); 24-month commitment with one-year extension. CDBG available for predevelopment or acquisition by request. No NOFA has been issued since; the City reports only one City-supported project remaining in the pipeline and limited general fund for housing.
per_unit_cap: City loan capped at 10% of the affordable units' total development cost (2018 terms).
affordability_requirement: Rental and supportive housing for lower income households; Measure A1 policies require at least 20% of units at 20% AMI for A1-funded projects; scoring favors special needs, homeless, larger units and deeper targeting.
next_deadline: No open NOFA as of 2026-11-08. The December 2024 Housing Policy and Resource Committee report floated an annual general fund allocation for a regular NOFA but no funding was identified. Watch the Doing Business with Hayward page and the Housing Division mailing list.
layering_notes: Hayward's role is mainly as pass-through for its Measure A1 base allocation (county record) and HOME Consortium share; local dollars are limited to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund balance and CDBG. Developers should expect to rely on Measure A1, Measure W, HACA project-based vouchers and state sources with the City providing land (surplus sites), entitlements under the Streamlined Affordable Housing Overlay, and its Prohousing designation points. NOFA page and 2018 program description were opened on hayward-ca.gov.
prevailing_wage_basis: City of Hayward 2018 Affordable Housing NOFA Program Description: the general contractor must comply with Davis-Bacon if applicable and State of California prevailing wage as determined by DIR; projects with federal funds pay the higher of federal or state rates; Measure A1 funded projects also follow County contracting requirements. https://hayward-ca.gov/sites/default/files/NOFA%202018%20%20Program%20Description%20-UPDATED%205.22.18.pdf

program_name: Streamlined Affordable Housing Overlay District, HMC Section 10-1.2650 (Ordinance 24-04, April 2, 2024)
administering_agency: City of Hayward Development Services Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Entitlement streamlining, not a subsidy. Ministerial site plan and tentative map approval for housing on sites carried over from prior housing element cycles and listed in the 6th Cycle Housing Element lower-income inventory, provided the project meets the Housing Element minimum density assumptions and at least 20% of units are deed restricted for extremely low, very low or low income households for 55 years (rental) or 45 years (ownership); site must not meet Gov Code 65913.4(a)(6) exclusion criteria; objective standards and standard conditions apply.
affordability_requirement: At least 20% of units at low income or below, 55-year rental or 45-year ownership restriction.
next_deadline: Ministerial application any time; approval lapses per 10-1.2690.
layering_notes: Hayward has no local density bonus chapter; state density bonus requests are processed with site plan review (recent approvals include townhome projects with 10% to 11% affordable units). The overlay lowers entitlement risk on the inventory sites and pairs with state SB 35/SB 423 streamlining. Fee relief for affordable projects is not offered by the City. Code read on the zoneomics mirror because municode is blocked.

Any City or County loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on the project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: HOME Investment Partnerships funds through the Alameda County HOME Consortium and CDBG entitlement (Cooperation Agreement FY 2027-2029)
administering_agency: City of Hayward Development Services Department, Housing Division; Alameda County HCD as Consortium lead
typical_award_size: Hayward has received over $15,000,000 in HOME funds since 1991 as a Consortium member (annual formula share), used for Glenn Berry, Sara Conner Court, Huntwood Commons, Tennyson Gardens, Leidig Court, Cypress Glen, Weinreb Place, Alta Mira and Mission Paradise, plus Project Independence tenant-based rental assistance ($500,000 renewed July 2026). affordability_requirement: 100% of HOME funds to households at or below 80% AMI with HOME rent limits; federal affordability period plus City regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: FY 2027 allocation set spring 2026; future allocations may be awarded through the County's HOME Consortium RFP (county record) under the centralized model. Verify with the Housing Division.
layering_notes: Small annual amounts (several hundred thousand dollars) but the only recurring development money Hayward controls. Pairs with the County HOME Consortium RFP, Measure A1 and HACA PBVs. prevailing_wage_basis: HOME: federal Davis-Bacon applies to projects with 12 or more HOME-assisted units (24 CFR 92.354). CDBG: Davis-Bacon applies to residential projects with 8 or more units (HCD Act section 110).
