County HCDS NOFAs normally exclude City of San Diego projects, so this and the SDHC AHF are the local layers. Prohousing: City designation (November 2022) lapsed January 2026 and renewal is pending (separate record).
cycle_notes: One to two rounds per year. Round 7 ran February 3 to April 6, 2026; Round 8 ran August 31 to October 19, 2026 ($15M: $10M LMIHAF, $5M PLHA).
prevailing_wage_basis: San Diego Municipal Code 22.3019 as written into City loan documents in the Bridge to Home Round 8 NOFA (August 31, 2026, NOFA page 6): the project is subject to state prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720 to 1861 for construction work over $25,000 and alteration, demolition, repair or maintenance work over $15,000, unless it qualifies for the Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption, and the City accepts no alternative language. Federal Davis-Bacon also applies where CDBG (8 or more units, 42 U.S.C. 5310) or HOME (12 or more HOME-assisted units, 24 CFR 92.354) is in the deal. https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/bth-8-round-nofa_final-for-posting.pdf
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: Award, AMI, cycle and deadline match the Bridge to Home page and Round 8 NOFA ($15M: $10M LMIHAF for new construction at 30 to 60 percent AMI, $5M PLHA for 30 percent AMI homeless units; due October 19, 2026; notice to successful applicants December 2026, Council consideration March to July 2027). Prevailing wage basis corrected: old basis cited only HOME and CDBG federal thresholds, which are not Round 8 sources; new basis cites the City's SDMC 22.3019 loan clause stated in the Round 8 NOFA. Trigger stays true.

program_name: Inclusionary Affordable Housing Regulations and Inclusionary In Lieu Fee (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 2, Division 13; O-21167 as amended through O-22109)
administering_agency: San Diego Housing Commission (administration, monitoring and Inclusionary Housing Fund; Genevieve Hernandez, genevieveh@sdhc.org, (619) 578-7588) and City Development Services Department (DS-530 checklist, fee collection)
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to residential development of 10 or more units outside the Coastal Overlay Zone, 5 or more units inside the Coastal Overlay Zone, and condominium conversions of 2 or more units (SDMC 142.1302). Rental: at least 10 percent of total units for very low or low income households at rents not exceeding 30 percent of 60 percent of AMI (fully effective July 1, 2024). For-sale: 10 percent at median income (100 percent AMI) or 15 percent at moderate income (120 percent AMI). In lieu fee $25.00 per square foot of net building area of unrestricted market-rate units effective July 1, 2024, updated annually by the ENR Los Angeles Construction Cost Index ($12.73 for projects deemed complete before July 1, 2020). Other compliance: off-site units, rehabilitation or conversion of existing units, SRO or hotel rooms to 55-year affordable units, land donation. North City Future Urbanizing Area projects are exempt from this Division and follow the Framework Plan inclusionary requirement (20 percent). IHF fee revenue FY25 $17.76M (255 percent above budget); FY27 projected new IHF revenue $4.04M.
affordability_requirement: Rental inclusionary units restricted at least 55 years; on-site affordable units count toward state density bonus; developments restricted at or below 80 percent AMI by agreement are exempt.
next_deadline: Applies at permit. The fee rate is set when the development permit, subdivision or building permit application is deemed complete (whichever is earliest) and is paid on or before the first residential building permit (SDMC 142.1306). Division 13 was amended June 15, 2026 by O-22109 (effective July 15, 2026, not yet effective in the Coastal Overlay Zone); Information Bulletin 532 revised August 2026.
layering_notes: Fees feed the Inclusionary Housing Fund, the larger of the two Affordable Housing Fund accounts (about $30.7M projected balance entering FY27) and the main source of the SDHC NOFA (record above). Projects that pay the fee are not eligible for the Affordable Housing Expedite Program; projects providing on-site units get expedite processing and may stack state density bonus and Complete Communities Housing Solutions FAR bonuses. Compare Chula Vista (10 percent at 20 or more units), Carlsbad (15 percent at 7 or more units) and Oceanside (15 percent at 3 or more units); the unincorporated County ordinance is a separate county record. Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov and the SDHC inclusionary page.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and mixed-use projects of 10 or more units (compliance)
audit_note: Nov 9, 2026 spot check: applicability thresholds (5 or more units in the Coastal Overlay Zone, condominium conversions of 2 or more units) and fee rate lock timing corrected from the September 2026 code PDF; the fee is CCI-indexed, so the current rate may exceed $25.00.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Housing Impact Fee (commercial linkage fee) funding the San Diego Housing Trust Fund (SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 6)
administering_agency: City of San Diego Facilities Financing (calculation) and Development Services Department (collection); San Diego Housing Commission administers the resulting Housing Trust Fund
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Charged per square foot on new office, hotel, research and development, retail and other commercial development; the 2014 compromise ordinance (adopted November 10, 2014) phased rates to $2.12 per square foot for office, $1.28 for hotel and retail, and $0.80 for research and development, with exemptions for manufacturing, warehouse and certain Enterprise Zone uses and an option to dedicate land in lieu of the fee. Revenue: FY25 collections $1.78M (39 percent above budget); FY27 projected $1.36M in new HTF revenue; projected HTF balance $6.38M entering FY27.
affordability_requirement: Fee revenue must serve very low, low and median income households (at least 60 percent of HTF to very low income).
next_deadline: Paid at building permit. SDHC adopts the Affordable Housing Fund Annual Plan each spring; FY27 plan allocated $2.5M of HTF to the FY27 NOFA and $150,000 to transitional housing grants.
layering_notes: The HTF has been a declining share of SDHC's local money; the Inclusionary Housing Fund is now about five times larger. HTF money is the most flexible local source (loans, grants, indirect assistance) and is used for the SDHC NOFA, homeless housing grants and administration. No comparable city linkage fee exists in Chula Vista, Oceanside, Escondido or Carlsbad (Carlsbad's trust fund collects housing impact fees under a different code section). Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov; the current fee amount should be confirmed with Facilities Financing because the code table shows the 2014 phase-in schedule.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: SDHC Multifamily Housing Revenue Bond Program (Housing Authority of the City of San Diego conduit bonds, Policy 300.301)
administering_agency: San Diego Housing Commission, Real Estate Division, Multifamily Housing Bond Program, 1122 Broadway, Suite 300, San Diego 92101; Colin Miller, (619) 578-7429, colinm@sdhc.org; MultifamilyBondProgram@sdhc.org
typical_award_size: Conduit tax-exempt private activity bonds sized to project debt; no City or SDHC liability. Application: Bond Inducement Application (DocuSign), $3,000 application fee and $10,000 deposit (refunded at closing, when issuer and ongoing administrative fees apply), plus notarized Developer Disclosure Statement. Issuances since 1982; program policy enacted 1989.
affordability_requirement: At least 20 percent of units at or below 50 percent AMI or 40 percent at or below 60 percent AMI; 55 year affordability; 95 percent of proceeds to capital costs.
next_deadline: Rolling; inducement must precede the CDLAC application rounds (CDLAC calendar sets the practical deadlines). Housing Authority (City Council) approval required for issuance.
layering_notes: SDHC is the issuer of choice inside the City; CMFA and CSCDA issuances are also used with City TEFRA approval (County TEFRA practice is a separate county record). Pairs with 4 percent LIHTC and the SDHC AHF NOFA and Bridge to Home loans. Chula Vista's Housing Authority now acts as issuer in most cases within that city (separate record); Oceanside has issued only occasionally (last 2016); Escondido and Carlsbad rely on JPAs.
prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village and PW 2006-005 Central Village Apartments, holds that loans of tax-exempt conduit bond proceeds for affordable housing, whether publicly offered or privately placed, are not a payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4), because the proceeds and repayments never enter public coffers; reaffirmed in PW 2010-008 and PW 2015-008. Bond financing alone does not trigger state prevailing wage; other public funds in the same deal (city or county loans, fee waivers, land) are tested separately, and federal sources such as HOME or 9+ PBVs carry their own Davis-Bacon rules. https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf

program_name: Complete Communities Housing Solutions (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 3, Division 10): FAR bonus, Development Impact Fee waiver and Neighborhood Enhancement Fee
administering_agency: City of San Diego Development Services Department and City Planning Department; SDHC reviews affordable unit compliance
typical_award_size: Optional incentive program within Sustainable Development Areas (sites zoned or designated for 20 or more units per acre, or within one-quarter mile of a rail station; SDMC 143.1002) replacing density limits with floor area ratio tiers (Tier 1 Downtown no FAR maximum, Tier 2 FAR 8.0, Tier 3 FAR 6.5, Tier 4 FAR 4.0, plus 1.5 FAR for family-sized units). Required (143.1015(a)): rental projects must restrict, excluding bonus units, 15 percent of units at 50 percent AMI rents plus 10 percent at 60 percent AMI plus 15 percent at 120 percent AMI (40 percent total), or alternatively 40 percent at 50 percent AMI, 100 percent at 60 percent AMI, or 100 percent moderate (half at 80 percent AMI, half at 120 percent AMI); for-sale tiers are in 143.1016; naturally affordable units must be replaced. Section 143.1010(f): waiver of Development Impact Fees for all covenant restricted affordable units, up to 30 percent of units of 500 square feet or less (if at least 10 percent are three bedroom units), and three bedroom units restricted at or below 150 percent AMI, when the project reaches at least 120 percent of base maximum density. Neighborhood Enhancement Fee (Resolution R-313282; about $9.00 per square foot of lot area per the program page) or a public space on sites of 25,000 square feet or more; the fee is waived only when 100 percent of units (excluding managers units) are restricted at or below 50 percent AMI (143.1010(g)). Permitting: 1,917 homes in 2024 and 3,372 homes 2021 to 2024.
affordability_requirement: Deed restricted on-site units for very low, low and moderate income households (up to 120 percent AMI) for 55 years; right to return and priority preference (75 percent of affordable units) for Communities of Concern residents.
next_deadline: Ministerial review; January 10, 2024 executive order requires departmental review within 30 days. The 2026 Land Development Code update (adopted mid 2026) adjusted FAR bonuses and DIF provisions; verify current 143.1010 text before relying on the waiver.
layering_notes: Can be combined with the inclusionary requirement (the required units satisfy both) but not with the state density bonus on the same project in most cases; developers choose Complete Communities or the Affordable Housing Density Bonus (separate record). DIF waiver is a City fee waiver and may be treated as public funds for Labor Code 1720 purposes; confirm with DIR. Expedite Program and Affordable Housing Permit Now apply to qualifying projects. Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov; program page on sandiego.gov/complete-communities.
prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule is recorded for this program. Complete Communities includes a Development Impact Fee waiver; the FAR bonus itself provides no public funds (1720(a)(1)). Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived or forgiven by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: Checked SDMC Chapter 14, Article 3, Division 10 (9-2026 edition). Old: affordable set-aside described as 15 percent at 50 percent AMI, or 10 percent at 60 percent AMI plus 15 percent at 120 percent AMI, per FAR tier; new: 15 percent at 50 plus 10 percent at 60 plus 15 percent at 120 percent AMI (40 percent total) or one of three alternatives, per 143.1015(a). Old: Neighborhood Enhancement Fee waived for the 50 percent AMI tier; new: waived only when 100 percent of units are restricted at or below 50 percent AMI (143.1010(g)). Geography updated from Transit Priority Areas to Sustainable Development Areas. The $9.00 rate is set by resolution and was not re-read in the code.

program_name: Affordable Housing Density Bonus Regulations (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 3, Division 7) and ADU Home Density Bonus Program
administering_agency: San Diego Housing Commission (density bonus affordable unit review; Genevieve Hernandez, (619) 578-7588) and City Development Services Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to developments of five or more units. Local enhancements adopted March 6, 2018 (Housing SD): 10 percent density bonus for projects within the permitted building footprint, incentives or waivers available without requesting a bonus, 100 percent density bonus for micro-units within the footprint, and bonuses for sites with existing or recently expired rent restricted units. State bonuses up to 50 percent (80 percent or unlimited for 100 percent affordable) apply. ADU Home Density Bonus (SDMC 141.0302(d)): within a Sustainable Development Area one bonus ADU for each deed restricted affordable ADU with no fixed cap; outside a Sustainable Development Area a maximum of one bonus ADU and one affordable ADU; not available in RS-1-1 to RS-1-4 and RS-1-8 to RS-1-11 zones unless the site is High or Highest Resource and designated Residential; a Community Enhancement Fee applies. Permitting: 2,619 homes under the density bonus in 2024 (8,726 in 2021 to 2024); 653 ADUs under the ADU bonus in 2024 (892 in 2021 to 2024, 41 percent affordable). SDHC charges land use application fees (adjusted November 1, 2025).
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 tiers (5 percent very low, 10 percent low, 10 percent moderate for-sale, senior, 100 percent affordable); 55 years for rental units. ADU Home Density Bonus affordable ADUs: at least 10 years at very low income (rent at 30 percent of 50 percent AMI) or low income (30 percent of 60 percent AMI), or at least 15 years at moderate income (30 percent of 110 percent AMI) (SDMC 141.0302(d)).
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; density bonus and ADU bonus regulations were amended in 2025 (O-21989) and the 2026 Land Development Code update; coastal zone versions lag Coastal Commission certification.
layering_notes: Developers choose between this and Complete Communities Housing Solutions (separate record). 100 percent affordable projects also get the Affordable Housing Expedite Program and Permit Now processing (separate record) and may use the Division 10 DIF waiver only if they elect Complete Communities. SDHC reviews affordability agreements for all programs and records them. Chula Vista, Oceanside, Escondido and Carlsbad ordinances simply conform to state law without these local enhancements. Read on sdhc.org (density bonus and ADU pages) and the City's 2025 Annual Report on Homes.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: SDHC density bonus page matches the 2018 local enhancements. ADU bonus checked in SDMC 141.0302(d) (9-2026 edition). Old: ADU bonus units restricted 15 years at moderate or low income, unlimited in TPAs; new: 10 years for very low or low income, 15 years for moderate income at 110 percent AMI; unlimited only within Sustainable Development Areas, one bonus ADU maximum outside them, and excluded from most RS-1 zones.

program_name: Affordable, In-Fill Housing and Sustainable Buildings Expedite Program (Information Bulletin 538, Council Policy 600-27, SDMC 143.0915) and Affordable Housing Permit Now (Executive Order 2023-1)
administering_agency: City of San Diego Development Services Department, Expedite Team (DSD-ExpediteProgram@sandiego.gov) and Ministerial Project Managers (DSDMinisterialPM@sandiego.gov)
typical_award_size: Expedite program fees are waived for 100 percent affordable projects (otherwise fees per IB-503, capped at 40 percent of staff hourly billings). Discretionary review cycles cut to about half of standard (20 business day first review, 10 day subsequent reviews, completeness check in 5 days); ministerial expedite goal 25 percent faster. Permit Now: first review of 100 percent affordable and shelter building and engineering permits within 30 business days, dedicated project managers, collaborative review meetings; 26 projects completed by July 2026 and 3,094 homes permitted 2023 to 2024. Expedite program 2018 to 2024: 435 projects, 3,490 homes. Section 143.0920 allows deviations through a Process Two Neighborhood Development Permit.
affordability_requirement: Eligibility: 10 or more units with at least 10 percent at or below 60 percent AMI (rental) or 100 percent AMI (for-sale, or 15 percent at 120 percent AMI); SDHC-funded projects with 15 percent at 120 percent AMI; projects restricted at or below 80 percent AMI by public agreement; infill projects in Transit Priority Areas with all units at or below 150 percent AMI; Promise Zone projects. Projects paying the inclusionary fee are not eligible.
next_deadline: Rolling; request eligibility confirmation by email before submittal. IB 538 dated March 2023; Permit Now 3-year progress report issued March 2026.
layering_notes: Processing benefit rather than cash, but the fee waiver and timeline savings matter for TCAC readiness deadlines. Stack with the SDHC AHF NOFA, Bridge to Home and Complete Communities. Mandatory Initial Review is required for discretionary expedite projects. No comparable formal expedite program was found for Chula Vista, Oceanside or Carlsbad; Escondido offers pre-application consultation and expedited review under Housing Element Program 2.8.
prevailing_wage_basis: IB 538 Section IV.B states the City waives expedite program fees for 100% affordable housing projects (and for retail or commercial with 100% affordable housing on site); other eligible projects pay the expedite fee in IB-503. A waived fee is a form of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (fees normally required that are waived or forgiven by a political subdivision), so the 100% affordable path can count toward public funding unless the subsidy is de minimis under 1720(c)(3) or another 1720(c) exemption applies. Mixed-income projects that pay the expedite fee receive processing priority only, which is not a 1720(b) form of public funds. https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletins/538 and https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: IB 538 reread. The Nov 9 note that projects pay all fees was wrong; expedite fees are waived for 100% affordable projects (standard fees and deposits still apply). Prevailing wage changed from false to unclear because the waiver is a 1720(b)(4) form of public funds whose weight depends on project size (de minimis test) and other 1720(c) exemptions.

program_name: City of San Diego CDBG entitlement NOFA (FY2028 RFQ and RFP cycle) and HOME entitlement administered through SDHC
administering_agency: City of San Diego Economic Development Department, Community Development Division, 1200 Third Ave., Suite 1400, MS 56D, San Diego 92101; CDBG@sandiego.gov, (619) 236-6700; HOME administered by SDHC
typical_award_size: FY2027 CDBG competitive categories: public services about $1.29M, community and economic development about $2.72M, nonprofit facility improvement $2.0M (March 2026 funding decision memos). Capital funds for affordable housing acquisition are deployed through Bridge to Home rounds (Round 5 used $18.38M CDBG for two acquisitions). City HOME: in FY2026, 113 of 709 affordable rental units built were HOME funded; HOME is combined with Affordable Housing Fund money in the SDHC NOFA.
per_unit_cap: HOME per-unit subsidy limits apply to HOME units; CDBG category caps set annually.
affordability_requirement: CDBG national objective (low and moderate income benefit); HOME units at or below 60 percent AMI rents for 15 to 20 years or longer under the SDHC NOFA (55 years).
next_deadline: FY2028 CDBG RFQ released October 5, 2026, RFQ responses due November 6, 2026 (5 pm), RFP to qualified organizations December 7, 2026, mandatory workshop December 8, proposals due January 15, 2027 (5 pm), CPAB scores March 5, 2027, Council action April to June 2027 with the FY2028 Annual Action Plan.
layering_notes: Developers rarely apply to the CDBG public services round; the relevant path is Bridge to Home (CDBG acquisition) and the SDHC NOFA (HOME). Federal cross-cutting rules (Davis-Bacon, NEPA, Section 3) attach. The County's Urban County CDBG and HOME Consortium (county records) do not cover the City of San Diego, which is its own entitlement and participating jurisdiction. FY2026 CAPER and FY2027 Annual Action Plan are posted on the CDBG page.
audit_note: Nov 9, 2026 spot check: FY26 CAPER says the 709 units with 113 HOME-assisted units are under construction, not built in FY2026. Bridge to Home has used $53.1M CDBG through FY2026 across seven rounds. The FY2028 RFQ closed November 6, 2026, so only organizations qualified through it can submit the January 15, 2027 RFP.
prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: State Prohousing Designation, City of San Diego (2022 designation and 2025 renewal application)
administering_agency: City of San Diego City Planning Department, Prohousing@sandiego.gov
typical_award_size: Not a direct subsidy. Prohousing status gives bonus points or set-asides in state AHSC, IIG, MHP and PLHA competitive rounds and eligibility for Prohousing Incentive Program grants. The City was designated in November 2022 and the designation was valid until January 2026; the City circulated a draft renewal application in November 2025 (public review now closed). HCD's Prohousing Application Tracker lists the City's renewal application as received June 12, 2026 with status Pending Revisions, and HCD's designated jurisdictions list as of August 10, 2026 shows San Diego County and Chula Vista but not the City of San Diego.
affordability_requirement: Not applicable.
next_deadline: No deadline; renewal application pending at HCD (status Pending Revisions as of November 8, 2026). Check the HCD designated jurisdictions list before claiming Prohousing points in a 2027 state application.
layering_notes: Matters for layering state funds onto SDHC and Bridge to Home awards: without the designation, City projects lose Prohousing points in AHSC and MHP scoring that Chula Vista and unincorporated County projects receive. Read the City Planning Prohousing page and HCD's designated list this pass; the renewal decision itself could not be confirmed.
cycle_notes: Renewal application received by HCD June 12, 2026; status Pending Revisions on the HCD tracker. Designation lapsed January 2026 pending renewal.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds; the Prohousing Designation is a state recognition that awards scoring points and pays no money for construction, so it does not trigger prevailing wage. State funds won with the points carry their own rules. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Chula Vista Housing Authority housing successor loans (Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund) and Local Housing Trust Fund gap financing; 2025-2026 affordable housing NOFA
administering_agency: City of Chula Vista Housing and Homeless Services Department (Housing Manager Brian Warwick) acting for the Chula Vista Housing Authority as Housing Successor to the former Redevelopment Agency
typical_award_size: Residual receipts style gap loans of $3M to $4M per project. June 16, 2026: Housing Authority Resolution 2026-006 and Council Resolution 2026-130 approved up to $4,000,000 (recommended as $3,000,000 Low-Mod plus $975,000 Local Housing Trust Fund) to Wakeland Housing for the 68-unit Park Hill UMC project at 545 East Naples Street, conditioned on reducing density to 62 units; Bayview Family Apartments was the alternate. June 10, 2025: up to $4.0M Low-Mod loan to Community HousingWorks for 201 Third Avenue (HA Resolution 2025-004); March 2025: $3.0M Low-Mod for the Palomar Motel permanent supportive housing conversion with Homekey+. The 2024-2025 NOFA offered about $4,000,000 for new multifamily construction (applications due January 15, 2026). Local Housing Trust Fund seeded in 2024 with a $500,000 City match (Resolution 2024-102) and a $500,000 HCD LHTF matching grant (Resolution 2024-163, awarded January 2026). FY 2026-27 Low-Mod administration and homeless prevention appropriation $800,000.
per_unit_cap: None published; awards have run about $44,000 to $59,000 per unit.
affordability_requirement: 55 year covenants; LMIHAF rules (Health and Safety Code 34176.1: 80 percent AMI maximum, 30 percent of funds to 30 percent AMI units); LHTF units for lower income households.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026; no new Housing Authority or LHTF NOFA has been posted since the 2025-2026 round, and the Housing and Homelessness Advisory Commission next meets January 27, 2027. Contact the Housing and Homeless Services Department for the next round.
layering_notes: Chula Vista's only city gap source beyond fee waivers. Stacks with Chula Vista Housing Authority conduit bonds (separate record), County HCDS NOFA 2026-03 (Chula Vista projects are eligible for County IHTF and HOME Consortium funds because the City is in the Urban County for HOME), HACSD project-based vouchers and 4 percent LIHTC. Housing Element (2021) noted the Balanced Communities in-lieu fund held only about $1.1M in 2020 and was inadequate for gap financing; the new Housing Inclusionary Fund (CVMC 19.91.070) will add in-lieu fees. Palomar Motel used Homekey+. chulavistaca.gov blocks automated access (403); agendas, minutes and item summaries were read on the City's eSCRIBE agenda portal, but staff report PDFs (filestream.ashx) return 403, so loan terms come from the agenda item text.
cycle_notes: NOFA issued as Low-Mod and LHTF funds accumulate; the 2025-2026 round ($4M) closed January 15, 2026 and funds were committed to Park Hill UMC in June 2026.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The Chula Vista NOFA and staff reports could not be read (chulavistaca.gov and the eSCRIBE attachments return 403), and the eSCRIBE agenda text for the Park Hill loan states no wage term. Construction paid solely with low and moderate income housing fund money plus private funds is excluded under 1720(c)(4). Local loans are public funds under 1720(b), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20 or more years at 80% AMI or below, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports a value.

program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, CVMC Chapter 19.91 (Ordinance 3572, 2024; threshold amended to 20 units by Ordinance 3581, November 2024) and Housing In-Lieu Fee / Housing Inclusionary Fund
administering_agency: City of Chula Vista Housing and Homeless Services Department and Development Services Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Residential and mixed-use projects of 20 or more units (applications deemed complete on or after July 1, 2024) must restrict 10 percent of units, split as evenly as possible between moderate income and low income households, for rental or for-sale product; density bonus units are excluded from the base. In-lieu fee for fractional units or in place of on-site units set by Council resolution on a square footage basis with different rates for for-sale and rental product (Master Fee Schedule Chapter 16, Resolution 2024-100, May 21, 2024, based on the RSG Inclusionary Policy and In-Lieu Fee Study); paid before the first building permit into the Housing Inclusionary Fund. Alternatives: off-site units within one mile or in TCAC high or moderate resource areas, land dedication, conversion of market rate units, preservation of at-risk units, transferable credits (10 year life), and incentive credits (for example 3.5 rental units of credit per very low income unit provided in place of a moderate unit). Replaced the 1981 Balanced Communities Policy (10 percent of 50 or more units).
affordability_requirement: 55 years rental (45 years ownership); moderate income (up to 120 percent AMI) and low income (up to 80 percent AMI) units; Chapter 19.94 marketing and lottery rules give preference to displaced Chula Vista residents and local residents and workers.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; the Council on May 21, 2024 voted 5-0 to set the threshold at 20 units (first reading) and adopted the Chapter 19.91 threshold amendment on November 12, 2024. Code is current through Ordinance 3617 (February 2026). Check the Master Fee Schedule Chapter 16 for the current per square foot in-lieu rate.
layering_notes: Projects of 20 to 24 units routinely pay fees, so the Housing Inclusionary Fund will grow slowly; Otay Ranch village developers (for example Village 8 East, Affordable Housing Agreement approved November 4, 2025) satisfy the requirement with dedicated affordable sites that then seek City Low-Mod loans and bonds (separate records). Inclusionary units may count toward the state density bonus (19.91.060). Ordinance text read on the zoneomics code mirror (chulavista.municipal.codes returns 403); Council actions read on the eSCRIBE agenda portal.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and for-sale projects of 20 or more units (compliance)
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: CVMC 19.91.050 confirms 20 unit threshold, 10 percent split moderate and low, 55 year rental and 45 year ownership terms, in-lieu fee by Council resolution paid before first building permit, and alternatives including 3.5 unit rental incentive credit (Ord. 3572 and 3581). Prevailing wage false is uncited; the chapter imposes a land use requirement with no public funds, so no wage rule is stated.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Parkland Acquisition and Development fee exemption for affordable units (Ordinance 3573 amending CVMC 17.10, 2024) and project fee waivers and deferrals for affordable housing
administering_agency: City of Chula Vista Development Services Department and Housing and Homeless Services Department; waivers by City Council resolution
typical_award_size: Ordinance 3573 (second reading May 28, 2024) exempts affordable units from Parkland Acquisition and Development (PAD) fees. Council also waives parkland dedication and in-lieu requirements case by case: Resolution 2026-087 (May 19, 2026) for the 96-unit Sol Vista (Enclave Montecito) affordable rental project in Otay Ranch Village 2 and Resolution 2024-060 (April 9, 2024) for the 100 percent affordable Chula Vista Seniors project at 178 Third Avenue. The Housing Element (Program 4.5) describes Council waivers or deferrals of development impact fees for projects with affordable units and a development fee deferral program for infill rental housing west of I-805. PAD fees in Chula Vista run tens of thousands of dollars per unit, so the exemption is a material subsidy.
affordability_requirement: Deed restricted affordable units; 100 percent affordable projects have received full parkland waivers.
next_deadline: Exemption applies at permit; discretionary waivers go to Council with the project's financing approvals. Confirm the current CVMC 17.10 text and whether other DIFs (transportation, public facilities) can be deferred for a specific project.
layering_notes: Fee relief is the second city layer after Low-Mod and LHTF loans (separate record). Waived City fees may be public funds under Labor Code 1720, so projects usually assume prevailing wage once they also take City or bond financing. County HCDS impact fee waivers (county records) do not apply inside the city. Read on the City's eSCRIBE agenda portal (May 19, 2026 and May 2024 agendas); chulavistaca.gov is blocked to scripts.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only general rule found: Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees waived or reduced by a political subdivision as payment out of public funds, but the outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts (the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test of under $600,000 and under 2 percent of project cost may exempt small waivers; the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption covers below-market loans, not fee waivers). No City ordinance, resolution or DIR determination on point was found. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: basis is only Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and depends on waiver size and other public funds in the deal.

program_name: Chula Vista Housing Authority tax-exempt multifamily housing revenue bonds (conduit issuer; 2024 bond policies)
administering_agency: Chula Vista Housing Authority (City Council acting as Authority), staffed by the Housing and Homeless Services Department
typical_award_size: Conduit private activity bonds sized to project debt. Enclave Montecito / Sol Vista (96 units, Otay Ranch Village 2): inducement up to $25 million (HA Resolution 2025-006, August 5, 2025), TEFRA hearing and bond issuance approval April 21, 2026 with an issuance amount not to exceed $14,000,000. Resolution 2024-103 (May 21, 2024) updated the Authority's conduit bond policies so the City is the issuer in most instances rather than JPAs; Master Fee Schedule Chapter 19 sets Housing Authority application, issuance and monitoring fees. Not every Chula Vista deal uses the Authority: Otay Ranch II (270 units, Rock Mountain Road and SR 125) received a $31,220,000 bond allocation on December 10, 2025 with the California Municipal Finance Authority as issuer, and the City's May 19, 2026 TEFRA approval for that project was for the CMFA issuance.
affordability_requirement: Federal 20 percent at 50 percent AMI or 40 percent at 60 percent AMI minimum; City regulatory agreements typically mirror the inclusionary and Low-Mod covenants (55 years).
next_deadline: Rolling; inducement needed before CDLAC application rounds. Contact the Housing and Homeless Services Department for the bond policy and fee schedule.
layering_notes: The 2024 policy makes the Housing Authority the default issuer, which keeps issuer fees local, but JPA issuance (CMFA for Otay Ranch II) still occurs; when a JPA issues, the City acts only as TEFRA host. Pairs with 4 percent LIHTC, City Low-Mod and LHTF loans and parkland fee waivers (separate records). Read on the City's eSCRIBE agenda portal; bond policy PDF not downloadable (403). Otay Ranch II issuer confirmed in the CTCAC/CDLAC staff report CA-25-798.
prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village and PW 2006-005 Central Village Apartments, holds that loans of tax-exempt conduit bond proceeds for affordable housing, whether publicly offered or privately placed, are not a payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4), because the proceeds and repayments never enter public coffers; reaffirmed in PW 2010-008 and PW 2015-008. Bond financing alone does not trigger state prevailing wage; other public funds in the same deal (city or county loans, fee waivers, land) are tested separately, and federal sources such as HOME or 9+ PBVs carry their own Davis-Bacon rules. https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf
audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: removed Otay Ranch II as an Authority bond example. CTCAC staff report CA-25-798 (Dec 10, 2025) names the California Municipal Finance Authority as CDLAC applicant and bond issuer.

program_name: Affordable Housing Incentives / Density Bonus, CVMC Chapter 19.90 (Ordinance 3572, 2024)

next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; pre-application conference encouraged. Density bonus units are exempt from the inclusionary requirement and are not counted in its base.
layering_notes: Inclusionary units can count toward both the inclusionary and density bonus requirements (19.91.060). Otay Ranch village SPA plans carry their own affordable housing plans. Chula Vista is on HCD's Prohousing list (as of August 10, 2026) and received a Prohousing Incentive Program grant (Resolution 2025-179, November 4, 2025), which adds points for state applications on Chula Vista sites. Ordinance text read on the zoneomics code mirror.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: official code host chulavista.municipal.codes (including the enactment PDF path for Ord. 3572) and codepublishing.com return 403; no eSCRIBE agenda item for Ordinance 3572 was found. Search results show gocodebook and zoneomics mirrors cite Ord. 3572 sec. 2 (2024) in Chapter 19.90, consistent with the record, but mirrors alone do not support verified.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

program_name: Chula Vista CDBG and HOME entitlement, PLHA Cycle 2 allocation and Prohousing Incentive Program grant
administering_agency: City of Chula Vista Housing and Homeless Services Department (HUD grants), Carlos Rodriguez, Management Analyst (PLHA)
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 HUD allocations appropriated June 16, 2026 (Resolution 2026-118): $2,501,482.59 CDBG and $1,200,730.78 HOME, plus ESG; Annual Action Plan adopted May 19, 2026 (Resolution 2026-089). PLHA: Council on October 6, 2026 adopted the PLHA CY2024-2028 302(c)(4) Plan and accepted Cycle 2 funds (Resolutions 2026-211 and 2026-212), directing them to Chula Vista Village at Otay shelter operations, as it did with earlier PLHA (Resolution 2025-084, June 2025). program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, Oceanside City Code Chapter 14C (Ordinance 24-OR0004-1, 2024) and Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fee
administering_agency: City of Oceanside Housing and Neighborhood Services Department (Housing Division) and Development Services Department (Planning)
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Ordinance 24-OR0004-1 (introduced January 24, 2024, adopted February 14, 2024, effective outside the Coastal Zone) raised the set-aside from 10 to 15 percent, added unit mix, dispersal and equal amenity rules for reserved units, and clarified ADU use. The Coastal Commission approved the amendment on February 5, 2026 (LCP-6-OCN-25-0030-2) with seven suggested modifications. The City Council introduced an ordinance adopting the modifications on June 3, 2026 (5-0) and adopted it June 17, 2026; it applies citywide. Current rules: applies to residential projects of 7 or more units (including mixed-use, condo conversions and time extensions); at least 15 percent of units reserved (for-sale units for lower and moderate income, rental units for lower income); acutely low income category added; affordability for at least 55 years for rental and for-sale; ADUs may satisfy the requirement in any residential project; affordable housing agreement recorded before building permit, final map or Coastal Development Permit. In-lieu fee per reserved unit is set by Council resolution, deferrable on impact fee terms, and deposited in the affordable housing trust account. Rental projects have been covered since the September 9, 2020 Phase 1 amendment.
affordability_requirement: 15 percent of base units (density bonus units excluded): for-sale units for lower and moderate income households, rental units for lower income households; minimum 55 year restrictions for rental and for-sale units.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm the current in-lieu fee rate with the Housing Division.

Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: Oceanside Density Bonus Ordinance (Zoning Ordinance, Housing Element Program 2) and development impact fee deferral for affordable units
administering_agency: City of Oceanside Development Services Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Housing Element Program 2 commits the City to amend its density bonus ordinance (Zoning Ordinance Article 30) to conform to AB 1763, SB 1227 and AB 2345. State law allows up to a 100 percent bonus for projects reserving at least 15 percent of base units for very low income, 24 percent for lower income or 44 percent for moderate income households. Coastal zone: the certified Article 30 density bonus provisions do not apply to the Downtown District. The Coastal Commission approved the Downtown density amendment (LCP-6-OCN-25-0029-2, 86 units per acre base density, 5,500 unit figure treated as a target) with modifications on February 5, 2026, including a requirement that the City submit updated density bonus regulations covering the Downtown District by January 1, 2029; the Council adopted the modifications (introduced June 3, 2026, ordinance adopted June 17, 2026). Inclusionary in-lieu fee deferral on the same terms as impact fee deferral is available.
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 tiers; 55 year rental affordability.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm the current Zoning Ordinance Article 30 text with Planning; updated density bonus regulations for the Downtown District are due to the Coastal Commission by January 1, 2029.
layering_notes: No local enhancements beyond state law were found; the practical local tools are the inclusionary in-lieu fund and the Affordable Housing Strategy NOFA (separate records). Smart and Sustainable Corridors Plan (Program 9) adds capacity along transit corridors. Read in the 2021-2029 Housing Element (HCD-hosted) and the Coastal Commission February 2026 staff report.
audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Housing Element Program 2 and Coastal Commission Th16a report reread; June 3, 2026 Council staff report (Legistar 26-1386) confirms Commission approval February 5, 2026, and the Article 12 ordinance with modifications was adopted June 17, 2026 (26-1553). Downtown status updated.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The density bonus itself (Gov. Code 65915) pays no public funds, but this record also covers development impact fee deferral for affordable units (Housing Element: fee deferrals for ELI and special needs projects, in-lieu fee deferral on the same terms as impact fees). Waived, reduced or deferred fees are public funds under 1720(b)(4) (fees or loans charged at less than fair market value), but 1720(c)(3) de minimis and other 1720(c) exemptions decide coverage. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Oceanside Housing Revenue Bonds (Multi-Family), Housing Element Program 1

audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Housing Element Program 1 text matches (City last issued private activity bonds in 2016 for Villa Storia, 38 units, with a CDLAC award; will issue bonds with other financing as needed).

Stacks with City HOME (separate record), County HCDS NOFA 2026-03 (Escondido projects are eligible for County IHTF), HACSD project-based vouchers and state density bonus. The Escondido Housing and Neighborhood Services page (Successor Housing Agency, Resolution 2012-16) states no wage term. program_name: Density Bonus and Residential Incentives Ordinance (Escondido Zoning Code Article 67, Sections 33-1410 to 33-1421) and Development Fee Deferral Policy
administering_agency: City of Escondido Development Services Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Article 67 grants state law density bonuses (up to 50 percent; 80 percent or unlimited for 100 percent affordable projects) and incentives and concessions to projects of five or more units (three or more in some areas), including student housing and child care provisions, in-lieu incentives of equivalent land value, land donation bonuses and a sliding scale (one percent bonus per one percent increase above the 10 percent very low income minimum); amended in 2020, 2021 and 2022 for AB 2345. Agreement processing and administrative fee apply (33-1421). The 2012 Development Fee Deferral Policy lets residential projects of five or more units defer development fees to occupancy (up to one year from permit). Density transfer programs exist in the Downtown and East Valley Specific Plan areas (Resolution 2019-69; Ordinance 2023-10).
affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 tiers; affordability tenure per 33-1418 (55 years rental).
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; density bonus request form on escondido.gov. A zoning ordinance update with lot consolidation incentives was planned for 2025; confirm current Article 67 text with Planning.
layering_notes: State conforming with no local fee waiver: a 2024 staff report noted neither state law nor the Municipal Code requires the City to give direct financial assistance to density bonus projects. The fee deferral is the only fee relief. Escondido is not on HCD's Prohousing list (as of August 10, 2026). Pair with City HOME and recycled RDA funds (separate records) and County HCDS NOFA. Article text read on the zoneomics code mirror; Housing Element and APR read on escondido.gov.
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: changed false to unclear because fee deferral and City financial in-lieu incentives can be public funds under 1720(b); density bonus alone would be false. Code read on zoneomics mirror.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. Article 67 grants regulatory density bonus incentives, but it also allows an in-lieu incentive of equivalent financial value offered by the City, and the record includes the Development Fee Deferral Policy (fees deferred to occupancy, up to one year). Waived, reduced or deferred fees are public funds under 1720(b)(4) (fees or loans charged at less than fair market value), but 1720(c)(3) de minimis and other 1720(c) exemptions decide coverage. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

Program 2.3 commits the City to identify properties for acquisition; no Escondido acquisition was confirmed this pass.
affordability_requirement: Low, median and moderate income households (up to 120 percent AMI); rent caps at 35 percent of AMI tier; terms per CalCHA regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; CalCHA transactions depend on bond market conditions and City host approval of each acquisition.

The welfare exemption for nonprofit LIHTC owners (county record) remains the tax tool for deed restricted projects. Read in the draft 2021-2029 Housing Element on escondido.gov; program status not confirmed.
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: changed false to unclear; no DIR determination or program rule on point was found for CalCHA middle-income acquisitions.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. CalCHA, a public JPA, acquires existing apartment communities with its own governmental purpose bonds (Housing Element Program 2.3). Acquisition of a completed building is not construction under 1720(a)(1), but repair or rehabilitation work the JPA contracts for on property it owns can be a public work, and no CalCHA or City wage rule was found. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Carlsbad Housing Trust Fund gap loans (Inclusionary Housing in-lieu fees, housing credit purchases and housing impact fees; CMC 21.85.110 and 21.85.120)
administering_agency: City of Carlsbad Housing and Homeless Services Department (Mandy Mills, Director); recommendations by the Housing Commission, approvals by City Council
typical_award_size: Residual receipts gap loans typically $500,000 to $4.25M per project. June 9, 2026: Council Resolutions 2026-107 and 2026-108 authorized sale of the City-owned 945 Chestnut Avenue (Chestnut Apartments) to The Chestnut Apartments, LP (Kingdom Development) through a carryback loan at appraised value plus a Housing Trust Fund loan not to exceed $850,000 for rehabilitation gap financing (Housing Commission Resolution 2026-004, May 14, 2026). Earlier: $4.25M residual receipts loan to Affirmed Housing (Windsor Pointe, about $8.3M total City assistance) and a 2025 $500,000 recommendation for West Oaks. Fund balance about $12.4M at October 30, 2020 (Housing Element); the FY 2025-26 Housing Trust Fund Annual Report was accepted by the Housing Commission October 8, 2026 (Resolution 2026-006). Fund sources: in-lieu fees ($4,515 per market rate unit as of 2020, fee study pending), sale of affordable housing credits, housing impact fees, loan interest and fund interest. The fund has helped produce about 2,300 affordable homes and leverages City money up to five times.
per_unit_cap: None published; sized by pro forma review.
affordability_requirement: 55 year affordability for lower income households (up to 80 percent AMI per the CMC 21.85.020 definition). Inclusionary rental units may not rent above 90 percent of the actual rent of a comparable market unit in the same development (CMC 21.85.090); this is not a cap at 90 percent of the lower income rent limit. Trust fund dollars may not be used to satisfy a project's own inclusionary requirement, only to exceed it.
next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026; there is no NOFA or deadline. Requests are taken on a rolling basis through Housing and Homeless Services staff, reviewed by the Housing Commission (meets second Thursday) and approved by City Council.
layering_notes: Carlsbad's trust fund is the best capitalized city fund in North County relative to deal flow, but Council has been selective (Chestnut, Windsor Pointe, West Oaks). Stacks with County HCDS NOFA 2026-03 IHTF and HOME Consortium funds (Carlsbad is in the County HOME Consortium and received County HOME for Vista Las Flores), HACSD or Carlsbad Housing Agency project-based vouchers, CMFA or CSCDA bonds and LIHTC. The CDBG-funded Housing Reserve Fund (separate record) can add acquisition money. carlsbadca.gov and its govaccess document host return 403 or time out; agendas were read on the City's Laserfiche WebLink (records.carlsbadca.gov) and the Housing Element on hcd.ca.gov. The annual report figures should be pulled from the October 2026 Housing Commission packet.
cycle_notes: Rolling, project-by-project requests; no NOFA.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The Carlsbad City Council record cited for the fund contains no prevailing wage term, and CMC 21.85 defines City financial assistance without a wage condition. Local loans are public funds under 1720(b), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20 or more years at 80% AMI or below, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: June 9, 2026 Council minutes confirm Resolutions 2026-107 and 2026-108 (carryback sale of 945 Chestnut Avenue and a Housing Trust Fund loan up to $850,000). Old affordability text said rents no more than 90 percent of the lower income limit rent; CMC 21.85.090 instead caps inclusionary rents at 90 percent of the actual rent for a comparable market unit in the same development. program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, Carlsbad Municipal Code Chapter 21.85 (Ordinance NS-535 as amended through CS-474, 2024), in-lieu fees and inclusionary housing credits
administering_agency: City of Carlsbad Housing and Homeless Services Department and Community Development Department (Planning)
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Residential developments of seven or more units must build and restrict at least 15 percent of total approved units (including density bonus units) for lower income households; off-site combined projects are allowed with Council approval and the percentage is computed on total units (market units divided by 0.85). Projects of fewer than seven units pay an in-lieu fee per market rate unit equal to 15 percent of the subsidy needed to make a typical new attached unit affordable to a lower income household ($4,515 as of 2020; schedule set by Council resolution; fee study authorized). Alternatives: off-site units, land dedication, contribution to special needs housing, purchase of surplus affordable housing credits from Villa Loma and other combined projects, and inclusionary credit schedules for units serving lower tiers. Offsets (21.85.100): the City may grant density increases, standards modifications, fee waivers and subsidies at its discretion. Rental inclusionary units required since 2017 (CS-324) after the 2010 Palmer suspension. The ordinance has produced 1,708 affordable units.
affordability_requirement: Lower income households (up to 80 percent AMI); rental units restricted 55 years and no inclusionary unit may rent above 90 percent of the actual rent charged for a comparable market unit in the same development (CMC 21.85.090); inclusionary units must match the tenure of the market units; for-sale units resale restricted.
next_deadline: Applies at entitlement through an Affordable Housing Agreement (21.85.140) before final map or building permit; in-lieu fee per Council resolution schedule, assessed on market rate units at building permit.
layering_notes: Fees and credit sales fund the Housing Trust Fund (separate record). Density bonus units count in the 15 percent base, which makes Carlsbad's requirement stricter than the state density bonus tiers; the inclusionary units themselves qualify the project for state density bonus incentives (CMC 21.86, separate record). Master and specific plans must carry inclusionary provisions (21.85.035). Code read on the zoneomics mirror; Housing Element Program 2.1 on hcd.ca.gov.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and for-sale projects of 7 or more units (compliance)
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; the inclusionary ordinance (CMC 21.85) imposes an affordability obligation and pays no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any City offsets or financial assistance granted under 21.85 (defined to include fee subsidies and direct financial aid) would be public funds tested separately. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: Old: rents no more than 90 percent of the lower income limit; new: rents no more than 90 percent of the actual rent of a comparable market unit in the same development (CMC 21.85.090). The 15 percent requirement for seven or more units, the in-lieu fee formula for fewer than seven units, and the 55 year term match. In-lieu and housing impact fees for five or more units are paid before building permit or may be deferred to final inspection (21.85.195). Code read on the zoneomics mirror because carlsbadca.gov and codepublishing.com return 403.

Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

program_name: Inclusionary Housing Requirements (Municipal Code Chapter 17.138, Ord. 1719, 2022) and Commercial Linkage Fee (Chapter 4.60)
administering_agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department, Housing Programs
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Rental projects: 6% of units affordable (3% very low, 3% low). For-sale projects: 10% of units (5% low, 5% moderate). In-lieu fee calculated on new habitable square footage at a rate set by Council resolution in the comprehensive fee schedule; the City's inclusionary page (not opened this pass, slocity.org blocks automated access) reports about $26.73 per sq ft for-sale and $21.42 per sq ft rental, with commercial linkage fees of about $6.42 per sq ft (office, service, hotel, retail) and $5.35 per sq ft (industrial, institutional). All in-lieu and linkage fees go to the City Affordable Housing Fund. By 2020 the program had produced more than 850 affordable units and $10.45 million in in-lieu funds committed to 464 units.
affordability_requirement: Inclusionary units deed restricted 55 years rental, 45 years ownership, at City Affordable Housing Standards. Fractional units may be met by paying a fractional in-lieu fee. Exempt: ADUs and JADUs, 100% affordable projects, projects using a density bonus, downtown flexible density units (Chapter 17.141), additions and remodels that add no units.
next_deadline: Not applicable; requirement applies at entitlement and in-lieu fee is paid before building permit issuance (phased projects pay proportionally).
layering_notes: Core local requirement for any market-rate multifamily deal in the City of SLO. 100% affordable projects and density bonus projects are exempt, so an LIHTC deal normally pays nothing and instead competes for the in-lieu revenue through the Affordable Housing Fund (separate record). Ordinance replaced the 1999 program in 2022 after a nexus study; the City notes Chapter 17.138 and Chapter 4.60 (nonresidential linkage fee) apply to mixed-use projects on both the residential and commercial components. County inclusionary ordinance (Title 22 Section 22.12.080) was repealed in 2022 and the County's Title 29 fund is now residual, so the City fund is the only growing in-lieu pool in the county. slocity.org returns 403 to automated access; the ordinance text was read on the zoneomics code mirror and the program history in the HCD-hosted 2020-2028 Housing Element. Confirm current fee rates on the City's inclusionary page before underwriting.
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. This program is a requirement imposed on private development and provides no public funds, so it does not itself trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing on the project.

program_name: City Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) grants and loans (in-lieu fee fund; award criteria Resolution 9263, 2001 Series; Housing Element Program 2.5)
administering_agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department, Housing Programs (Council awards)
typical_award_size: Gap grants and below-market loans at Council discretion under adopted criteria (Resolution 9263, 2001 Series). Housing Element history: $10,450,954 of in-lieu funds granted, loaned or committed to 464 deed-restricted units since the 1999 inclusionary ordinance; Bishop Street Studios (34 units) received $1,595,500 combined AHF loan, impact fee deferral loan and CDBG loan; $330,000 grant to TMHA for a 6-unit acquisition-rehab. Not confirmed on an agency source in the audit: a $2 million January 2020 approval for a 108-unit project; a 2023 Council resolution approving $3.2 million to HASLO for 736 Orcutt Road ($2.0 million) and 279 Bridge Street ($1.2 million); and $750,000 of 2024 Prohousing Incentive funds routed through the AHF. Housing Element target: support at least 4 new affordable developments during the planning period.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low, very low, low and moderate income; deed restrictions of 55 years rental and 45 years ownership under City Affordable Housing Standards. Housing Element Program 2.5 directs the fund to projects that would not be feasible without AHF support and to production efficiency.
next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency. No formal NOFA; developers request awards through the Housing Programs Coordinator (housing@slocity.org) and awards go to Council by resolution, usually timed to TCAC or CDLAC rounds.
layering_notes: Largest city-controlled housing fund in the county. Revenue is the Chapter 17.138 in-lieu fee and Chapter 4.60 commercial linkage fee plus shared-equity recapture; the City also receives its own CDBG share through the Urban County (county record: Urban County Action Plan NOFA, due October 30, 2026 for the 2027 program year) and has layered CDBG loans with AHF awards. Typical stack for a City of SLO LIHTC deal: AHF grant or loan, City impact fee deferral loan (separate record), County Title 29 or Regional Housing Fund, HASLO project-based vouchers, SLO County Housing Trust Fund predevelopment loan, then state sources. HCD-hosted Housing Element was the only agency document that could be opened; slocity.org (403) and the City eScribe agenda host pub-slocity.escribemeetings.com (filestream 403, JS-only listings) could not be read, so current fund balance and 2025-2026 awards are unconfirmed.
audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: no program rule found stating prevailing wage applies; changed true to unclear because only the general 1720(b) public-funds definition supports a value.
prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The City Housing Element (Program 2.5 and AHF description) states no wage term for Affordable Housing Fund awards. Local loans are public funds under 1720(b), but 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts privately owned residential projects whose only public participation is below-market loans with at least 40% of units restricted for 20 or more years at 80% AMI or below, and 1720(c)(3) exempts de minimis subsidy. AHF grants are public funds under 1720(b)(1). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

program_name: Affordable Housing Incentives and local density bonus (Municipal Code Chapter 17.140; Ord. 1705, 2021)
administering_agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department (Director approval; review authority resolution for alternative incentives)
typical_award_size: Requirement-based entitlement, not a subsidy. Density bonus of 20% to 50% per Tables 8-3 and 8-4 (10% low income earns 20%, rising to 50% at 24% low income; 5% very low earns 20%); the Director may approve a bonus above 50% at the developer's request. One to three incentives or concessions on the state schedule, and alternative incentives listed in Section 17.140.070 include deferral of application and development review processing fees, deferral of park land in-lieu fees or dedication, mixed-use zoning, reduced site standards and parking. Housing Element Program 2.14 commits the City to support bonuses above the 35% state base; the City approved more than 15 density bonus requests in 2018-2020.
affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% senior, 10% transitional foster youth, disabled veterans or homeless); affordable units covenanted per state law through an affordable housing agreement (Section 17.140.080). Applies to projects of five or more units including mixed-use.
next_deadline: Not applicable; requested with the planning application.
layering_notes: Local enhancement beyond state law: Director can approve bonuses above 50% and fee deferrals count as incentives. Projects using a density bonus are exempt from Chapter 17.138 inclusionary requirements. Base densities in the City's high-density zones are 24 or more units per acre before bonus, and the Downtown Flexible Density Program (Chapter 17.141) allows small units (150 to 600 sq ft) outside the inclusionary ordinance. Stack with AHF awards and the City impact fee deferral; the County's Regional Housing Incentive Program (Title 22 Section 22.12.010) applies only to unincorporated land. Read on the zoneomics mirror because slocity.org blocks automated access.
audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: Section 17.140.040 confirms 5+ unit applicability, Tables 8-3 and 8-4 (10% low = 20% to 24% low = 50%; 5% VLI = 20%), Director may approve bonus above 50%; 17.140.070 lists fee deferrals; 17.138.020(A)(4) exempts density bonus projects from inclusionary. prevailing_wage_trigger false is uncited (entitlement only, no public funds).
prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. program_name: Development services fee waiver and citywide development impact fee deferral loans for affordable units (Housing Element incentives table; Chapter 4.56 impact fee deferral)
administering_agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department and Finance Department

Waived, reduced or deferred fees are public funds under 1720(b)(4) (fees or loans charged at less than fair market value), but 1720(c)(3) de minimis and other 1720(c) exemptions decide coverage. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
